2608.16949.title: Critical couplings of two dimensional Ising model on various lattices
2608.16949.summary:
- Unified fermionic‑field (Kac–Ward) formulation expresses the 2D Ising partition function as a determinant of a finite momentum‑space matrix for multiple planar lattices.
- Exact critical couplings for square, honeycomb, triangular, kagomé, and dual kagomé lattices are reproduced; the anisotropic kagomé critical surface and low‑energy spectrum are fully determined.
- In the isotropic dice model the low‑energy spectrum is relativistic massive, with the mass vanishing at cosh(2J_c) = (1+√/

2608.16980.title: Hydrodynamization in 1D Bose gases at nonzero temperature
2608.16980.summary:
- Hydrodynamization of a 1D hard‑core Bose gas after a Bragg‑pulse quench is examined at finite temperature.
- The hydrodynamic coherence time is temperature‑independent, while higher temperatures reduce the damping and prethermalization times.
- The shortening is linked to a broadened rapidity distribution, leading to a defined nonzero‑temperature dephasing time.

2608.17009.title: PowderLine: a programmatic powder diffraction analysis application
2608.17009.summary:
- PowderLine is a Python tool that packages entire Rietveld or single‑peak refinements into a declarative, schema‑validated recipe.
- The recipe is machine‑readable/writable, enabling users, scripts, and autonomous agents to run refinements consistently.
- It supports high‑throughput, interactive, and autonomous powder‑diffraction workflows by returning structured, machine‑readable results.

2608.17040.title: Local magnetic resonance of scalar spin chirality
2608.17040.summary:
- Finite scalar spin chirality produces an orbital magnetic moment that has not been directly measured.
- Local spin‑resonance drives break cyclic symmetry, activating chirality‑changing transitions that expose the orbital moment.
- Lindblad simulations show detectable signatures in STM‑ESR, silicon donor spins, and quantum‑dot spin qubits.

2608.17061.title: Emissivity by Design: Geometric Mesh Inductance Governs Thermal Radiation in Metallic Nanowire Networks
2608.17061.summary:
- Emissivity is set by the geometric inductance of inter‑wire gaps, not by wire length or percolation.
- A parameter‑free reactance \(X_L = Z_0(g/\lambda)\ln(2g/\pi D)\) captures diameter dependence, sheet‑resistance trends, and angular behavior.
- The model fits 56 silver‑nanowire samples (MAE , unifies data on a universal curve, and predicts emissivity–transmittance for independent studies.

2608.17076.title: Hidden Ergodic Relaxation in the Quench Dynamics of a Bichromatic Mott Lattice
2608.17076.summary:
- Sudden quench of secondary lattice in a bichromatic Mott lattice drives coefficient and second‑Renyi entropies toward GOE predictions, while local observables (momentum, fragmentation, Glauber correlations) stay nearly static.
- Entropy dynamics collapse onto a universal relaxation trajectory largely independent of quench strength, revealing hidden ergodic relaxation beneath persistent Mott‑like order.
- An effective embedded random‑matrix model captures the crossover from restricted to extensive Hilbert‑space spreading, providing a framework for the observed dynamics.

2608.17080.title: Controlling Structure and Properties of Vapor-Deposited Glasses of Organic Semiconductors: Recent Advances and Challenges
2608.17080.summary:
- Vapor‑deposited organic semiconductor glasses can be tuned via substrate temperature to vary density and molecular orientation.
- Optimized glass structures enhance OLED external quantum efficiency and device lifetime.
- Molecular simulations now reproduce experimental structures, enabling in‑silico design and guiding future research.

2608.17086.title: Rejuvenation versus overaging: The effect of cyclic loading/unloading on the segmental dynamics of PMMA glasses
2608.17086.summary:
- 5000‑cycle tensile tests (003–007 strain, Tg – 10 K to Tg – 25 K) on PMMA show no overaging; segmental dynamics are unchanged or faster.
- Probe reorientation reveals relaxation‑time changes that recover on a time scale ≈ aging time, preserving the sample’s original age memory.
- Mechanical properties change little, highlighting probe reorientation’s higher sensitivity to nonlinear deformation effects.

2608.17089.title: Over what length scale does an inorganic substrate perturb the structure of a glassy organic semiconductor?
2608.17089.summary:
- ~8 nm near Si or Au substrates shows disordered packing in vapor‑deposited DSA‑Ph glasses.
- Grazing‑incidence X‑ray scattering across 10–600 nm films confirms substrate‑induced disorder is confined to a few nanometers.
- Coarse‑grained MD reproduces this length scale; deposition temperature controls structure beyond the interfacial layer.

2608.17125.title: Demonstration of a scalable all-solid-state refrigerator exploiting diffusion geometries and limiting interfacial conductances at temperatures below 1
2608.17125.summary:
- 1121 SINIS junctions form a scalable all‑solid‑state refrigerator that cools phonons below 1 K.
- Diffusive quasiparticle flow and engineered superconductor‑trap interfaces suppress back‑heat leakage.
- Device uses W/TiW cold side, Al₂O₃ insulator, Al superconductor, Au trap; achieves sub‑Kelvin phonon temperatures on a 9 mm² silicon chip.

2608.17303.title: Second Harmonic Generation Spectroscopy of the Surface Charge Density Wave in the Weyl Semimetal CoSi
2608.17303.summary:
- RA‑SHG detects a surface CDW on CoSi(with T_c ≈ 90 K.
- SHG intensity follows a power law, β = 30 ± 03 (3D XY universality).
- Transition is purely surface‑driven; scaling linked to Fermi‑arc–bulk coupling.

2608.17424.title: Many-Anyon Braiding in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect with Hybrid Monte Carlo Simulation
2608.17424.summary:
- Hybrid Monte Carlo yields many‑anyon braiding matrices for Moore‑Read quasiholes.
- Global‑rotation braiding schemes are robust against finite‑size effects, outperforming two‑anyon exchanges.
- Electron interactions and local traps shift fusion‑channel energies but leave non‑Abelian braiding matrices unchanged, evidencing long‑range entanglement.

2608.17548.title: Absence of nontrivial local conserved quantities in a class of $U(1)$-symmetric spin-1 chains
2608.17548.summary:
- No nontrivial k‑local conserved quantities exist for 3 ≤ k ≤ N/2 in U(-symmetric spin‑1 chains with vanishing quadrupolar couplings.
- In frustration‑free chains with U(symmetry breaking, any local conserved operator up to half the system is a linear combination of 1, S^z, and H.
- The same absence of k‑local conserved quantities holds for the periodic Motzkin chain, linking symmetry breaking to frustration‑free structure.

2608.17558.title: Inducing metal-insulator transition via disorder in correlated kagome systems
2608.17558.summary:
- Hopping disorder combined with electron correlations localizes carriers, reducing the critical Coulomb interaction for a Mott transition in kagome lattices.
- Disorder suppresses but does not fully destroy antiferromagnetic order, producing a phase diagram with antiferromagnetic metal, correlated Anderson insulator, and disordered Mott insulator.
- Determinant QMC calculations of kinetic energy, dc conductivity, and DOS confirm a disorder‑driven metal‑insulator transition, offering guidance for experimental control of kagome device states.

2608.17631.title: Gauge-constrained Spinon Complexes Near Deconfined Quantum Criticality
2608.17631.summary:
- Pinned‑spin defects create controllable spinon–antispinon pairs, showing string breaking when dipoles reorganize into shorter neutral dipoles.
- QMC visualizes VBS domain‑wall strings, whose connectivity is set by lattice‑scale VBS phase offsets, spin projection, and vorticity.
- Multi‑pin patterns form robust four‑spinon complexes and extended domain‑wall networks that preserve global connectivity under local distortions.

2608.09644.title: A spin-bond theory unifying non-relativistic spin splitting and emergent spin-orbit textures
2608.09644.summary:
- Unified spin‑bond theory connects even‑parity altermagnets and odd‑parity p‑wave magnets through unitary spin phases and Hermitian spin amplitudes.
- Non‑commuting unitary and Hermitian sectors generate mixed, non‑coplanar spin textures with even‑in‑momentum transverse polarization, observable via ARPES.
- Synthetic spin‑orbit coupling can be dynamically tuned by controlling bond non‑commutation, enabling field‑free spin qubits.

2608.17647.title: Wavelength-Resolved Control of Photovoltaic Screening and Defect-Mediated Doping in Photo-Ferroelectric/Graphene Devices
2608.17647.summary:
- Demonstrates wavelength‑dependent control of ferroelectric/graphene electrostatics using 365 nm (above‑bandgap) vs 530 nm light.
- 365 nm generates free carriers that screen the ferroelectric dipole, dropping graphene resistance contrast from 290 % to 15 %.
- 530 nm excites defect states, only weakly suppressing contrast, enabling selective optical tuning of polarization and doping.

2608.17745.title: Bridging ambient- and high-pressure superconductivity in La$_2$LnNi$_2$O$_7$ films
2608.17745.summary:
- Ambient‑pressure La₂LnNi₂O₇ films: T² resistivity, Tc ≈ 41–42 K; 16 GPa raises Tc to 67–73 K.
- Tc tracks normal‑state transport: T² → T‑linear evolution under pressure.
- Ln‑substitution lattice compression mimics pressure but lowers Tc, underscoring lattice‑superconductivity interplay.

2608.17777.title: Entropy mapping under uniaxial pressure utilizing the elastocaloric effect
2608.17777.summary:
- Developed a.c. elastocaloric method combining low‑frequency strong‑coupling and high‑frequency quasi‑adiabatic data to recover absolute entropy and specific heat under uniaxial pressure.
- Mapped Sr₂RuO₄’s entropy across its phase diagram, showing maximal entropy quenching at the critical strain (Van Hove singularity).
- Determined the specific‑heat jump Δc/(γT) at the Van Hove strain is smaller than earlier indirect estimates.

2608.18065.title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Preconditioning for Stable Training of Recurrent Neural Quantum States
2608.18065.summary:
- Stabilizes minSR for RNN-based NQS using simple regularization, enabling robust training with few samples.
- Outperforms Adam on 1D transverse‑field Ising and cluster states; competitive on 2D Heisenberg and \(J_1\!-\!J_2\) models.
- Opens the door to curvature‑based optimizers for autoregressive NQS in quantum simulation.

2608.18168.title: Embedding Paired Free-Fermion Gaussian States into Gutzwiller-Projected Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer Wave Functions
2608.18168.summary:
- Embeds any even‑parity spinless fermionic Gaussian state into a Gutzwiller‑projected BCS state of spinful Abrikosov fermions.
- Demonstrated exactly for the 1D transverse‑field Ising model.
- Supplies controlled initial states for variational Monte‑Carlo studies of non‑integrable systems.

2608.18189.title: Breaking the mutual exclusivity between metallicity and ferroelectricity in a non-polar covalent semiconductor via orbital selective doping
2608.18189.summary:
- Heavy N‑doping of cubic SiC induces metallicity and a polar R3m phase via a pseudo‑Jahn‑Teller transition, breaking the metallicity–ferroelectricity rule.
- Directional antibonding orbitals prevent screening, enabling 180° polarization reversal under 1 V bias with ~50 ns switching speed.
- Ferroelectric tunnel junctions exhibit HRS/LRS memory, >85 000‑cycle endurance, and projected 100‑year retention, offering low‑power, high‑speed non‑volatile memory.

2608.18199.title: Chern insulator boundary criticality
2608.18199.summary:
- Critical Hall conductivity σ_xy = ½ e²/h at the C=1 transition, described by a massless Dirac fermion with a parity anomaly.
- Chiral edge mode delocalizes into the bulk at criticality, yet boundary fermion correlators retain chiral structure and bulk scaling dimension, matching the anomaly.
- Generalizes to higher Chern numbers and 3+1 d TI transitions, identifying parity‑odd terms in current and stress‑tensor correlators via residual conformal symmetry.

2608.18248.title: Learning constructive models of emergent systems
2608.18248.summary:
- Introduces Layer‑Restricted Boltzmann Machine (LRBM) that constrains information flow across entropic scales to construct emergent systems.
- Demonstrates hierarchical encoding: low layers capture global structure, higher layers encode fine‑grained features across images, language, and enzyme sequences.
- Validated by designing 1,130 chorismate mutase variants; functional enzymes achieved up to 53% sequence divergence, showing fold emerges at intermediate layers but function requires all layers.

2608.18267.title: Finite-temperature Green's function cluster expansion from thermofield doubles: Breakdown of the polaron picture
2608.18267.summary:
- Finite‑temperature Green’s‑function cluster expansion (FTGFCE) combines a generalized cluster expansion with the thermofield‑double formalism to compute single‑particle Green’s functions of polarons at finite temperature.
- The method delivers momentum‑resolved spectral functions, dispersions, lifetimes, and effective masses for the Holstein polaron up to \(T/\Omega \sim 1\), agreeing quantitatively with finite‑temperature DMRG.
- FTGFCE is numerically exact in principle, avoids time evolution, and is implemented in an open‑source software package.

2608.18277.title: On the electronic and vibrational dimensionality of nanometer-scale silicon structures
2608.18277.summary:
- Uses electron/phonon coherence length (inelastic mean free path) as the key scale for dimensionality.
- Estimates electron quantum confinement in Si nanosheets at room T below ~8 nm.
- Phonon confinement is wavelength‑dependent: short‑wavelength modes ~10 nm, long‑wavelength acoustic modes ~1 µm.

2608.18278.title: Writing and erasing skyrmions by single ultrafast laser pulses in monolayer Janus 2D magnets
2608.18278.summary:
- Field‑free, nonvolatile Nèel skyrmions in monolayer Janus Cr chalcogenides imaged by PEEM and NV magnetometry.
- Janus‑induced inversion symmetry breaking enhances Dzyaloshinskii‑Moriya interaction, stabilizing tunable skyrmions.
- Reversible skyrmion writing/erasing achieved with a single ultrafast laser pulse at 300 Oe.

2608.18301.title: Rare-earth spin textures and a route to electronic inhomogeneity in $Pr_2Ir_2O_7$
2608.18301.summary:
- Monte‑Carlo spin‑ice Pr configurations coupled via Kondo exchange to an Ir Hartree‑Fock model reproduce surface Kondo‑inhomogeneity in Pr₂Ir₂O₇.
- The all‑in‑all‑out charge gap closes smoothly with J_K, and jellyfish monopole textures lower the insulating gap by ΔJ_Kc ≈ 03 t.
- Synthetic tunneling maps reveal island‑like Fermi‑level DOS variations that, through Doniach exponential sensitivity, tip the balance between Kondo screening and magnetic order, explaining the observed coexistence.

2608.18337.title: Engineering kekule superconductivity from layer-selective interactions in rhombohedral graphene
2608.18337.summary:
- Finite‑momentum Kekulé superconductivity arises in rhombohedral multilayer graphene from layer‑dependent opposite‑sign interactions, preserving time‑reversal and inversion symmetry.
- The state appears only above a critical carrier density when a Kane‑Mele mass is present, with opposite‑chirality condensates in the two valleys.
- Phase diagram, Tc versus chirality index \(J\) and mass \(\lambda\), and the BKT transition temperature are mapped, demonstrating orbital‑dependent interactions favor finite‑momentum pairing.

2608.18370.title: Interface-Controlled Spin-Orbit Torques in Rare-Earth Synthetic Ferrimagnets Probed by Sagnac Magneto-Optics and Harmonic Hall Measurements
2608.18370.summary:
- Sagnac interferometry and harmonic Hall analysis jointly quantify damping‑like SOT in Co/Gd synthetic ferrimagnets.
- Torque magnitude is strongly tuned by Gd thickness and interface order, with Gd contributing even when Pt spin Hall effects cancel.
- Interface engineering yields perpendicular anisotropy in Gd/Pt/Co/Al, enabling SOT switching at 8–10 MA cm⁻².

2608.18527.title: Topology is not silent in the transport noise of multiband bosons
2608.18527.summary:
- Topological Berry curvature cancels in electron Hall‑current noise at a Fermi surface, but not for thermally populated bosonic bands.
- Boson noise contains an occupation‑weighted dispersion of Chern numbers, a new term absent at zero temperature.
- Derived from a fluctuating Boltzmann equation; measurable only via an equilibrium sum‑rule protocol, not in driven experiments.

2608.18529.title: Universal thermal breakdown of polaron coherence in one, two, and three dimensions
2608.18529.summary:
- Polaron coherence universally breaks down at \(T \approx 5\,\Omega\), independent of dimensionality or coupling strength.
- Effective mass \(m^*\) and inverse lifetime \(1/\tau\) rise monotonically with temperature until the quasiparticle peak dissolves into an incoherent continuum.
- A finite‑temperature Momentum‑Average approximation produces a self‑energy that matches exact 1D benchmarks (VED‑FTLM, DMRG) across all coupling regimes.

2608.18530.title: High-field fate of the Kitaev quantum spin liquid in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$
2608.18530.summary:
- High‑field specific heat up to 24 T shows a crossover at μ₀H*≈15 T where the Kitaev description breaks down.
- Above H*, the six‑fold angular modulation collapses, the excitation gap deviates from the H³ scaling and decreases with field.
- In‑plane magnetization anisotropy persists to ~24 T, indicating KQSL signatures survive up to ~90 % of saturation.

2608.18540.title: Hubb_DMFT and Wan2mb_DMFT: Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo Solvers for Single- and Multi-Orbital Hubbard Model
2608.18540.summary:
- Introduces Hubb_DMFT and Wan2mb_DMFT, DMFT solvers for single‑band and multi‑orbital Hubbard models.
- Built on iQIST v.7 with CT‑HYB core, providing exact self‑energy and vertex calculations for density‑density interactions.
- Wan2mb_DMFT directly couples Wannier tight‑binding Hamiltonians to many‑body solvers for realistic material studies.

2608.18706.title: Transitions and Critical Divergences in Periodically Hopping Modulated Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chains
2608.18706.summary:
- CRG analysis of SSH chains shows curvature‑function divergence at Δ=0 (two‑site) and at |Δ/t|=√2 (four‑site) marking topological transitions.
- Δ=0 exhibits faster divergence and larger correlation‑length exponent than the Dirac‑like |Δ/t|=√2 point, placing them in distinct universality classes.
- Edge modes decay slowly into the bulk near Δ=0 but quickly near |Δ/t|=√2; the study extends similarly to eight‑site periodic modulations.

2608.19028.title: Sign-problem-resilient singular-value probe in determinant quantum Monte Carlo
2608.19028.summary:
- Uses adjacent gap ratio of low‑lying singular values of the fermion matrix to detect interaction‑driven transitions in determinant QMC.
- Accurately tracks the Dirac‑semimetal to antiferromagnetic Mott transition in the sign‑free honeycomb Hubbard model.
- Remains robust in the sign‑affected Haldane‑Hubbard model, surviving phase reweighting and locating the transition near earlier estimates.

2608.19178.title: Chiral bosonic mean-field Ansatz and spin dynamics in spin-1 Kitaev magnets
2608.19178.summary:
- Introduces a triplet‑pairing φ_t = π/2 mean‑field Ansatz for the S = 1 Kitaev model, extended to weak symmetric Γ, Γ′ exchanges.
- Calculates the dynamical spin structure factor; the π/2‑flux Ansatz yields a flatter spectrum and stronger suppression of long‑range correlations than the 0‑flux Ansatz, matching short‑range Kitaev physics.
- Demonstrates that spectral flatness is tied to short‑range spin correlations and explores the effect of weak Γ, Γ′ perturbations near the pure Kitaev limit.

2608.19274.title: Exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size
2608.19274.summary:
- Exact two‑spin correlation formulas for the boundary row of a finite rectangular Ising lattice with mixed periodic/free edges.
- Demonstrated emergence of long‑range order as temperature decreases; thermodynamic‑limit expressions depend on the order of taking \(L\) and \(N\) limits.
- Confirmed that the thermodynamic‑limit results match previously known expressions, illustrating size effects with diagrammatic examples.

2608.19280.title: Multi-Tool Robotics Enables In-Situ Sample Manipulation for Time-Resolved Synchrotron Measurements
2608.19280.summary:
- Modular multi‑tool robot performs real‑time sample handling inside a synchrotron hutch.
- Enables in‑situ manipulation of perovskite thin films during continuous high‑flux X‑ray data acquisition.
- Establishes a platform for automated, autonomous synchrotron experiments beyond human‑access limits.

2608.19284.title: Extension of the Shockley-Queisser Limit for Nanostructured Solar Cells
2608.19284.summary:
- Extends Shockley‑Queisser limit to nanostructured cells using quantum phase‑space formalism, linking geometry to thermodynamics via a momentum‑variance matrix.
- Derives an analytical maximum‑efficiency expression; predicts >48 % for 3–5 nm PbS nanostructures, far exceeding bulk 8 % and classical limits.
- Numerical simulations show two efficiency peaks for constant‑volume shapes and recover classical values for large sizes.

2608.19312.title: Interferometric Signatures of Zero Modes in Fractional Quantum Hall-Superconductor Heterostructures
2608.19312.summary:
- Parafermion zero modes in FQH–SC heterostructures cause stochastic switching in the fractional Josephson spectrum of a junction with a QPC.
- A two‑QPC Fabry‑Pérot interferometer shows fusion‑channel‑dependent interference; weak tunneling preserves the signal, strong tunneling suppresses it to zero.
- The vanishing interference in the strong‑tunneling limit reveals the non‑Abelian nature of the defects, even when the parent FQH state is Abelian.

2608.19320.title: Quantum R\'enyi-Jarzynski Equality
2608.19320.summary:
- Non‑destructive quantum Jarzynski equality conditioned on bath observables → R\'enyi‑Jarzynski equality linking bath drift to R\'enyi \(k\)-divergence.
- Serves as a tunable cost function for quantum optimal control, reducing bath drift in state preparation and gate design.
- Toy model shows R\'enyi order \(k\) tunes sensitivity to bath distribution; minimizing drift across energy levels requires system‑bath entanglement.

2608.19341.title: Cumulative X-ray Damage in Bismuth Selenide Examined by Simultaneous TXM and XRD
2608.19341.summary:
- 27,000 PAL‑XFEL pulses cause rapid vaporization holes in <100 pulses, then slow grain refinement and sputtering over thousands of pulses.
- Williamson‑Hall analysis shows a transition from single‑crystal to nanocrystalline Bi₂Se₃, with grain size shrinking from micron to nanometer scale.
- Finite‑element modeling and SEM reveal 47 µm X‑ray penetration heats material >1600 K, producing sputter streaks, prismatic crystals, and disordered microcrystals, with grain‑boundary feedback accelerating damage.

2608.19343.title: Self-calibrating thermal interferometry of vortex parity in a two-dimensional chiral superconductor
2608.19343.summary:
- A reconfigurable domain wall in a 2D chiral superconductor serves as a ballistic thermal channel (counting Majorana modes) and a Fabry–Pérot resonator (detecting vortex parity via half‑level shifts).
- Exact transmission, heat full‑counting statistics, and a theorem show that linear‑response heat scattering reveals vortex parity but not fusion channels of distant cores.
- With rhombohedral‑graphene parameters, sub‑mic

2608.19352.title: Hysteresis without coexistence: disorder-rounded first-order transitions in a van der Waals magnet
2608.19352.summary:
- Disorder rounds the first‑order transition, eliminating macroscopic phase coexistence while preserving hysteresis.
- Br substitution introduces a new phonon branch that softens and gains spectral weight with increasing concentration.
- Findings confirm Imry‑Wortis/Aizenman‑Wehr predictions of domain fragmentation in low‑dimensional systems.

2608.19362.title: Channel-selective magnetic filtering in a nodal-line semimetal
2608.19362.summary:
- Magnetic barrier selectively blocks inner toroidal Fermi contour before outer one, acting as channel‑selective filter.
- Closed‑form, channel‑resolved transmission derived via two‑band Hamiltonian and wave‑function matching.
- Two‑terminal conductance drops in steps as barrier strength increases, revealing toroidal Fermi surface fingerprints.

2608.19365.title: Layered matter that maintains spacing but loses stacking order
2608.19365.summary:
- Swollen stiff, charged nanosheets keep a sharp, salinity‑tunable spacing while stacking order collapses to only 2–3 layers.
- A weak osmotic restoring slope (< 1 Pa nm⁻¹) holds the spacing, causing slow fault relaxation and a quenched, ageing‑like metastable registry.
- The effect is intrinsic (not defect‑driven) and should generalise to other stiff nanosheets such as clays, oxides, and graphene oxide.

2608.19465.title: Antiferromagnetic order and lattice response in DyCuAs$_2$

2608.19604.title: Universality of long-wavelength behavior of composite-fermion Fermi liquid
2608.19604.summary:
- CF diagonalization refines the wave function yet still gives \(\bar{S}(\mathbf{q})\sim q^3\), not \(q^3\ln q\).
- The small‑\(q\) scaling of \(\bar{S}(\mathbf{q})\) is independent of the electron‑interaction potential.
- Findings support a universal \(q^3\) long‑wavelength behavior for the composite‑fermion Fermi liquid.

2608.19856.title: Tilted $p$-wave magnet candidate CeNiAsO
2608.19856.summary:
- CeNiAsO exhibits commensurate AFM order with a tiny out‑of‑plane moment (~05 µB).
- The spin axis is tilted from the c‑axis, forming a “tilted p‑wave” magnetic configuration.
- This tilt boosts non‑relativistic spin splitting, revealing a new paradigm for correlated p‑wave magnets.

2608.19864.title: Volatile resistive-switched state in a bulk organic conductor with a sharp metal-insulator transition
2608.19864.summary:
- Volatile resistive switching observed in bulk (d7‑DMe‑DCNQI)₂Cu with a sharp first‑order metal‑insulator transition and minimal heat dissipation.
- Temperature locks to the MIT and an inverse Ohm’s law (V ∝ 1/I) appear, highlighting strong Joule‑heating effects.
- Results elucidate nonlinear thermal contributions to resistive switching, informing efficient device development.

2608.20057.title: Pressure-tuning of electronic structure of CeTe3 probed by femtosecond collective mode spectroscopy
2608.20057.summary:
- CDW transition drops from ~570 K to ~300 K at ~6 GPa, disappearing above 7 GPa.
- Pressure strengthens electron‑phonon coupling and weakens Fermi‑surface nesting, driving CDW suppression.
- Below 7 GPa, low‑T relaxation slows, signaling heavy‑electron behavior from Ce 4f–itinerant hybridization.

2608.20221.title: Universal meson spectra near $(1+1)$-dimensional Ising criticality
2608.20221.summary:
- Magnetic perturbation near 1+1D Ising criticality confines excitations into mesons whose masses scale universally after rescaling microscopic couplings.
- The count of stable mesons is set by the lightest two‑meson threshold, while the lightest‑meson mass follows a single‑parameter trajectory confirmed by Hamiltonian truncation in Ising field theory and mixed‑field Ising chains.
- Tensor‑network studies of four‑periodic spin‑½ Heisenberg‑Ising chains (

2608.20269.title: Nonlinear Drude weight of the one-dimensional Hubbard model
2608.20269.summary:
- NLDWs in the 1D Hubbard model at quarter filling are obtained from Bethe‑ansatz and strong‑coupling expansion, matching numerics.
- Tomonaga‑Luttinger theory predicts divergent NLDWs above a threshold from Umklapp, yet exact results remain finite, revealing a mismatch.
- At half filling, finite‑size scaling across the Mott transition yields insulating‑phase asymptotics and a verified hyperscaling ansatz near criticality.

2608.21316.title: Ultralow-Field Triplon Condensation in a Spin-Ladder Magnet
2608.21316.summary:
- First ultralow‑field triplon BEC observed in a spin‑ladder, with μ₀H_c1 = 17 T in Henmilite.
- Thermodynamic, μSR, and neutron data show a quantum‑disordered coupled‑ladder ground state, refuting earlier zero‑field AF order.
- An asymmetric ordered dome (H_c2 ≈ 2 T) is reproduced by QMC, placing Henmilite just on the gapped side of the ladder‑ordering

2608.21291.title: Neural quantum states in condensed matter: advances, best practices, and prospects
2608.21291.summary:
- Neural quantum states combine neural-network parametrizations with Monte Carlo sampling to flexibly represent many‑body wave functions.
- Recent work applies them to frustrated magnets, lattice fermions, and non‑equilibrium dynamics, emphasizing symmetry constraints, optimization, and sampling strategies.
- Key challenges remain: learning sign/phase structures, reducing variational bias, scaling optimization, and stabilizing real‑time evolution.

2608.21284.title: Two distinct gap structures in the mid-infrared optical conductivity of the Hubbard model
2608.21284.summary:
- Two distinct gaps—pseudogap (AF spin fluctuations) and Mott‑Hubbard—drive universal MIR conductivity.
- Each gap yields a characteristic MIR spectral shape and distinct doping dependence, enabling experimental separation.
- Doping evolution: low‑doping Mott peak in visible; high‑doping broad MIR response from waterfall‑induced correlations, matching experiments.

2608.21250.title: Emergent Vibronic Spectral Hierarchy in a Kagome Flat-Band Insulator
2608.21250.summary:
- Raman spectra reveal a giant Franck‑Condon progression from a nearly dispersionless 7 cm⁻¹ phonon, with a 6 cm⁻¹ comb‑like fine structure.
- The comb spacing is field‑independent, yet its spectral weight is strongly tunable by magnetic field, indicating a coupled electron‑vibrational manifold.
- The 260–280 K transition is an electronic localization without conventional structural or magnetic order, implicating dispersionless phonons in vibronic self‑trapping and the insulating phase.

2608.21161.title: Berry-Curvature Effect in Anomalous Transport
2608.21161.summary:
- Derives Berry‑phase contribution to anomalous transport via quasiclassical matrix kinetic equation in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals.
- Extends beyond anomalous Hall effect to include anomalous heat flow and thermoelectric currents driven by temperature or chemical‑potential gradients.
- Provides an alternative formulation to Di Xiao et al., emphasizing the role of a field‑dependent density of states.

2608.21110.title: Pair size versus coherence length and quantum geometry in the spin-orbit coupled BCS-BEC crossover
2608.21110.summary:
- Exact pair‑size tensor in helicity basis separates into intraband and quantum‑geometric interband parts set by the quantum metric.
- Two many‑body lengths: Cooper‑pair size (mean‑field) and coherence length (Gaussian fluctuations); they coincide in BCS but diverge across the crossover.
- In 3D Rashba/Weyl and 2D Rashba SOC, pair size monotonically decreases with SOC, while coherence length exhibits a pronounced minimum at the crossover, with quantum‑geometric terms contributing up to ~1/3 of the pair size.

2608.21029.title: Doping-driven Mott transition from steady-state density functional theory
2608.21029.summary:
- Applies steady‑state i‑DFT to the Hubbard model’s doping‑driven Mott transition.
- Links the i‑DFT exchange‑correlation bias to quasiparticle weight using Fermi‑liquid theory, guiding functional construction.
- Numerical results confirm i‑DFT captures the Mott transition.

2608.20981.title: A Classification of Translation-Invariant Quantum Codes in Any Dimension
2608.20981.summary:
- Classifies D‑dimensional translation‑invariant quantum codes using length‑D chain complexes.
- Proves such codes are equivalent to multiple copies of the D‑dimensional toric code.
- Applies to multivariate multicycle codes where the number of variables equals the number of cycles.

2608.20978.title: Quasi-one-dimensional topological band structure and van Hove singularities in monolayer TaIrTe$_4$ from laser $μ$-ARPES
2608.20978.summary:
- μ‑ARPES reveals a highly anisotropic, quasi‑1D band structure in monolayer TaIrTe₄.
- A saddle‑point van Hove singularity exists, yet it lies at a carrier density where transport shows no anomalies.
- Quasiparticle linewidths indicate weak correlations, suggesting van Hove singularities and electron interactions play a secondary role in the quantum spin Hall phase.

2608.20849.title: Spin models with critical ground space degeneracy from Lie algebra relations
2608.20849.summary:
- SO(-symmetric spin chain built from an MPS of so(generators, encoding the algebra’s quadratic relations.
- Ground‑state degeneracy: OBC → quadratic (one irrep per odd dimension); PBC → linear (singlet + maximal‑spin ferromagnet), yielding gapless modes.
- Construction extends to SO(d) and other compact simple Lie groups, illustrating that small parent Hamiltonians of injective MPS can exhibit critical, non‑unique ground spaces.

2608.20403.title: Criticality in Neural Network Function Space through Wilsonian Fixed Points and Finite-Width Corrections
2608.20403.summary:
- Infinite-width nets ↔ free-field fixed point; finite width adds non‑Gaussian interactions via Wilsonian RG.
- Criticality occurs when higher‑order correlations become relevant/marginal, making the function distribution scale‑sensitive.
- Width, depth, activation, init variance, and training dynamics serve as control parameters; overparameterization suppresses interactions, exposing finite‑width critical structure.

2608.20404.title: Robust Discovery of Coarse-Grained Continuum Equations from Microscopic Dynamics
2608.20404.summary:
- PDE‑SINDy recovers phase‑separation PDEs; more data suppresses spurious terms, improving accuracy.
- Expanding the function library hampers efficiency; a stringent threshold yields a correct Model‑A‑like equation.
- Selection probabilities expose a hierarchy of equations, enabling accurate dynamics for the Glauber Ising model.

2608.20409.title: Centipede-Like Metastrip Enables On-Demand Programmable Droplet Motion
2608.20409.summary:
- Elastic metastrip with centipede‑like cantilevers couples in‑plane and out‑of‑plane motion, creating a frequency‑dependent phase map that directs droplet motion.
- Tuning resonator tip masses opens reconfigurable out‑of‑plane bandgaps, locally suppressing droplet movement for spatial selectivity.
- Multi‑frequency excitation selectively actuates droplets at their resonances, filtering them by volume and position.

2608.20410.title: Graphon Spin Systems as Exactly Solvable Models
2608.20410.summary:
- Formulates Ising model on graphons, deriving mean‑field limit and exact critical temperatures from Hilbert‑Schmidt eigenvalues.
- Computes critical points for Erdős–Rényi, small‑world, and power‑law graphs; small‑world shows ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and multistable phases.
- Combines analytical solvability with broad network applicability, confirmed by Monte‑Carlo simulations.

2608.20417.title: Modelling the onset and evolution of immiscible viscous fingering in porous media
2608.20417.summary:
- Demonstrated that matching experimental finger widths requires the most unstable wavelength at onset to be several times smaller than the final finger width, accounting for shielding and merging.
- Showed that small‑scale channelling is necessary to eliminate the stable trailing region seen in homogeneous‑media simulations.
- Included a weak oil‑wet capillary pressure function to reproduce the bypassed oil observed in the experiment.

2608.20419.title: One-dimensional Polar Spinor Droplets
2608.20419.summary:
- Derived a channel‑resolved Lee‑Huang‑Yang correction and extended Gross–Pitaevskii model for 1D polar spin‑1 quantum droplets.
- Stationary solutions cross over from soliton‑like to flat‑top droplets, with saturated chemical potential and peak density; both types are stable.
- Quench and collision dynamics reveal a finite‑size crossover that modulates breathing modes and phase‑dependent scattering, underscoring distinct density and spin fluctuation roles.

2608.20422.title: Revisiting the hydromechanical formulation of a micromechanics-based phase-field model for poro-elastoplastic media
2608.20422.summary:
- Discontinuities in strength surface arise from non‑associative plastic flow and missing fluid‑pressure coupling in the Helmholtz free energy.
- Introducing an associative Drucker–Prager flow rule and the omitted coupling term restores a continuous strength surface and accurate fracture driving force.
- The revised model matches analytical benchmarks and reproduces shear‑dominated fractures in hydraulic fracturing and biaxial compression simulations.

2608.20426.title: Conservation capacity of local learning rules in physical networks
2608.20426.summary:
- Local learning rules in resistive networks conserve a “mass‑like” function tied to each circuit sector, determined by Tellegen’s identity and Kirchhoff’s laws.
- The number of independent conserved masses equals a topological property bounded by the number of output electrodes, yielding a capacity theory for memory protection.
- In linear circuits, these conserved identities are exactly classified, with adjoint coupled learning draining sectors at rates set by squared output multipliers.

2608.20434.title: An LLM agent for end-to-end computational materials discovery
2608.20434.summary:
- MAESTRO automates the entire MOF discovery pipeline using an LLM agent, from literature mining to database curation.
- It links publications to crystal structures and screens candidates with progressively higher‑cost calculations.
- The system discovers high‑performance MOFs for wet flue‑gas separation from unrelated studies, surpassing conventional screening.

2608.20449.title: The friction-era VOS amplitude of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ string network from nematic disclination data

2608.20604.title: Note on proliferation transitions of non-Abelian anyons
2608.20604.summary:
- Framework for (2+d topological phase transitions driven by proliferation of anyons in a braided fusion subcategory, coupling TQFT to dynamical matter.
- SymTFT description localizes dynamics on the symmetry boundary of a (3+d slab, with explicit Chern‑Simons‑Higgs models realizing the transitions.
- Application to non‑invertible one‑form symmetry gauging (e.g., Rep(G) and SU(\_{10}→Spin(\_, identifying which anyons proliferate.

2608.20694.title: Distinguishing Mott and strain-induced anisotropic semimetals in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene using Landau level spectroscopy
2608.20694.summary:
- Distinguishes Mott semimetal from strain‑induced anisotropic semimetal in magic‑angle TBG using Landau level spectroscopy.
- Strain‑induced state shows a robust gap hierarchy Δ±4 > Δ±8 > Δ±12; Mott state has Δ±4 largest but Δ±8/±12 depend on magnetic field.
- Out‑of‑plane magnetic field provides a sharp probe, with findings consistent across strain orientations, lattice relaxation, and finite‑B incompressibility data.

2608.20838.title: Electronic Toroidal Metals: Landau Theory and Magnetoelectric Fingerprints
2608.20838.summary:
- Introduces electronic toroidal metal (ETM) as a Fermi‑liquid instability with toroidal order emerging from itinerant electrons, using a projected criterion that removes uniform charge‑current contributions.
- Defines the toroidal moment through the antisymmetric magnetoelectric tensor, linking it to pseudospin‑vortex topology and showing that changes in vortex winding markedly enhance the response.
- Predicts distinctive nonlinear charge transport in ETM, including a pronounced interband quantum‑geometric contribution.

2608.20760.title: Quantum Wake Dynamics from Distinct Spectroscopic Perturbations
2608.20760.summary:
- RIXS selection rules filter fractionalized excitations, revealing distinct quantum wakes in a spin‑½ Heisenberg chain.
- Spin correlators propagate at the spinon light cone \(v_s=\pi J/2\), while bond correlators form a slower dominant wake \(v\approx92J\).
- The resulting momentum‑frequency responses are experimentally accessible, link to quantum Fisher information, and serve as benchmarks for quantum simulations.

2608.21451.title: Power Series for the Quantum Statistical Mechanics Probability with Results for the Second Virial Coefficient of Helium
2608.21451.summary:
- Power‑series expansion of the Wigner‑Kirkwood pair commutation function derived by recursion.
- Second virial coefficient for helium matches experimental values for T > 65 K.
- Outlines prospects for a general quantum Monte Carlo algorithm.

2608.21490.title: Electrostatic lens of a charged vortex
2608.21490.summary:
- Derived the near‑axis electrostatic potential of a charged vortex with radially varying density and compressibility.
- Expressed the constant, quadratic, and quartic coefficients in terms of local screening and vortex‑density gradients, including a thermodynamic term from compressibility.
- Applied to a 3D unitary Fermi gas, separating equation‑of‑state contributions from ordinary screening and charge‑source terms, linking vortex‑core thermodynamics to the electrostatic profile.

2608.21492.title: Dynamical Signatures and Kibble-Zurek Scaling of Localization in Tilted Bose-Einstein Condensates
2608.21492.summary:
- Tilt strength controls localization–delocalization crossover in a 1D BEC; repulsive interactions promote delocalization.
- Sudden quenches show localized condensates with high survival probability, revivals, and narrow spectra, while delocalized ones exhibit weak recurrences, irregular dynamics, and broad spectra.
- Finite‑rate ramps across the threshold reveal Kibble‑Zurek scaling of the localization length and Bogoliubov gap, yielding critical exponents.

2608.21493.title: All-Optical Control of Interfacial Polarization in MoS$_2$/WSe$_2$ Heterobilayers
2608.21493.summary:
- Predicts persistent out‑of‑plane polarization in MoS₂/WSe₂ heterobilayers driven by intense ultrafast pulses.
- Intermediate field strengths quadruple interlayer charge transfer, marking a transition from perturbative to strong‑field dynamics in the high‑harmonic spectrum.
- Lattice strain can tune the resonance condition while preserving the induced permanent dipole, enabling femtosecond all‑optical control of polar phases.

2608.21514.title: Theory of the Spinon-Mediated Witness Spin Glass in Herbertsmithite
2608.21514.summary:
- Spinon‑mediated coupling of Cu²⁺ impurities forms a 260 mK spin glass, reproducing noise, susceptibility, and neutron data.
- A single‑parameter model fits both Z₂ and

2608.21525.title: Machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals for molecules, solids, and reactive surfaces
2608.21525.summary:
- CIDER26SS: a machine‑learned, non‑local exchange‑correlation functional regularized for wide transferability.
- Outperforms conventional functionals, correctly predicting CO/Pt(binding site, adsorption energy, Pt lattice constant, and surface energy without Pt training data.
- Size‑extensive, efficient, and accurate even for systems far outside the training domain, enabling reliable heterogeneous catalysis simulations.

2608.21528.title: High Speed Contact-Resonance Tracking using Brownian motion
2608.21528.summary:
- Introduces iDART, an interferometric dual‑AC resonance tracker that uses Brownian motion for drive‑free contact‑resonance AFM imaging.
- Positions the interferometer at the cantilever displacement maximum to suppress detector noise below thermal levels, enabling pixel‑resolved imaging at conventional scan rates.
- Shows that low‑frequency and resonant electrical/photothermal excitation boosts contrast without shifting the contact resonance, providing practical high‑speed nanomechanical mapping.

2608.21540.title: Automated Analysis to Reveal Grain Boundary Phase Microstructures
2608.21540.summary:
- Automated tool maps planar GB microstructures, identifying distinct interfacial phases and their separating dislocation lines.
- Quantifies phase‑specific excess properties and estimates Burgers content at phase junctions.
- Demonstrated on diffusion‑limited GB phase transformations, indistinguishable vacancy/interstitial phases, and phase‑nucleus microstructures.

2608.21542.title: Noise-Robust Spin-Orbit Qubit in Germanium Holes via p-Orbital Encoding
2608.21542.summary:
- Introduces a spin‑p‑orbital (SpO) qubit encoded in the p‑shell of a three‑hole Ge/SiGe quantum dot, with charge‑noise sweet spots tuned by confinement and magnetic field.
- Demonstrates SpO qubit relaxation comparable to single‑hole spin qubits and enables all‑electrical Landau‑Zener state transfer without microwaves.
- Enables fast two‑qubit entangling gates via quadrupole‑quadrupole Coulomb interaction using adiabatic shuttling between neighboring dots.

2608.21586.title: A minimal mechanism to generate long timescales without fine tuning
2608.21586.summary:
- Introduces a dynamical feedback gain in a linear recurrent neural network to eliminate fine‑tuning of recurrent strength.
- The gain self‑organizes so the effective recurrent matrix spectrum is gapless, with the top eigenvalue at the stability edge.
- This mechanism generically yields long timescales and scale‑free power‑law correlations, confirmed analytically and numerically.

2608.21870.title: Pair Filters in an Extended Hubbard Model at Resonance
2608.21870.summary:
- Bound pairs and single fermions have identical dispersion but scatter differently.
- A neighboring doublon pair is dynamically pinned in the strong‑interaction regime.
- The pinned doublon transmits singlet pairs perfectly while reflecting single fermions, acting as an efficient filter.

2608.22260.title: Anomalous metallic states at magnetic interfaces in an antiferromagnetic topological insulator candidate DyPtBi with ferroquadrupolar order
2608.22260.summary:
- DyPtBi is an antiferromagnetic topological insulator with ferroquadrupolar 4f order.
- Conductive magnetic domain walls are controllable by uniaxial stress and magnetic field, causing abrupt resistivity jumps.
- Compressive stress aligns domains, suppresses domain‑wall conduction, and raises resistivity by ~14 %.

2608.22473.title: Strain-driven spin-flop transition and collapse of the giant magnon gap in the bilayer iridate Sr$_3$Ir$_2$O$_7$
2608.22473.summary:
- Biaxial compression (~–4 %) flips Sr₃Ir₂O₇’s easy axis from the c‑axis to the ab‑plane, collapsing its giant magnon gap.
- A first‑principles magnetic Hamiltonian (no fitting) shows interlayer exchange suppression and in‑plane exchange strengthening drive the flop; Hund’s coupling > 15 eliminates the collinear state.
- Compressed films sit on a metamagnetic boundary ending at a zero‑temperature bicritical point, enabling charge‑neutral control of moment direction.

2608.22517.title: Anomalous dynamical energy flows via nonlinear phononics in spin-Peierls chains
2608.22517.summary:
- THz IR mode nonlinearly excites Raman dimerization, modulating magnetic exchange in a spin‑Peierls chain.
- Energy transfer follows a dynamical impedance‑matching condition; continuous driving induces back‑action, overdamping phonons and broadening magnetic features.
- Short pulses keep the response perturbative, preserving sharp Fano‑like interferences and enabling magnetic control without quenching lattice modes.

2608.22743.title: Role of d-electron density of states in the quantum size effect of Pt-Ni and Pt-Pd nanoparticles
2608.22743.summary:
- QSE detected in Pt–Ni and Pt–Pd nanoparticles via ^195Pt NMR; Pt–Ni shows clear energy discretization, Pt–Pd behaves similarly to Pt.
- Ni enrichment increases d‑electron DOS, lowers T* (Kubo gap), while Pt–Cu lacks QSE.
- Ferromagnetic correlations strengthen with Ni, nearing a quantum‑critical regime, highlighting d‑electron importance.

2608.23081.title: Interplay of Magnetic Order, Structural Stability, and Orbital Ordering in BaFe2X3 (X = S and Se)
2608.23081.summary:
- Stripe‑AFM in BaFe₂S₃ vs. block‑AFM in BaFe₂Se₃, with pressure‑induced superconductivity and orbital‑selective states.
- Resistivity anomalies above T_N show that magnetic order determines crystal structure, orbital ordering, and transport anisotropy.
- The contrasting electronic behavior of the two ladder compounds is explained by the interplay of magnetic configuration, structural stability, and orbital degrees of freedom.

2608.23160.title: Quantics tensor cross interpolation for high-order strong-coupling expansions
2608.23160.summary:
- Uses quantics tensor cross interpolation to cut bond dimensions in high‑order strong‑coupling DMFT.
- Enables self‑consistent steady‑state DMFT up to 4th order and 6th‑order diagram convergence studies.
- Validated on equilibrium and photo‑doped systems, revealing the asymptotic onset of the expansion.

2608.23340.title: Anomalous stabilization of excitons by metallic proximity
2608.23340.summary:
- CuCrO₂ thin films host ~489 meV excitons that redshift by 241 meV as Pd is added, approaching a percolation‑driven metal–insulator transition at x≈
- Image‑charge effects from isolated metallic Pd clusters enhance electron‑hole binding, while a continuous metallic network restores conventional dielectric screening.
- The work demonstrates anomalous exciton stabilization and possible coexistence

2608.23379.title: A DQMC study of the spectral and conductive properties of the two-dimensional Holstein model
2608.23379.summary:
- DQMC study of 2D Holstein model across phonon energies, couplings, doping, and temperature.
- Calculated spectral function and optical conductivity, revealing a transition from dressed metal → polaron liquid/insulator → CDW insulator.
- Results corroborated by equal‑time correlations and released as an extensive open dataset (~16,640 points).

2608.23442.title: Interaction-mediated Co-existence of Altermagnetism and Topology
2608.23442.summary:
- Extended Hubbard model on Lieb lattice (filling 2, produces simultaneous altermagnetic order and topological gap.
- Unrestricted Hartree‑Fock and exact diagonalization confirm coexistence and a quantum spin Hall effect over a large phase region.
- Breaking inversion symmetry yields second‑order topological phases with corner modes.

2608.24925.title: Self-assembly and Electronic Properties of Graphyne and Graphdiyne Molecular Wires on Metallic Surfaces
2608.24925.summary:
- Non‑aligned graphyne/graphdiyne wire arrays are energetically favored on Au(, Ag(, and Al(due to van der Waals binding.
- Molecular orbitals do not form interface states; XPS C 1s peaks shift uniformly, indicating dominant metallic screening.
- Band‑structure calculations reveal preserved semiconducting character with negligible hybridization, supporting their use in molecular electronics.

2608.24927.title: Reply to Comment on: Microscopic signatures of an imaginary charge density wave in a kagome metal
2608.24927.summary:
- Refutes crystalline mosaicity as cause of asymmetric NMR spectra in kagome metal.
- Argues mosaicity would require unrealistic temperature‑ and site‑dependent orientation and EFG asymmetry distributions.
- Concludes mosaicity cannot explain the observed site‑selective spectral asymmetry.

2608.24950.title: A Simple Regularization of the Smooth Quantum Hydrodynamic Model
2608.24950.summary:
- Introduces a regularization replacing density gradients in the momentum equation with a Boltzmann distribution to suppress unstable modes.
- Applies the regularized smooth quantum hydrodynamic model to a resonant tunneling diode, reproducing realistic negative differential resistance and hysteresis.
- Demonstrates close agreement with fully quantum mechanical simulations for the diode’s current‑voltage characteristics.

2608.24967.title: Heat Transfer and Torque in Enclosing Cylindrical Configurations with Nonreciprocal Materials
2608.24967.summary:
- Torque in enclosing cylindrical setups is bounded by heat transfer when at least one object is rotationally symmetric; nonreciprocal media are required for nonzero torque if both are symmetric.
- For concentric cylinders with nonreciprocal dielectric, heat transfer and torque are expressed via an angular‑momentum‑resolved flux Φₙ(ω), and a new analytic Casimir force formula for dilute plates at different temperatures is derived.
- A bound between torque, friction, and heat transfer limits the efficiency of a contactless rotational heat engine.

2608.24980.title: Nonlocal thermal noise in electrically coupled conductors: A microscopic two-dimensional study
2608.24980.summary:
- Simulations of capacitively coupled wires show temperature‑gradient‑induced nonlocal correlations in electromotive forces, breaking the local‑noise assumption.
- The model reproduces Ohm’s law, equilibrium Johnson noise, and zero correlations at equal temperature, but predicts systematic deviations in inferred Johnson temperature when wires differ in temperature.
- Results suggest that independent local thermal‑noise sources are invalid for electrically coupled conductors out of equilibrium, even with short‑range interactions.

2608.24984.title: High-harmonic fingerprints of sharp spin twists in a chiral soliton lattice
2608.24984.summary:
- HHG from itinerant electrons in a CSL directly probes lattice‑scale spin twists.
- Intensity grows nonperturbatively with drive amplitude as winding localizes, driven by spatially varying hopping.
- In the continuum limit (large magnetic period) high‑order harmonics collapse, showing HHG resolves real‑space CSL structure.

2608.24989.title: Quantum spin Hall crystals at fractional filling of twisted MoTe$_2$
2608.24989.summary:
- Predicts interaction‑driven quantum spin Hall crystals (QSHCs) that emerge at fractional filling through topology and spontaneous translation‑symmetry breaking.
- Finds 9‑fold quasi‑degenerate √3×√3 charge‑ordered QSHCs at ν = −8/3 in 5° twisted MoTe₂, organized by a Z₃ index into TR‑invariant Z₂ topological states and TR‑related doublets with U(_v spin‑Chern number.
- Determines the conditions that favor QSHCs over competing intervalley‑coherent crystals.

2608.24995.title: Microscopic Modeling of the Charge-Density-Waves in the Rare-Earth Tritellurides
2608.24995.summary:
- Mean‑field 2D electron‑phonon model yields a unidirectional CDW with the experimentally observed ordering vector.
- Predicts two successive symmetry‑breaking transitions: CDW onset, then a lower‑temperature translation‑symmetry breaking seen in heavy‑rare‑earth RTe₃.
- Reveals an intermediate mirror‑symmetry‑breaking transition, accounting for recent experimental evidence of mirror‑symmetry breaking.

2608.25002.title: Photonic spin-Hall effect as a probe for time-reversal-symmetry broken band topological phases
2608.25002.summary:
- PSHE causes spatial splitting of reflected Gaussian beam into opposite circular polarizations.
- Centroid shift of the split beams directly measures optical Hall conductivity, revealing topological order.
- Frequency‑dependent sign of the shift distinguishes time‑reversal‑symmetry‑broken topological phases from trivial ones.

2608.25076.title: High-pressure phase transitions in the quantum spin liquid candidate Na2Co2TeO6 probed by Raman spectroscopy
2608.25076.summary:
- Raman study of Na₂Co₂TeO₆ up to 3 GPa shows three distinct pressure regimes.
- Mode appearance/disappearance and polarization changes, notably above 8 GPa, signal pressure‑induced phase transitions.
- Results imply pressure‑tuned bond geometry can alter Kitaev exchange in this quantum spin liquid candidate.

2608.25132.title: The Effects of Inter-Valley Coupling of Dirac Fermions near Four Dimensions
2608.25132.summary:
- One-loop RG in 4‑ε shows inter‑valley coupling destabilizes the decoupled GNY fixed point.
- A new stable fixed point emerges with distinct critical exponents and broken Lorentz invariance from valley‑frame rotations.
- At large Nψ the inter‑valley coupling stays finite, yet Lorentz symmetry is asymptotically restored.

2608.25224.title: Dynamical splitting and a nodal Bose liquid in 2d chiral XYZ model
2608.25224.summary:
- Introduces “dynamical splitting” allowing exact diagonalization on lattices ~2× larger.
- Applies to chiral XYZ on triangular lattice; large‑N limit yields gapless state with three nodal lines.
- N=2 exact results show \(L\log L\) entanglement and CFT‑like chord scaling, confirming a nodal Bose liquid.

2608.25265.title: Electric excitation of spin resonance in altermagnetic and antiferromagnetic conductors
2608.25265.summary:
- Predicts electric‑dipole spin resonance (EDSR) in altermagnetic conductors.
- In a magnetic field perpendicular to the magnetization, an AC electric field produces a spin‑resonance peak above the threshold frequency ω₋ = 2H⊥.
- EDSR can diagnose altermagnetism and differentiate it from higher‑symmetry antiferromagnetic order in clean samples.

2608.25656.title: Phase calibration of quantum oscillations in the magnetostrictive coefficient using the topological antiferromagnet YbMnBi$_2$
2608.25656.summary:
- Calibrated phase offset of quantum oscillations in the ac magnetostrictive coefficient by direct comparison with magnetization in YbMnBi₂.
- Identified a single 160 T frequency up to 14 T, eliminating multi‑frequency ambiguity.
- Observed a ~π/2 phase shift between magnetostrictive and magnetization oscillations, confirming the Maxwell relation and enabling Berry‑phase extraction.

2608.25778.title: Quasi two dimensional magnetic structure of the triclinic double perovskite Ca$_2$CuWO$_6$
2608.25778.summary:
- Ca₂CuWO₆ orders antiferromagnetically below 32 K with k = (½,½,in triclinic P ¯1, collinear Cu moments ≈ 66 µB.
- Using a common supercell, the same W‑mediated second‑neighbor exchange stabilizes the magnetic structure in both Ca₂CuWO₆ and Sr₂CuWO₆.
- Triclinic symmetry lifts the four‑domain degeneracy of Sr₂CuWO₆, selecting a single k‑domain in Ca₂CuWO₆.

2608.26231.title: When chemical potential continuity fails: kinetic interface models for hydrogen isotope transport
2608.26231.summary: - LTE interface models assume fast equilibration, a single exchange pathway, and known carrier species—assumptions that break down at metal/molten‑salt boundaries.

2608.26245.title: Exact pair density wave in topological moire flat bands and universal superfluid stiffness
2608.26245.summary:
- Exact PDW ground state realized in a twisted bilayer checkerboard lattice with topological flat bands via quantum geometric nesting.
- Momentum‑space nonsymmorphic symmetry stabilizes the PDW against competing orders.
- Universal superfluid stiffness: \(D_s = 2N_{\text{flat}}\nu(1-\nu)/m_{\text{pair}}\) for any nondegenerate QGN superconductor.

2608.26252.title: Quantized Transport through a Supermoir\'e Chern Mosaic
2608.26252.summary:
- Magic‑angle helical trilayer graphene forms a mosaic of domains with opposite valley Chern numbers, hosting a network of domain‑wall modes.
- A moderate magnetic field triggers a valley‑selective topological transition, opening a global C = –6 Chern gap that gaps the domain‑wall modes.
- Hall resistance in this gap is quantized to within 2 % of –h/6e² at 6 K, demonstrating robust quantized transport.

2608.26260.title: Hidden Frustration in Collinear Altermagnets: Pairing Vortices and Equilibrium Spin Current Loops
2608.26260.summary:
- Collinear altermagnets exhibit a gauge‑irreversible vortex‑antivortex pair in magnon pair correlations from staggered Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya coupling.
- Hidden vortices produce an antiferrochiral array of equilibrium spin‑current loops around neighboring plaquettes.
- Quantum frustration survives classical collinearity, linking squeezed‑vacuum spin correlations to flux‑phase and spin‑liquid physics.

2608.26264.title: Statistics as a local phase: crystalline order and quench dynamics of emergent dimers in Ising gauge theories
2608.26264.summary:
- Emergent dimers in a 2+1D ℤ₂ gauge theory inherit the microscopic particle statistics via a single local hopping phase ϕ (0 for bosons, π for fermions).
- The phase diagram, mapped with tensor‑network methods, shows a ϕ‑driven transition from a dimer superfluid to a charge‑density‑wave, plus a novel gapped phase of resonating plaquette crystals.
- A quench protocol reveals distinct real‑time dynamics for identical dimer configurations, enabling dynamical detection of the underlying statistics and ordered phases.

2608.26265.title: Supercurrent detection and manipulation of topological phase transitions in Shiba-Majorana hybrid systems
2608.26265.summary:
- Detects ground‑state parity changes in Shiba‑Majorana chains by measuring supercurrent.
- Observes sharp critical‑current discontinuities at zero‑energy level crossings.
- Implements a robust, non‑invasive readout using a single control adatom with a Yu‑Shiba‑Rusinov state.

2608.26269.title: How quantum is quantum geometry?
2608.26269.summary:
- Classical particle with magnetic moment in a momentum‑dependent field reproduces Berry‑curvature and quantum‑metric phenomena.
- Transverse precession generates a position spread whose second moment equals the quantum metric, plus an orbital magnetic moment and inertial mass.
- The induced inertial mass yields a nonzero Drude weight in a nominally flat band, illustrating classical origins of quantum‑geometric observables.

2608.26270.title: Time and Momentum Resolved Tunneling Spectroscopy of Floquet dynamics
2608.26270.summary:
- Time‑ and momentum‑resolved tunneling spectroscopy probes instantaneous Floquet spectra beyond the high‑frequency limit, capturing transient and non‑adiabatic dynamics.
- Method benchmarked on driven non‑interacting fermions and extended to strongly correlated systems via time‑dependent DMRG.
- Microscopic explanation of resonantly induced in‑gap states and brief discussion of finite‑temperature analogs.

2608.26279.title: Critical Properties and Glass Transitions in Randomly Coupled Fields
2608.26279.summary:
- Random scalar fields with quenched random couplings form Gaussian universality classes set by eigenvalue density near the spectral edge.
- Wigner coupling gives diverging correlation length but finite susceptibility; one‑loop replica analysis points to an upper critical dimension of one.
- In the solvable spherical variant, heat capacity jumps for \(d>1\) and the glass phase preserves critical correlations, yielding scale invariance without Goldstone modes.

2608.26312.title: Milled to order: toward predictive mechanochemistry of halide perovskites
2608.26312.summary:
- Mechanochemical milling can scale solvent‑free synthesis of halide perovskites, aiming to shift from empirical to predictive control.
- Key questions: are milled phases truly metastable or just routes to equilibrium, and what atomistic pathways govern their formation?
- Achieving programmable metastability would unlock new compositions and intermediates,

2608.26347.title: Dynamical signatures of deconfined spinons in dimerized sawtooth chains
2608.26347.summary:
- Broad two‑spinon continuum dominates the zero‑temperature DSF, with the one‑triplon peak strongly suppressed.
- Closed‑form spinon dispersions set the continuum edges and track the dominant band across the dimerized phase, VBS point, and first‑order boundary.
- The results

2608.26534.title: Competition between Geometrical Frustration and the Kondo Effect in CePdAl Revealed by High-Resolution Magnetization
2608.26534.summary:
- First‑order metamagnetic transitions at 80 mK without plateaus, showing frustration lifted by Kondo suppression and spin flips.
- Anomaly in nonlinear susceptibility at 3 T reveals nondipolar correlations in the polarized paramagnetic state.
- Absence of non‑Fermi‑liquid behavior in the high‑field, AFM‑suppressed regime defines thermodynamic limits for the field‑induced spin‑liquid in CePdAl.

2608.26540.title: Field-amplified readouts of weak altermagnetic exchange in MnF$_2$
2608.26540.summary:
- MnF₂’s sublattice‑odd exchange (δJ₇≈+8 µeV) is resolved by first‑principles mapping, confirming its altermagnetic character.
- A longitudinal field B∥c linearly amplifies this hidden scale, producing two measurable signatures: a compensation field B*≈34 T and a fixed‑field contrast ≈

2608.26609.title: Thermally quenched metastability in metal-insulator transitions via elemental substitution
2608.26609.summary:
- Rapid cooling (>10⁹ K s⁻¹) suppresses the VO₂ metal‑insulator transition when tungsten is substituted, trapping a long‑lived metallic phase.
- Relaxation follows nucleation‑dominated kinetics with a thermally activated barrier introduced by W.
- Elemental substitution thus provides a route to thermally quenched metastability in electronic phase transitions.

2608.26751.title: Interlayer-engineering of Charge Order Wave Vector in Kagome Metals
2608.26751.summary:
- Interlayer coupling tunes CsV₃Sb₅ from a 4×1 charge order in the monolayer to a 2×2 order in the bulk.
- Monolayer phonons show instability at q = (¼, 0, ; increasing interlayer spacing softens the M‑point phonon, triggering the bulk 2×2 instability.
- The study unifies surface‑observed 4×1 and bulk‑observed 2×2 charge orders as competing tendencies controlled by dimensionality.

2608.27134.title: 3D- (H-theta-phi) magnetic phase diagram of antiferromagnetic metal GdB6 with electron and lattice instability
2608.27134.summary:
- GdB6 exhibits static Jahn‑Teller distortions and dynamic charge stripes, producing anisotropic charge transport.
- Two antiferromagnetic phases (AF I, AF II) form an impeller‑shaped H–φ phase diagram in the (and (planes.
- A 5d spin‑density wave and stripe‑induced RKKY suppression generate the observed anisotropy and phase boundaries.

2608.27200.title: Multi-orbital physics in inverse Lieb lattice altermagnets
2608.27200.summary:
- Developed symmetry‑based microscopic Hamiltonian for inverse Lieb lattice altermagnets, incorporating sublattice and orbital degrees of freedom.
- Applied to vanadium oxychalcogenides: \(xy\) orbitals stabilize altermagnetism; Hund’s coupling induces \(xz/yz\) orbital order.
- Multi‑orbital models uncover orbital‑selective topological edge states.

2608.27411.title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
2608.27411.summary:
- Continuous confinement–deconfinement transition in TlYbS₂: antiferromagnetic order below 53 K gives way to a gapless spin‑liquid with a spinon Fermi surface at μ₀H_c≈3 T.
- Signatures: finite residual κ/T, Pauli‑like susceptibility, T‑independent NMR Knight shift, and enhanced scattering rate without critical density‑of‑states growth.
- Indicates a quantum critical point governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg–Landau paradigm.

cond-mat/0401304.title: Quantum-magneto oscillations in a supramolecular Mn(II)-[3 x 3] grid
cond-mat/0401304.summary:
- High‑field torque magnetometry on Mn(II)-[3 × 3] grid reveals oscillatory torque vs. field above 5 T.
- Oscillations observed at 3 He temperatures, indicating quantum‑magneto effects.
- A theoretical model successfully reproduces the magneto‑oscillation behavior.

cond-mat/0401293.title: Ferromagnetism in Fe-doped SnO2 thin films
cond-mat/0401293.summary:
- Fe‑doped SnO₂ thin films are transparent ferromagnets with TC ≈ 610 K and Ms ≈ 2 Am²/kg.
- Mossbauer spectra reveal high‑spin Fe³⁺; only ~23 % of Fe ions are magnetically ordered, each carrying ~8 µB.
- Ferromagnetism attributed to Fe³⁺ coupling through an electron trapped in an oxygen vacancy (F‑center).

cond-mat/0401296.title: Ultrafast Conductivity Dynamics in Pentacene Probed using Terahertz Spectroscopy
cond-mat/0401296.summary:
- Measured picosecond photoconductivity in pentacene crystals via optical‑pump THz‑probe.
- Mobility drops from ~4 cm²/Vs at 30 K to ~2 cm²/Vs at room temperature.
- THz signal indicates rapid (< ps) trapping of photoexcited carriers, likely by excitons, polarons, or impurities.

cond-mat/0401292.title: Phases of a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate with anharmonic confinement
cond-mat/0401292.summary:
- Identified three phases (multiple, single, mixed quantization) in a rotating BEC with quadratic‑plus‑quartic confinement.
- Derived a universal phase diagram; continuous transitions exact for weak coupling and small anharmonicity.
- Variational predictions agree with Gross‑Pitaevskii numerical solutions.

cond-mat/0401280.title: Observation of narrow fluorescence from doubly driven four-level atoms at room temperature
cond-mat/0401280.summary:
- Narrow fluorescence peaks appear in Rb‑85 under dual‑laser 3D molasses; one laser fixed detuned from cooling transition, the other scanned over repumping lines.
- Peaks form symmetric pairs whose separation increases with cooling‑laser detuning; large detunings yield additional small peaks.
- A simple model explains the observed spectral features.

cond-mat/0401279.title: Fluorescence from doubly driven four-level atoms - A density matrix approach
cond-mat/0401279.summary:
- Four‑level density‑matrix model reproduces narrow Rb‑85 fluorescence peaks under cooling and repumper lasers.
- Quantum interference alters probe‑induced population transfer, sharpening double‑resonance velocity selection.
- Co‑ and counter‑propagating beam geometry yields narrow fluorescence peaks in a room‑temperature thermal gas.

quant-ph/0401089.title: Optical conductivity of small adiabatic polarons with a long-range electron-phonon interaction
quant-ph/0401089.summary:
- Calculated optical conductivity and effective mass of small adiabatic Fröhlich polarons at zero temperature.
- Compared results with small adiabatic Holstein polarons, highlighting differences due to long‑range electron‑phonon coupling.
- Modeled ions as isotropic 3D oscillators to analyze electron hopping and optical absorption.

cond-mat/0401267.title: A first principles simulation of rigid water
cond-mat/0401267.summary:
- CP simulations of water with rigid molecules use larger time steps, enabling longer time scales.
- Structural properties and diffusion coefficients from the rigid model match experiments better than flexible simulations.
- The approach paves the way for ab initio studies of aqueous solutions (e.g., hydrophobic solvation) beyond current time‑scale limits.

cond-mat/0401232.title: Origin of asymmetric reversal modes in ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic multilayers
cond-mat/0401232.summary:
- Asymmetric reversal modes appear in certain exchange‑bias multilayers.
- Domain‑state simulations show the effect depends on the angle between the AFM easy axis and the applied field.
- At specific angles the FM reverses symmetrically via coherent rotation; at others it reverses asymmetrically, sometimes producing zero perpendicular magnetization.

cond-mat/0401212.title: Vortex waves and the onset of turbulence in $^3$He-B
cond-mat/0401212.summary:
- Finne et al. identified the intrinsic turbulence onset criterion \(q=\alpha/(1-\alpha')<1\) in \(^{3}\)He‑B.
- The criterion corresponds to marginally damped Kelvin waves; for \(q>1\) waves cannot grow to trigger reconnections.
- Analysis of rotating‑superfluid modes confirms \(q=1\) as the crossover between damped and propagating Kelvin waves in the long‑wavelength limit.

2608.27457.title: Spectral Fingerprints of Gauge Theories on a Quantum Computer
2608.27457.summary:
- Unbiased maximally mixed state spectral sampling extracts finite‑resolution spectra across the entire energy range of a Hamiltonian.
- Applied to a (1+d SO(gauge theory, the algorithm runs on near‑term superconducting hardware with 78 two‑qubit‑gate depth and halves qubit count via dynamical circuits.
- Introduces Pauli‑frame compilation for controlled‑time evolution, trivial readout‑error mitigation, and post‑processing for disordered transitions and mid‑spectrum density of states.

2608.27453.title: Metallogenic quantum criticality: Fermi surface nucleation at transitions between gapped phases
2608.27453.summary:
- MGQCP: a quantum critical point where a full Fermi surface emerges between two fully gapped insulators, breaking the usual isolated‑point gaplessness rule.
- Effective field theory for transitions between distinct fractional Chern insulators shows conformal transport scaling yet a non‑Fermi‑liquid electron spectral function.
- Minimal microscopic realization: a periodically modulated quantum Hall bilayer, with implications for tunable Chern bands in moiré materials.

2608.27446.title: Exact Stiffness and Dynamical Responses from Fock-Space Fragmentation
2608.27446.summary:
- QGN models show Fock‑space fragmentation: excitations split into Krylov subspaces with fixed particle‑hole number, giving dynamically invariant sectors.
- The stiffness of the broken continuous symmetry equals its variational Gaussian value; a phase twist couples only to the one‑particle–one‑hole fragment, making the variational curvature exact.
- Perturbations staying within a fixed fragment yield exact response functions (susceptibility, conductivity, structure factors, Green’s functions) from the corresponding few‑body sector.

2608.27445.title: Band's Geometry Origin of Quantum Spin Transport Phenomena
2608.27445.summary:
- Geometric framework links band/Fermi‑surface structure to spin‑dependent transport.
- Hyperbolic constant‑energy regions generate a Fermi‑velocity term that drives spin currents.
- Time‑reversal symmetry maps spin operators to the band’s exterior algebra, enabling a symplectic/contact‑geometric description of spin‑separated transport.

2608.27228.title: 2-Morita Theory of $E_2$-Algebras and Module Categories
2608.27228.summary:
- Introduces $n$‑Morita categories $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$ to unify $n$‑Morita equivalence for $E_n$‑algebras and topological orders.
- Proves for $n=1,2$ that the functor $\mathrm{Mod}_n$ is an equivalence, linking algebraic higher Morita theory with module‑category realizations.
- Uses bi‑bimodules and orientation data to describe local and confined modules, clarifying defect fusion rules from condensation.

2608.26954.title: Decoupled domain-texture switching from magnetic easy axis in kagome ferromagnet EuTi3Bi4
2608.26954.summary:
- Domain orientation in EuTi₃Bi₄ switches between a‑ and b‑axes with temperature or an out‑of‑plane field, despite a fixed c‑axis easy magnetization.
- Switching arises from competing in‑plane anisotropies: single‑ion anisotropy favors a‑axis, while nearest‑neighbor anisotropic exchange favors b‑axis.
- Exfoliated flakes raise the critical switching temperature, demonstrating tunable texture control via in‑plane interaction balance.

2608.27519.title: Exact branch-transfer criterion for common-mode Thomson heat cancellation in thermoelectric couples
2608.27519.summary:
- Exact branch‑transfer criterion: common‑mode Thomson heat cancels iff the differential thermopower measures of the p‑ and n‑branches are equal.
- In the linear‑common‑mode limit, matching \(R_i/K_i^{\text{leg}}\) suffices for cancellation, even with non‑identical legs.
- Derived array law for split thermal pads: \(\Delta Q_{c,\Sigma}=\sum_j C_j I_j \Delta T_{c,j}\); for series elements with isothermal hot pairs, \(I\Delta V_\Sigma=-\Delta Q_{c,\Sigma}\).

2608.27520.title: Asphericity Lifts the Degeneracy Among Ordering Mechanisms on Curved Surfaces
2608.27520.summary:
- Spherical surfaces hide the signature of different ordering mechanisms; asphericity lifts this degeneracy.
- On an ellipsoid, mechanisms separate into distinct powers of the distance to the tangent plane, readable from the structure‑factor quadrupole and radius of gyration.
- Riesz s‑energy shows a sharp transition at a marginal power, while screened Coulomb potential lets ionic strength continuously tune the exponent, enabling experimental control of the conductor‑to‑packing crossover.

2608.27533.title: Ab initio Modeling of MoS2/Oxide Device Interfaces with Machine Learned Electronic Structures
2608.27533.summary:
- ML‑electronic structure + QT solver gives 10,000× speedup for >20k‑atom MoS₂/oxide devices.
- Explicit HfO₂/Al₂O₃ oxides modeled in transport domain for single‑layer MoS₂ FETs.
- Undercoordinated Hf/Al atoms at the interface strongly modify current magnitude and propagation.

2608.27552.title: Collinear altermagnetism for 3D chiral higher-order topological insulators
2608.27552.summary:
- Altermagnetism on a Lieb lattice combined with a 3D TI produces a chiral \(C_4\mathcal{T}\)-protected higher‑order topological insulator.
- The collinear \(d\)-wave magnetism shifts and gaps surface Dirac cones, yielding chiral hinge channels.
- Candidate material classes are identified, demonstrating altermagnetism as a viable route to intrinsic chiral HOTIs.

2608.27572.title: Scale-free correlations in extremely persistent active matter
2608.27572.summary:
- Demonstrates algebraic decay of density and swim‑velocity correlations as \(r^{-(d+}\) (with log corrections in 2D) for infinitely persistent active Brownian particles at low density and small swim velocity.
- Finds corresponding cusps at \(k=0\) in reciprocal space, confirming scale‑free behavior.
- Validates analytical predictions with numerical simulations.

2608.27587.title: Compiling Chemical Knowledge into Executable Descriptors for Materials Prediction
2608.27587.summary:
- CRISP generates, consolidates, and compiles chemical rules into scalar descriptors using a language‑model, without requiring labeled data.
- For inorganic‑crystal synthesizability, CRISP outperforms expert‑curated and generic representations and surpasses specialized models, especially under domain shifts.
- The same workflow yields competitive descriptors for formation energy and ionic conductivity, revealing task‑specific limits for shear modulus and offering a dataset‑blind, auditable knowledge‑to‑representation pipeline.

2608.27588.title: Topological signatures in the quench dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems
2608.27588.summary:
- Quench of graphene by circularly polarized light produces a period‑averaged edge bond current that oscillates around a dc value, signaling an induced topological phase.
- In an isolated ribbon the dc current equals Floquet band currents weighted by their occupations; coupling to a fermionic bath causes the current and conductance to rise then saturate to a nonequilibrium steady state.
- In the weak‑coupling limit the summed conductance is quantized, revealing the number of edge modes at the zero‑quasienergy and Floquet‑zone‑boundary gaps, confirmed by two‑terminal transport in a finite‑size model.

2608.27589.title: Atomistic Indicators of the Ductile-to-Brittle Transition in Polycrystalline Tungsten: Temperature and Rhenium Effects on Crack-Tip Plasticity
2608.27589.summary:
- Temperature lowers instability stress and stiffness in W, with a sigmoid crossover near 870 K under high‑rate loading.
- 10 % Re increases pre‑instability plasticity and work accumulation, modifying dislocation pathways instead of merely strengthening.
- Re alters retained ½<111> line character and the timing of near‑tip dislocation activity, offering atomistic markers of the ductile‑to‑brittle transition.

2608.27590.title: Physics-informed learning for the inverse problem in resonant ultrasound spectroscopy
2608.27590.summary:
- Physics‑informed learning transforms the resonant‑ultrasound inverse problem into a constrained regression on a low‑dimensional manifold of admissible elasticity tensors.
- The method uses reduced spectral and geometric features (length, scale, aspect ratio, scale‑free spectral signatures, stability‑respecting ratios) to analytically recover full elastic constants.
- Benchmark results: MAE ≈ 20 GPa (C₁₁), 24 GPa (C₁₂), 2 GPa (C₄₄); MAPE 4–
