2609.23978.title: Decoupling the Magnetic Field Operator as an Independent Operator Class in Stochastic Series Expansion Quantum Monte Carlo
2609.23978.summary:
- Treats magnetic field as an independent operator class in SSE QMC, enabling it to update like other terms.
- Validated on the 2D antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model; results agree with conventional SSE.
- Achieves competitive autocorrelation times and simplifies measurement of field‑related observables.

2609.23993.title: A Majorana Formulation of Time-Dependent Two-Particle Reduced-Density-Matrix Dynamics
2609.23993.summary:
- Time‑dependent two‑particle RDM algorithm for interacting Majorana fermions, closing BBGKY at the two‑particle level via three‑particle reconstruction.
- Stabilized by a positivity projection that preserves energy; outperforms Hartree–Fock on Hubbard quenches and Kitaev flux dynamics.
- Gauge coherence is essential for flux dynamics; the projection induces effective irreversibility impacting long‑time evolution.

2609.25075.title: Multimodal Visual Sensing of Temperature and Pressure: From Spectroscopic Readout to Multiple Linear Regression-Enhanced RGB Analysis
2609.25075.summary:
- Tunable KGaGeO4:Bi³⁺,Eu³⁺ host allows selective thermometry or manometry via dopant balance.
- Bi³⁺ and Eu³⁺ luminescence

2609.25079.title: Thermally Robust and Strongly Pressure-Responsive NIR Luminescent Manometer Based on Cr3+-Ni2+ Emission
2609.25079.summary:
- NaLu₂Ga₃Ge₂O₁₂:Cr³⁺,Ni²⁺ exhibits record pressure sensitivity (Ni²⁺ 3T₂→3A₂ band shifts 34 nm GPa⁻¹, ratiometric 158 % GPa⁻¹).
- Ratiometric NIR readout achieves a thermal‑invariance factor of 19 900 K GPa⁻¹, the highest known.
- Combines high pressure sensitivity, NIR operation, and thermal robustness for accurate pressure sensing under temperature variations.

2609.25205.title: Re-entrant p-wave superconductivity in a Chern Dartboard Insulator
2609.25205.summary:
- Exact 2‑band superconductor theory with inter‑orbital pairing and HK interactions applied to a Chern dartboard insulator.
- HK interaction lifts the doubly‑occupied band, inducing superconductivity in the BCS‑predicted insulating phase.
- Re‑entrant insulator–superconductor–insulator transition occurs (U = 1, μ = due to the interplay of HK interactions and inter‑orbital pairing.

2609.25210.title: Kitaev spin liquid in superconducting networks
2609.25210.summary:
- Realizes Kitaev honeycomb Hamiltonian in a superconducting metamaterial using Cooper‑pair boxes and semiconductor–superconductor heterostructures.
- Bond‑directional interactions arise from normal and anomalous virtual propagation, controlled by out‑of‑plane flux and semiconductor Fermi energy.
- Numerical analysis identifies an experimentally accessible regime with suppressed corrections, enabling equilibrium quantum spin liquids.

2609.25223.title: Scaling of qubit coherence in quantum dot based Majorana chains: Rabi and Ramsey oscillations of Majorana qubits formed by four and six quantum dots
2609.25223.summary:
- Rabi oscillations remain length‑independent in the pristine limit, but disorder limits coherence via three competing dephasing channels.
- Ramsey oscillations in six‑dot chains suffer larger leakage because the third site suppresses unwanted splittings yet requires larger detuning that excites bulk states.
- Neither Rabi nor Ramsey coherence universally improves with chain length; extra dots help only if inter‑chain tunneling fluctuations are suppressed, while Ramsey coherence depends on detuning‑induced energy‑splitting fluctuations.

2609.25226.title: Disorder-promoted stability
2609.25226.summary:
- Heterogeneity can enhance stability in high‑dimensional, non‑Hermitian network dynamics, contrary to earlier findings.
- Disorder acts as a stabilizing resource across neural, power‑grid, material, and ecological networks.
- Non‑reciprocal interactions in one‑dimensional dynamics also yield stability via non‑Hermitian effects.

2609.25242.title: From Effective Temperature to Non-Boltzmann State Selection in Driven-Dissipative Quantum Criticality
2609.25242.summary:
- Large‑N analysis uncovers an overdamped open quantum‑critical regime distinct from the closed Lipkin–Meshkov–Glick model.
- Fluctuations in the quantum‑critical fan are governed by an effective temperature \(T_{\rm eff}\), which

2609.25243.title: Extended symmetric quantum phase in a honeycomb Heisenberg model with sublattice-selective interactions
2609.25243.summary:
- Identified an extended symmetric phase (4 ≲ J′₂/J₁ ≲ on the honeycomb lattice with no magnetic, valence‑bond, or chiral order.
- Numerical evidence (iPEPS, MPS, ED) shows diverging correlation length and algebraic scaling, indicating a gapless spin‑liquid ground state.
- Proposed a symmetry‑protected Z₂ Dirac spin‑liquid parton state as a candidate, while also considering a possible short‑range entangled gapped phase.

2609.25252.title: Approach to Steady-State in Nested Resetting Processes
2609.25252.summary:
- Derived accumulation times to quantify first‑passage to steady state in nested resetting processes.
- For equal rates, closed‑form wavefront relaxation with linearly increasing delay along the chain.
- For heterogeneous rates, exact steady‑state distributions, moments, and accumulation times; relaxation governed by the minimum resetting rate and its multiplicity.

2609.25263.title: Order-parameter-dependent mobility in the Convective-Viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation
2609.25263.summary:
- Mobility in Cahn‑Hilliard equations can depend on the order parameter, yet constant mobility is often assumed.
- The paper analyzes reciprocal linear and quadratic mobility forms and obtains exact traveling‑wave solutions.
- Reciprocal quadratic mobility provides a good approximation to polynomial mobilities within a limited parameter range.

2609.25283.title: Thermally melted quadrupolar order and intrinsically quantum phases in 5$d^1$ double perovskites
2609.25283.summary:
- Classical Monte Carlo on the j = 3/2 FCC lattice shows thermal melting of the intermediate‑temperature quadrupolar phase in 5d¹ double perovskites.
- Four‑sublattice AFM and FM phases stay robustly classical, while the coplanar canted FM[110] state collapses, revealing it as an intrinsically quantum phase.
- Thermal fluctuations selectively destabilize quadrupolar order, mapping the boundary between classical and quantum stability.

2609.25384.title: Lattice in Line: Optimized DMRG ordering for complex lattice geometries
2609.25384.summary:
- Optimized DMRG site ordering via proxy loss functions: bandwidth \(B\), cutwidth \(C\), and average interaction range \(R\).
- Lexicographic targeting of \((C,R)\) gives the lowest energies; \(B\) only indirectly reduces \(C\) and is largely irrelevant.
- A staged CP‑SAT (Google OR‑Tools) solver outperforms classic heuristics and QUBO formulations for lattice compilation.

2609.25418.title: Coherent lattice dynamics distinguish Holstein and Su-Schrieffer-Heeger electron-phonon coupling
2609.25418.summary:
- Time‑dependent DMRG of a 1D Mott insulator with Holstein vs. SSH phonon coupling.
- Electronic responses are alike, but Holstein yields long‑lived coherent phonon oscillations at resonance, SSH does not.
- Coherent lattice dynamics thus serve as a direct nonequilibrium probe of the microscopic e‑ph coupling mechanism.

2609.25494.title: Efficiency of Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo Updates in the Ferromagnetic State of the Doped SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
2609.25494.summary:
- Segment‑based CT‑HYB solver efficiency examined for doped SU(Hubbard model in DMFT.
- Double‑flip update gives lowest autocorrelation in ferromagnetic regime; flavor‑permutation update excels in paramagnetic regime.
- Effectiveness traced to distinct occupation changes induced by each update.

2609.25585.title: Model Fractional Quantum Hall States on Lattices: Exact Parent Hamiltonians and Routes to Realization
2609.25585.summary:
- Built Hermitian parent Hamiltonians whose zero‑mode manifold consists of lattice‑sampled continuum LLL model states.
- Short‑range density interactions stabilize Laughlin ground states at ν=1/3, 1/4; onsite repulsion yields a Moore–Read triplet at ν=
- Multiband calculations show Laughlin manifolds remain robust to interband mixing, whereas the Moore–Read triplet loses spectral isolation and crosses competing states near the interband scale.

2609.25829.title: Strong coupling polarons in cavity quantum materials: limits of cavity-induced electron mass renormalization
2609.25829.summary:
- Mass renormalization stems from field‑mediated coupling between electrons and polarizable cavity mirrors.
- 2D electron path integral solved exactly with quantum Monte Carlo.
- Upper bound set by the Landau‑Pekar polaron in planar geometry, linking cavity control to dielectric engineering.

2609.26807.title: Exact Collision Vertex for Stress and Heat Flux
2609.26807.summary:
- Exact nonlinear generating vertex for collisional stress and heat‑flux in hard‑sphere Boltzmann equation.
- Stress hierarchy reduces to a universal traceless tensor times a scalar radial law; heat flux obtained by exact contraction.
- DSMC tests confirm predictions; convergence independent of the Gaussian foot used in Hermite representation.

2609.26815.title: Electrothermal Compact Drift Model of TiO$_2$ Memristors: Verilog-A Implementation and Dimensionless Regime Mapping
2609.26815.summary:
- ATDM couples Strukov‑style drift to an Arrhenius‑mobility heat balance, adding one thermal state while keeping the electrical state variable.
- Verilog‑A implementation matches a reference model within 009 % peak‑voltage error and recovers isothermal limits at zero activation energy.
- Dimensionless analysis introduces thermal lag ε and switching number Θ, mapping valid quasi‑static regimes and proving the reduced stroboscopic map is strictly increasing, precluding period‑doubling or chaos.

2609.26844.title: Suppressed Defect Emission and Enhanced Blue Luminescence of Zn-Doped CuBr Quantum Dots synthesized in Room-Temperature Synthesis
2609.26844.summary:
- Zn doping suppresses defect emission and enhances blue luminescence in CuBr QDs.
- Eco‑friendly room‑temperature synthesis yields 46 nm QDs with reduced bandgap and improved quantum confinement.
- Resulting QDs exhibit 4 % color purity (CIE 1520, and extended carrier lifetimes.

2609.26845.title: Analytical Solution of the Nonlinear Boltzmann Equation For Multicomponent Systems
2609.26845.summary:
- Exact analytical solutions of the nonlinear relativistic Boltzmann equation for homogeneous, isotropic massless multicomponent systems with anisotropic scattering.
- For two-component systems, three solution classes: equilibrium, a hybrid Maxwell‑Jüttner plus nontrivial distribution, and shared nontrivial dynamics.
- The hybrid Maxwell‑Jüttner structure and shared nontrivial dynamics are unprecedented in kinetic theory and relativistic contexts.

2609.26869.title: Easy-plane anisotropy of magnetic fluctuations in UTe2
2609.26869.summary:
- INS shows AFM spin fluctuations at Y are isotropic in the ac‑plane but vanish along b, disproving Ising anisotropy.
- Results favor a d‑vector along b, excluding AFM exchange as the triplet pairing glue.
- A tight‑binding model with itinerant and localized 5f moments reproduces the overdamped excitations via FM intra‑dimer interactions and Landau damping.

2609.26871.title: Experimental Characterization of the Passive Mechanical Behavior of Rat Pelvic Floor Muscles: Effects of Test Conditions and Pregnancy
2609.26871.summary:
- Rat levator ani passive tensile properties were tested under varying preconditioning, loading rates, and storage; pregnancy did not significantly alter peak strain.
- Preconditioning effects depended on loading rate: at 5 %/s peak strain tapered near 2 % preconditioning, while at 1 %/s no tapering occurred up to 15 %.
- Rat samples displayed larger peak strains and lower high‑strain stiffness compared to digitized human cadaver levator ani data.

2609.26881.title: Fermion bag study of the two-dimensional Majorana-Hubbard model at finite hopping
2609.26881.summary:
- Hamiltonian fermion‑bag QMC removes the sign problem for \(g\lesssim7\) on lattices up to 256 sites.
- Interactions strengthen U(‑charged dimerization, suppress the neutral channel, and restore U(symmetry in the even‑bond component while the odd component remains nematic.
- Results show a gapless Majorana semimetal throughout the sign‑problem‑minimal window.

2609.26916.title: Interlayer-correlated fractional quantum Hall state in a trilayer electron system
2609.26916.summary:
- Detected a ν = 5/7 fractional quantum Hall state in a high‑quality GaAs trilayer quantum well.
- The state matches the predicted Ψ₃₃₃₁₁ wavefunction: 1/3 intralayer and 1 interlayer correlations.
- Establishes a new Halperin‑Laughlin member, extending interlayer coherence to three layers.

2609.26925.title: First Passage in the Presence of Jump Rate Fluctuations: A Transition from Infinite to Finite Mean
2609.26925.summary:
- Symmetric random walk on 1D lattice has divergent mean first‑passage time.
- Introducing stochastic jump‑rate fluctuations can make the mean first‑passage time finite.
- A phase transition occurs: broad rate fluctuations → finite mean; weak fluctuations → infinite mean.

2609.26943.title: Viscous Dissipation Governs Bubble Morphology and Failure in Soft Matter
2609.26943.summary:
- Viscous dissipation suppresses shape instabilities, letting viscoelastic gels sustain large spherical bubbles while elastic gels form ellipsoidal cavities that rupture quickly.
- A modified Rayleigh–Plesset model and finite‑element simulations show that higher Deborah numbers favor elastic growth; lower De favors relaxation and spherical morphology.
- The study establishes viscous dissipation as a key stabilizing mechanism for cavitation in soft matter, impacting tissue damage, ultrasound therapy, and hydrogel characterization.

2609.26957.title: Matrix Density Waves and Fractionally Charged Point Defects in Flavor Weyl Semimetals
2609.26957.summary:
- Matrix density wave in two‑flavor Weyl semimetals forms a traceless adjoint condensate with order‑parameter manifold \((S^2\times S^/\mathbb Z_2\).
- The manifold supports both unit hedgehogs and half‑quantum Alice strings, each generating a full electronic mass gap.
- Hedgehogs bind a single zero mode carrying \(\pm e/2\) charge, while Alice strings host a chiral mode and flip hedgehog winding when braided.

2609.26971.title: Robust Strange Metallicity across Attractive and Repulsive Hubbard Models
2609.26971.summary:
- Both attractive and repulsive 2D Hubbard models (|U|/t = exhibit linear‑T resistivity over a broad temperature range, despite differing low‑energy correlations.
- The linear‑T behavior stems from the U‑even leading term in the conductivity moment expansion and is tied to a Curie‑like compressibility with weakly temperature‑dependent diffusivity.
- Only at low temperatures do the models diverge: the attractive case shows a diffusivity feature linked to pair formation, while the incoherent regime remains largely insensitive to microscopic details.

2609.26991.title: Spin Configurations of Anyonic excitations in Moir\'e Fractional Chern Insulators
2609.26991.summary:
- Finite‑size twisted bilayer MoTe₂ at 1/3 filling forms a spin‑unpolarized fractional Chern insulator coupled to a planar parabolic quantum dot.
- The energy gap is large and weakly dependent on dot‑bilayer separation, supporting low‑energy spin‑unpolarized quasiparticles/quasiholes.
- Charge density shows spin‑unpolarized excitations localize positive charge near the negatively charged QD, unlike spin‑polarized ones.

2609.27132.title: Exact Equivariance from Ordinary Neural Networks for Lattice Many-Body Dynamics
2609.27132.summary:
- MLPs with finite‑group averaging yield exactly equivariant surrogates, decoupling symmetry from the network architecture.
- Accurately predicts Falicov–Kimball hopping energies and Holstein conservative forces, matching exact diagonalization.
- Enables large‑scale simulations that reproduce charge ordering and CDW coarsening in correlated electron systems.

2609.27324.title: Mobility-Gap Robustness and St\v{r}eda-Hall Separation in Disordered Axion Pumping
2609.27324.summary:
- Second Chern number remains quantized up to \(W\approx5\), beyond the global gap closure at \(W_g\approx5\).
- Středa–Hall response falls off after gap closure, serving as a control for mobility‑gap protection versus finite‑size artifacts.
- 3D unitary Anderson transition at each pump slice, with mobility edge at \(\tau=0\) and critical disorder \(W_c\approx18\).

2609.27642.title: Asymmetric magnetoresistance in 3$d$-5$d$ based La$_{0.67}$Ca$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$/SrIrO$_3$ bilayer: The role of unidirectional anisotropy
2609.27642.summary:
- 3 d FM La₀.₆₇Ca₀.₃₃MnO₃ / 5 d HM SrIrO₃ bilayer shows magnetic ordering in SIO at ~42 K, inducing Mn/Ir interfacial coupling.
- Magnetoresistance evolves from negative at high T to positive‑to‑negative crossover as LCMO orders, then becomes asymmetrically positive at low T due to SIO ordering.
- Asymmetric MR attributed to interface‑driven spin‑scattering between itinerant and localized electrons, highlighting tunable interfacial anisotropy.

2609.28418.title: Intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in the surface conduction regime of non-magnetic narrow-gap insulator FeSi
2609.28418.summary:
- Intrinsic anomalous Hall effect appears in FeSi surface conduction below ~55–75 K, showing zero‑field hysteresis without bulk magnetism.
- Surface conductivity scales with roughness and inversely with thickness, confirming metallic surface states (CSS) below T_CSS ≈55–75 K.
- Bulk susceptibility and specific heat reveal no phase transition, indicating emergent magnetic order confined to the surface.

2609.28436.title: Cooperative Domain-Wall Dynamics in a Two-Dimensional Quasiclassical Holstein Model
2609.28436.summary:
- CDW coarsening in a 2‑D Holstein model shows growth exponents between ¼ and ½, driven by a crossover kinetics \(\dot{L}=[D(T)/L][1+L_\times^2(T)/L^2]\).
- At low \(T\), binary occupations force cooperative wall rearrangements, giving \(L(t)\sim t^{1/4}\); thermal broadening allows curvature‑driven motion, restoring \(L(t)\sim t^{1/2}\).
- Fits, rate collapse, and large‑system simulations confirm that microscopic charge conservation generates long‑

2609.28593.title: Boundary and bulk perturbations in vectorial active matter
2609.28593.summary:
- Examines how global anisotropic environments break rotational symmetry in active matter and proposes ways to detect small anisotropies.
- Studies boundary‑induced symmetry breaking in confined polar active fluids, showing walls generate local anisotropies that penetrate far into the bulk.
- Demonstrates that boundary effects markedly alter both bulk and boundary dynamics in finite‑size flocking systems.

2609.28620.title: Competing magnetic and spin vestigial orders from continuum field theory
2609.28620.summary:
- Developed a continuum field theory with independent vector and tensor fields to capture competing antiferromagnetic and spin‑nematic orders.
- RG analysis finds the multicritical fixed point at imaginary coupling, implying a first‑order triple point; a direct paramagnetic‑to‑AFM transition can be continuous, governed by cubic (3D) or Ising (2D) universality.
- The model predicts two‑step transitions with an intermediate spin‑vestigial (nematic) phase, controlled by the tensor mass and dimensionality.

2609.28624.title: Stimulation of superconductivity in $d$-wave superconductors
2609.28624.summary:
- External EM radiation can enhance pairing in disordered \(d\)-wave superconductors via the Eliashberg effect, whereas a clean system shows no enhancement.
- The enhancement is confined to a finite frequency window set by gap, disorder, inelastic scattering, and temperature, with edges governed by quasiparticle redistribution, heating, and pair breaking.
- Unlike \(s\)-wave, the upper frequency threshold is not pinned at \(2\Delta\); it rises above the gap as the critical temperature is approached.

2609.28628.title: Theory of extrinsic contributions to the full orbital current
2609.28628.summary:
- Developed a microscopic theory of extrinsic orbital Hall effect by solving the quantum‑kinetic equation for wave‑vector off‑diagonal density‑matrix elements, incorporating side‑jump and skew‑scattering within the non‑crossing approximation.
- Applied the theory to a massive Dirac cone and a particle‑hole‑asymmetric variant, finding disorder‑generated τ⁰ contributions comparable to the intrinsic current that cannot be isolated by disorder‑strength scaling.
- For the bare Dirac cone, the extrinsic correction cancels the conventional intrinsic value, leaving a total current exactly twice the quantum correction; particle‑hole asymmetry activates conventional skew scattering.

2609.28630.title: Weak-Coupling Pair-Density-Wave from Momentum-Space Nonsymmorphic Symmetry
2609.28630.summary:
- Momentum‑space nonsymmorphic symmetry turns PDW into the leading weak‑coupling instability in a twisted bilayer checkerboard lattice.
- At charge neutrality, attractive interactions give spin‑singlet or spin‑triplet PDW; repulsive interactions favor quantum Hall or finite‑Q density waves.
- Doping preserves PDW dominance via a protected Cooper logarithm; breaking time‑reversal while keeping nonsymmorphic symmetry yields a fully gapped topological spin‑triplet PDW with BdG Chern number

2609.28636.title: Majorana zero modes in half-quantum vortices of pair density wave superconductors
2609.28636.summary:
- Spinless honeycomb model exhibits a PDW phase where half‑quantum vortices bind Majorana zero modes.
- Hartree‑Fock shows PDW relative‑phase stiffness ≈ superfluid stiffness near the PDW–Dirac transition, enabling vortex fractionalization and a field‑driven half‑vortex lattice transition.
- The resulting two‑flavor half‑vortex lattice hosts a Majorana lattice with geometry‑ and flux‑dependent bands, including Dirac nodes and zero‑energy Fermi lines.

2609.28642.title: Interaction induced flattening of optical transition quantum geometry
2609.28642.summary:
- Electron‑hole interactions flatten the quantum geometry of excitons, even when built from extended Bloch states.
- Localized particle‑hole excitations exhibit uniform, flat Hermitian curvature, whereas delocalized ones have non‑vanishing curvature.
- The resulting flat excitonic geometry quenches third‑order circular photoconductivity and ties the Hall response to that of the ground state in non‑magnetic systems.

2609.28643.title: Defect Poisoning of Quantum Spin Ice
2609.28643.summary:
- Dilution as low as 2 % of magnetic vacancies qualitatively changes low‑energy physics of quantum spin ice.
- Vacancy‑induced quantum fluctuations connect percolating spin clusters, dominating over clean‑system dynamics.
- Experimental signatures of quantum spin ice may be obscured by such defects, as shown by large‑scale QMC and exact diagonalization.

2609.28647.title: Compact representation of strongly correlated Green's functions: the MOR+EC way to explore phase space
2609.28647.summary:
- MOR+EC merges eigenvector continuation with model‑order reduction to compute Green’s functions efficiently across parameters and frequencies.
- Achieves ~10⁻⁴ relative error and 16–91× speedup versus exact diagonalization, enabling high‑resolution phase‑space

2609.28655.title: Bayesian Monitoring of a Diffusive Particle in One Dimension
2609.28655.summary:
- Bayesian tracking of a 1‑D diffusing particle with noisy continuous measurements yields a bounded Shannon entropy for constant monitoring, quantified via KPZ exact results.
- When monitoring intensity decays as \(t^{-\alpha}\), entropy grows logarithmically: \(\overline{S(t)}\sim \tfrac12\ln t\) for \(\alpha>1/2\) and \(\overline{S(t)}\sim \alpha\ln t\) for \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
- These regimes are derived through a replica mapping to a time‑dependent Lieb‑Liniger Hamiltonian, confirmed by simulations of discrete polymer models.

2609.28680.title: Altermagnetic Kondo Logic via Floquet Symmetry Conversion
2609.28680.summary:
- Floquet symmetry conversion with an in‑plane AC field exposes hidden altermagnetic spin splitting, creating a local spin‑dependent hybridization channel.
- The resulting Kondo resonance splits with a crystalline form factor identical to the altermagnet, enabling Kondo tomography of the spin texture.
- The Kondo splitting is tunable by field orientation, providing a symmetry‑controlled route to Kondo‑based logic gates.

2609.28738.title: Imaging an obstructed Wannier orbital
2609.28738.summary:
- Phase‑resolved imaging of an obstructed Wannier orbital in an acoustic flat‑band metamaterial, locating its f‑like center in a void between lattice sites.
- Boundary states appear only when the lattice termination severs the orbital, confirming the bulk‑boundary correspondence of obstructed atomic insulators.
- The platform directly probes single‑particle quantum geometry relevant to electronic flat‑band phenomena such as unconventional superconductivity.

2609.28786.title: Plane-Wave Photon-Fock Cavity QED-DFT: Chiral-Cavity-Induced Topology in Graphene
2609.28786.summary:
- Plane‑wave × photon‑Fock framework for the velocity‑gauge Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, enabling first‑principles cavity QED of periodic solids.
- Application to monolayer graphene in linear and chiral cavities yields a polarization‑selective Haldane gap with distinct DOS, real‑space, and circular‑dichroism signatures.
- Brillouin‑zone Berry‑curvature analysis shows a non‑monotonic Chern‑number sequence (1 → 3 → –1 → 1 → 2 → –1 → , confirming chiral‑cavity‑induced topological phases.

2609.29004.title: Exact selection of a toric-code vison crystal in a flux-conditioned Kitaev model
2609.29004.summary:
- Exactly solvable Kitaev extension where conserved ℤ₂ fluxes dictate both signs and connectivity of Majorana hopping.
- At a tuned loop point the matter Hamiltonian fragments into independent Majorana rings, yielding a frustrated Ising term plus a non‑negative residual that selects 2/3‑vison crystal ground states.
- The crystal ground space maps to a sheared square‑lattice toric code, giving fourfold topological degeneracy and demonstrating exact gauge‑matter feedback.

2609.29241.title: Mixed-Valent Magnetism in CeFe$_2$ from Multi-Impurity DFT+DMFT
2609.29241.summary:
- Multi‑impurity DFT+DMFT reproduces Ce and Fe spin/orbital moments and total saturation moment, matching XMCD data.
- Ce 4f occupancy ≈ 85 with variance 27 shows strong valence fluctuations; spectral function contains Fermi‑level weight plus incoherent features.
- Bath‑mediated polarization and configuration mixing are identified as the essential drivers of CeFe₂’s electronic structure and magnetism.

2609.29400.title: Thermal quasi-Devil's staircase in an anisotropic triangular-lattice Rydberg array
2609.29400.summary:
- Realizes a thermal quasi‑Devil’s staircase in finite anisotropic triangular‑lattice Rydberg arrays via Ising‑antiferromagnet mapping.
- Shows winding‑sector crossovers emerge when thermal fluctuations overcome topological barriers, detectable through winding distributions and structure factors.
- Provides experimentally feasible predictions for current Rydberg platforms, linking energy–entropy balance to commensurate–incommensurate transitions.

2609.29728.title: Exact phase diagram of the XXZ Heisenberg chain in a staggered magnetic field
2609.29728.summary:
- Exact analytical relation between exchange anisotropy and staggered field yields a highly degenerate ground‑state manifold with off‑diagonal long‑range order on the phase boundary.
- The boundary separates a ferromagnetic phase from a gapless Luttinger liquid, with a first‑order transition confirmed by DMRG.
- Reducing anisotropy further drives the gapless phase into a gapped quantum‑disordered phase, completing the full phase diagram.

2609.30265.title: Upper critical dimension for dirty Weyl semimetal-to-metal quantum phase transitions
2609.30265.summary:
- Lower and upper critical dimensions for the disorder‑driven Weyl semimetal‑to‑metal transition are \(d_{\ell}=2\) and \(d_{u}=4\).
- Numerical ADOS yields a correlation‑length exponent \(\nu\approx5\) for \(d\ge4\) and a dynamic exponent \(z\approx d/2\) for \(d\ge3\).
- Field‑theoretic RG confirms \(z=d/2\) exactly, enabling analytical treatment near both critical dimensions.

2609.30202.title: Incipient superconductivity and tunable Chern insulators in twisted Bernal bilayer-trilayer graphene
2609.30202.summary:
- Incipient superconductivity emerges from a displacement‑field‑driven trivial insulator at ν = −2, showing a sharp transition and critical current but no zero resistance.
- Chern insulators with |C| ≤ 3 form at integer/fractional moiré fillings for electron doping over 05°–50°, tunable by twist angle and carrier density.
- In‑plane magnetic field expands the superconducting pocket beyond

2609.30162.title: From dimensional reduction to tetramerization in mixed ferro-antiferro breathing pyrochlores
2609.30162.summary:
- Classical Monte Carlo and Gaussian approximation show thermal order‑by‑disorder selects a collinear Type‑I \(X=(1,0,\) state via a strong first‑order transition.
- Pseudofermion FRG and DMRG reveal a nonmagnetic window with nearly ideal tetramer correlations on antiferromagnetic tetrahedra, while the structure factor still peaks at \(X\).
- A third‑order effective Hamiltonian and exact diagonalization confirm that reversing inter‑tetrahedron coupling drives a uniform tetramer selection, matching the high‑temperature expansion of local singlet dynamics.

2609.30142.title: Disorder-induced quantum Fisher information in topological quantum systems
2609.30142.summary:
- Disorder leaves the toric‑code ground state unchanged but boosts the QFI for estimating perturbations when a separable probe evolves under the disordered Hamiltonian.
- In the ordered case, optimal product probes give a transient quartic‑time scaling of QFI, with quadratic and cubic terms vanishing.
- The disorder‑enhanced QFI remains high over a range of perturbation strengths, encoding times, and survives dephasing, bit‑flip, and amplitude‑damping noise.

2609.30124.title: Characterizing quasiparticles in strongly correlated systems using nonlinear spectroscopy in quantum simulators
2609.30124.summary:
- Nonlinear spectroscopy and fluctuation protocols identify quasiparticle charge sign without synthetic gauge fields.
- Second‑order density/current responses and third‑order cumulants distinguish electron‑ vs hole‑like carriers; hole‑doping in a Fermi‑Hubbard ladder reverses the sign, matching Hall coefficient behavior.
- The method applies to hard‑core bosons, where finite‑momentum, finite‑frequency drives reveal carrier sign and are amplified near resonant collective modes.

2609.30101.title: Leg-Tied Tensor Network States: Entanglement Beyond Virtual Bonds
2609.30101.summary:
- LETTA shares physical legs among tensors, directly encoding long‑range correlations while a virtual MPS backbone captures short‑range entanglement.
- Uses a deterministic DMRG‑style variational algorithm with exact contractions over active tie‑boundary sets.
- Outperforms same‑bond‑dimension MPS on 2D J₁–J₂ Heisenberg and 3D transverse‑field Ising models, reaching larger‑MPS accuracy with ~10× fewer parameters.

2609.30066.title: Beyond Bond Gauge: Exact Tensor-Network Tangent Spaces at Weighted Graph States
2609.30066.summary: - Exact tangent‑space characterization for weighted graph state PEPS (q ≥ , with non‑bond gauge variations given by

2609.30025.title: Orientational Ordering of Janus Particle Arrays as Classical Compass Spin Systems
2609.30025.summary:
- Janus particle orientations map to classical compass spins with bond‑dependent interactions, modeled by a 120° compass and Kern–Frenkel potentials.
- Monte Carlo simulations reveal a low‑temperature sixfold ordered phase, a high‑temperature disordered phase, and an intermediate quasi‑long‑range regime with two BKT transitions driven by thermal order‑by‑disorder.
- Adding higher‑order terms alters the emergent anisotropy: a quadratic term reverses the sixfold selection, while a cubic term lifts the degeneracy and selects lattice‑aligned directions observed experimentally.

2609.29472.title: Selective strain tuning of nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics in BiFeO$_\text3$
2609.29472.summary:
- Tensile strain suppresses ultrafast photoinduced reduction of ferroelectric displacement in BiFeO₃.
- Antiferrodistortive oxygen‑octahedra rotation (magnetic order) remains strain‑insensitive.
- Strain acts as a selective control knob for ultrafast multiferroic dynamics.

2609.30284.title: Von Neumann's Two Quantum Entropies
2609.30284.summary:
- Von Neumann introduced two quantum entropies (1927 and to define thermodynamic entropy.
- The 1927 entropy (von Neumann entropy) vanishes for pure states and is best viewed as an entanglement measure.
- The 1929 entropy, nonzero for almost all pure states, should be regarded as the true thermodynamic entropy.

2609.30300.title: The Scale Invariance Behind Boltzmann Counting
2609.30300.summary:
- Exact scale invariance in Boltzmann counting yields specific entropy without asymptotic approximation.
- Resolving Gibbs excess at multinomial level uncovers a state‑dependent scale structure that generates a continuum reference measure.
- For an ideal gas, these scales acquire operational meaning via reversible work, linking combinatorial origins to continuous statistical mechanics.

2609.30311.title: Synchronizing Spectral and Interference Criticalities at an Exceptional Point
2609.30311.summary:
- Loss imbalance in a superconducting double‑dot system drives a Bogoliubov sector to an exceptional point, synchronizing spectral and interference criticalities.
- At the EP, CAR and ECT interference boundaries coalesce, creating a CAR‑dominated window that opens with a square‑root critical law.
- Detuning/retuning controls the synchronization, and the resulting bifurcation is directly observable in nonlocal conductance.

2609.30346.title: What Becomes of the Antiferromagnetic String When Long Range Neel Order Is Lost? Exact Results
2609.30346.summary:
- Loss of long‑range Néel order permits a projective RP² description, yielding half‑vortex defects.
- Half‑vortex pairs are logarithmically confined, V(R)=κ ln(R/r_core) with κ=πρ_s/2, instead of a 1D string.
- Antiferromagnetic confinement survives as a global 2D spin texture, replacing the local path‑dependent string.

2609.30347.title: Loop content of bond percolation on hyperbolic triangulations: an exact identity and a $1/\lambda$ expansion
2609.30347.summary:
- Homology of bond‑percolation clusters on disk patches of regular \(\{3,q\}\) triangulations for \(q=7\)–\(20\).
- Total persistent \(H_1\) per vertex is nearly linear in \(1/\lambda(q)\), where \(\lambda(q)\) is the asymptotic ring‑size ratio.
- Exact identity reduces loop persistence to the minimum‑spanning‑tree weight minus a boundary term; first‑order \(1/\lambda\) expansion yields the closed‑form intercept \(5/4-2\pi/(3\sqrt\) and agrees with measurements.

2609.30363.title: Disentangling the Toric Code
2609.30363.summary:
- Finite‑dimensional ancillae cannot render commuting‑projector Hamiltonians (Ising, toric code) on‑site because fractionalized excitations obstruct it.
- Infinite‑dimensional ancillae (e.g., rotors) enable disentanglement, producing on‑site symmetries for both models.
- The findings align lattice and QFT anomaly analyses, while finite ancillae may lead to non‑invertible on‑site obstructions.

2609.30365.title: Repulsion-Driven $p - i p$ Superconductivity in a Single Valley Revealed by DMRG
2609.30365.summary:
- Repulsion drives spinless chiral \(p\)-wave superconductivity in a single‑valley Dirac system on the Qi‑Wu‑Zhang lattice.
- Pairing starts at low doping on a small, isotropic Fermi pocket, tied to band quantum geometry rather than dispersion details.
- At higher doping a pair‑density‑wave coexists with zero‑momentum pairing, with order‑parameter winding opposite to the parent anomalous Hall state.

2609.30368.title: Is the fractional Chern insulator-superconductor transition in twisted MoTe$_2$ direct?
2609.30368.summary:
- Reassesses transport data near a fractional Chern insulator in twisted MoTe₂, questioning a direct anyon‑superconductor transition.
- Proposes that a reentrant integer quantum Hall effect (RIQHE) intervenes, extending to low displacement fields at very low temperatures.
- A patchwork model reproduces the phase diagram and predicts a split transition with a narrow RIQHE region at low electronic temperatures.

2609.30372.title: Non-vanishing Density of States in Disordered Weyl Semimetals
2609.30372.summary:
- Shows that weak short‑range disorder produces a finite zero‑energy density of states in 3D Weyl semimetals.
- Employs a supersymmetric saddle‑point calculation: instanton is a j = ½ hedgehog, fluctuations give a convergent one‑loop prefactor.
- Derives ρ(=A w⁻⁴ exp(–s*/w²) (A≈5, s*≈which matches numerics over four orders of magnitude.

2609.30380.title: Anyonic molecules through the trion looking glass
2609.30380.summary:
- Anyons bind to electronic trions near defects, forming an anyonic molecule.
- The bound state shows a few‑meV PL red‑shift that scales with the anyon’s fractional charge and kinetic energy.
- Numerical results agree with twisted MoTe₂ experiments, revealing both universal and non‑universal anyon traits.

2609.30381.title: Cooper pair charge Kondo effect in a hybrid quantum dot - superconductor device
2609.30381.summary:
- Four‑dot hybrid device near particle‑hole symmetry shows a charge Kondo effect driven by Cooper‑pair crossed Andreev reflections.
- The two‑channel Kondo physics turns the system into a double Cooper‑pair splitter, spatially separating Cooper pairs from incoming electrons.
- RG analysis predicts non‑Fermi‑liquid signatures and observable fractional conductance over a broad temperature and anisotropy range.

2609.30518.title: Nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate near a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic quantum critical point
2609.30518.summary:
- Zero‑point spin fluctuations alter the nuclear spin‑lattice relaxation rate 1/T₁ near a 2D antiferromagnetic quantum critical point in the self‑consistent renormalization framework.
- For weak mode‑mode coupling (y₁ < 1/T₁ follows thermal‑fluctuation behavior; for strong coupling (y₁ > 1/T₁ shows a local maximum versus temperature.
- The local maximum observed in ⁶³Cu 1/T₁ of lightly doped La

2609.30871.title: Systematic Evolution of Magnetic Anisotropy and Crystal-electric-field Ground States in SmTr2Ge2
2609.30871.summary:
- Magnetic anisotropy shifts from easy ab‑plane (Co, Ni) to easy c‑axis (Cu, Ag).
- CEF ground‑state level crossing occurs between Ni and Cu, with systematic change in first excited level.
- Magnetic properties correlate with local structural parameters, linking ligand environment to Sm 4f states.

2609.31001.title: Multiorbital periodic Anderson model for CeRh2As2
2609.31001.summary: - Built a multiorbital periodic Anderson model for CeRh₂As₂ that includes Γ₇ and Γ₆ 4f doublets, non

2609.31319.title: Criticality enabled long-range order in a U(1)-symmetric spin-1 Heisenberg chain with biquadratic interactions
2609.31319.summary:
- Numerical study of anisotropic spin‑1 Heisenberg chain confirms U(symmetry breaking at critical point.
- Magnetization exponent β≈29 agrees with ε‑expansion β≈28; Luttinger parameter diverges with exponent tied to Nahum transition.
- Finite‑size spectra give dynamical critical exponent z≈2, supporting Nahum’s field‑theory predictions.

2609.31616.title: A Unified Spin-Fermion Framework for Magnetic Diversity in Chromium Monopnictides
2609.31616.summary:
- Chromium monopnictides (CrSb, CrAs, CrP) evolve from altermagnetism → double‑helical AFM → no long‑range order as ligand itinerancy increases with chemical pressure.
- A unified spin‑fermion model shows that Cr\(^{1+}\) \(d^5\) moments coupled to itinerant pnictogen states undergo exchange‑parameter reconstruction across NiAs → MnP structures.
- The resulting magnetic phase diagram explains the contrasting orders via competing Cr–Cr exchanges and proximity to a frustrated regime in CrP.

2609.31618.title: Quantum Representation Selects Neutral Skyrmion Molecules
2609.31618.summary:
- Quantum states on each lattice site select Skyrmion compositions that cancel their sideways gyroscopic force, forming gyroscopically neutral molecules.
- Two SU(magnet models show the neutral composition changes from a pair to a trimer while classical energies stay identical, isolating the quantum‑state effect.
- Mean‑field analysis finds both pair and trimer bound and locally stable; the trimer remains robust to interaction variations and moves with little deformation.

2609.31672.title: From a three-fluid junction to Young's law: Constitutive and rigid-support limits of wetting
2609.31672.summary:
- Links Neumann balance at a three‑fluid junction to Young’s law through a viscoelastic continuum limit.
- Demonstrates that stiffening a solid suppresses displacement yet permits reversible wet‑dry migration, producing Young’s angle while retaining capillary reaction forces.
- Provides two rigorous convergence results (finite‑strain clamped model and quadratic half‑space model) explaining coexistence of local Neumann ridges with distant Young angles.

2609.31707.title: Blockwise friction heterogeneity redistributes stretching in a 2D Gaussian polymer under Batchelor-Kraichnan random flow
2609.31707.summary:
- Friction heterogeneity leaves equilibrium conformation unchanged but changes block mobilities and relaxation spectrum.
- In a Batchelor‑Kraichnan flow, the high‑friction block stretches more than the low‑friction block, with asymmetry increasing with friction contrast.
- Random strain preferentially amplifies the slowest mode, and the effect persists even when global relaxation timescales are matched.

2609.31721.title: Growth and Interface Engineering of Superconducting TiN on Sapphire by Thermal-Laser Epitaxy
2609.31721.summary:
- TLE grows TiN on sapphire up to 1150 °C, boosting superconducting performance.
- High ammonia pressure and temperature create voids at the TiN‑sapphire interface, raising defect density.
- An 850 °C TiN seed layer suppresses voids, achieving Tc = 8 K, RRR = 2, and 19 µΩ cm resistivity.

2609.31730.title: R-transforms for non-Hermitian block random matrices: a spherical integral approach
2609.31730.summary:
- Extends spherical‑integral method to compute $\mathcal{R}$‑transforms for non‑Hermitian matrices with a fixed $K\times K$ block structure.
- Introduces a rank‑$K$ spherical integral yielding a scalar $H$‑transform on $2K\times2K$ overlap matrices and a matrix‑valued $\mathcal{R}$‑transform capturing joint block correlations.
- Uses replica analysis to conjecture a subordination relation for sums of independent block matrices, enabling determination of spectral boundaries for large block‑structured non‑Hermitian ensembles.

2609.31761.title: A Robust "Shrink-and-wrap" Piecewise Construction Transforms 3-Dimensional Mesh Structures into Mechanical Metamaterials
2609.31761.summary:
- Introduces a “shrink‑and‑wrap” transformation that turns any triangular or tetrahedral mesh into a 3‑D mechanical metamaterial with guaranteed negative Poisson ratio.
- Embeds counter‑rotating mechanisms within each simplex, enabling locally programmable stiffness while preserving overall geometry.
- Demonstrated on convex polyhedra, CSG‑designed models, and 3‑D reconstructions from mobile‑phone video, showing scalability to arbitrary complex objects.

2609.31831.title: Emergent low-energy many-body Hilbert spaces in Chern bands
2609.31831.summary:
- Dominant many‑body subspace in Chern bands is density‑dependent and built from conformal Hilbert spaces (CHS).
- Short‑range Coulomb interactions select the smallest CHS, yielding an anyonic description via the many‑body quantum metric.
- Band mixing is strongly suppressed by ideal trace conditions and short‑range interactions, even at strong coupling.

2609.31839.title: Zoology of chiral superconductors in Chern bands
2609.31839.summary:
- Target‑phase optimization uncovers chiral superconductors in a minimal Chern‑band model with screened Coulomb interactions.
- Exact diagonalization finds a rich set of chiral phases (f‑i f, p±i

2609.31846.title: Read-Rezayi fractional Chern insulators in modulated Bernal graphene
2609.31846.summary:
- Realized a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ Read‑Rezayi fractional Chern insulator at $\nu=3/5$ in modulated Bernal bilayer graphene with screened Coulomb interactions.
- Band structure emulates lowest and first Landau levels; at $\nu=1/2$ the ground state corresponds to the Moore‑Read state.
- Employed target‑phase optimization with band‑projected exact diagonalization to efficiently identify non‑Abelian phases in realistic high‑dimensional models.

2609.31860.title: Mechanical Clustering of Cells via the ExtraCellular Matrix
2609.31860.summary:
- Contractile cells form long‑range aligned/densified ECM fiber bands that mechanically couple cells into clusters.
- Finite‑element modeling shows ~10 % cell volume fraction suffices for internal stiffening via stress‑band mediation, far below percolation threshold.
- Percolation of these fiber bands triggers a sharp transition to bulk stiffening, illustrating long‑range cell–cell mechanical communication shapes tissue mechanics.

2609.31872.title: Connecting finite-size scaling and renormalization-group flows in Anderson localization on random graphs
2609.31872.summary:
- Finite‑size scaling of eigenfunction moments and RG flows of multifractal dimensions $D_q$ are connected in the Anderson transition on small‑world random graphs.
- RG flows for $D_q$ with $q<1/2$ confirm a strongly multifractal localized phase, clearly distinct from the localized regime at strong disorder.
- A single beta function for eigenfunction moments collapses data across disorder strengths, supporting single‑parameter scaling and excluding Kosterlitz‑Thouless‑like two‑parameter behavior.

2609.32012.title: Chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetallic state through enhanced correlation in CeGaGe
2609.32012.summary:
- CeGaGe transitions from achiral I4₁md to chiral P4₃ at low T, enabling a chiral Weyl‑Kondo semimetal.
- Anomalous Hall conductivity remains constant below the Kondo temperature (~7 K) and falls sharply above it, tracking Kondo coherence rather than magnetic order.
- First‑principles calculations confirm Kramers‑Weyl and symmetry‑enforced band crossings near the Fermi level in the chiral phase.

2609.32266.title: Symmetry-permuting entanglers for non-invertible symmetry-protected topological phases
2609.32266.summary:
- Symmetry‑permuting finite‑depth local unitary circuits connect 1+1D SPT phases with non‑invertible symmetries.
- The three Rep(D₈) SPT phases, previously disconnected by symmetric entanglers, are linked by such circuits.
- An explicit matrix‑product unitary reproduces the TQFT‑predicted anyon permutation on string order parameters.

2609.32633.title: GEM: An implementation of the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation for simulating interacting quantum systems
2609.32633.summary:
- GEM: open‑source Python package implementing the ghost‑Gutzwiller approximation for equilibrium properties of multi‑orbital lattice models.
- Supports zero‑ and finite‑temperature calculations, symmetry‑broken phases, and integrates with TRIQS for model construction, self‑consistent solving, and observable evaluation.
- Validated against benchmark results, demonstrating computational efficiency relative to more demanding quantum embedding approaches.

2609.32968.title: How Much Do We Understand Ce L3 XANES? Ab Initio Insights into Configuration-Specific Screening at the Multiplet--Continuum Frontier
2609.32968.summary:
- Coupled multiplet–continuum XSpectruplet model links local multiplet dynamics to continuum photoelectron propagation in self‑consistent Kohn–Sham potentials.
- Two Ce⁴⁺ screening states in CeO₂ split by ~3 eV, weighted 63 %/30 %, arise from collective orbital rehybridization, not extra 4f occupancy.
- Ce³⁺ in CePO₄ shows a localized 4f¹ spectator that directly participates in multip

2609.33454.title: Kitaev-Heisenberg model on the square-hexagon-dodecagon lattice
2609.33454.summary:
- Gapped toric‑code phase in the anisotropic Kitaev model on the SHD lattice, with a single Dirac point at the phase boundary; vortex excitations on square, hexagon, and dodecagon plaquettes realize distinct \(e/m\) anyon assignments.
- In the isotropic Kitaev–Heisenberg model, robust toric‑code phases persist near the Kitaev limits, while four collinear magnetic orders emerge, identified via PEPS, ED, and spin‑wave calculations.
- The full phase diagram is mapped by tracking Majorana zero modes and vortex‑bound states, delineating transitions between topological and magnetic phases.

2609.33568.title: Generalized {\eta}-pairing eigenstates in three-component Hubbard models under a transverse field
2609.33568.summary:
- Generalized η‑pairing operator for three‑component Hubbard model under transverse field yields exact eigenstates via restricted spectrum‑generating algebra.
- Eigenstates show off‑diagonal long‑range order; a tensor‑product state realizes quantum many‑body scar dynamics with long‑range magnetic order.
- Three quench protocols are proposed and numerically validated to prepare the scar state.

2609.33777.title: Scaling Theory for Learning Low-Energy Quantum Subspaces
2609.33777.summary:
- Low‑energy subspace can be learned efficiently from nearby sampled states; error scales as \(d^{2(q+}\).
- For gapped local ground states on \(n\) sites, error \(\sim d^2 (n d^^q\); \(nd^2\) is the natural scaling variable, giving sampling cost \(K=O([\log(1/\varepsilon)]^D)\).
- Numerical results on Heisenberg and transverse‑field Ising chains confirm the scaling law and enable finite‑size probes of criticality.

2609.35838.title: Memory-induced optimal switching in a dynamic Ising-Kuramoto model
2609.35838.summary:
- Combines Ising spins and continuous phases in a globally coupled stochastic system with Glauber switching and Ornstein‑Uhlenbeck noise.
- Shows a nonmonotonic synchronization threshold \(K_c\) minimized at an optimal finite switching rate, balancing Glauber response against memory susceptibility.
- Confirms via theory and simulations the appearance of antiphase composite order, mode mixing, and a τ‑dependent shift of the optimal switching rate.

2609.35940.title: Discrete Scale Invariance of Ising Mesons
2609.35940.summary:
- Discrete scale invariance emerges in mesons of a marginal \(1/r^4\) transverse‑field Ising chain via an inverse‑square attraction between dressed domain walls.
- The scale‑anomaly exponent, fixed by spontaneous magnetization and two‑kink threshold curvature, governs meson hierarchy, binding‑energy ratios, and log‑periodic scattering.
- Exact diagonalization and weak‑field analysis confirm coupled energy–size scaling, realizing quantum limit‑cycle physics in a many‑body magnetic system.

2609.35960.title: Advancing Fuzzy-Sphere CFTs: $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Rotation-Resolving Exact Diagonalization, 3D Ising Heavy Primaries, and Quasi-Hole-Space Projection
2609.35960.summary:
- SO(-resolving exact diagonalization for fuzzy-sphere CFTs, cutting costs by hundreds.
- Discovered ~100 3D Ising primaries, including heavy scalars up to Δ≈5 and resolved parity‑odd tension.
- Quasi‑hole projection shrinks Hilbert space for critical points tied to fractional quantum Hall states, linking CFTs with topological order.

2609.35977.title: Topological Band Theory for High-Dimensional Parameter Spaces
2609.35977.summary:
- Extends quantum‑Hall band theory to high‑dimensional flux‑parameter manifolds from genus‑>1 Riemann surfaces and higher‑form gauge couplings.
- Identifies richer topological invariants (first Chern class + higher curvature terms) that yield protected Kubo‑like responses from current correlations.
- Illustrates the framework with hyperbolic band theory on the genus‑two Bolza surface, relevant to recent synthetic‑dimension experiments.

2609.35984.title: Nonreciprocal Chiral Automata
2609.35984.summary:
- Introduces a lattice‑gas cellular automaton with chiral collisions that yields a nonzero odd pressure coefficient.
- Shows that a local parity‑breaking collision acts as an effective magnetic field, converting bulk viscosity into odd pressure.
- Derives general relations between Hall viscosity, odd pressure, and odd torque and their parity‑even counterparts.

2609.36027.title: Spectroscopy of phonon-coupled integer and fractional Chern insulators: emergence of polarons and chirality deficit of graviton mode
2609.36027.summary:
- Phonons dress excitons (CI) and magnetorotons (FCI) into polarons that soften and herald charge‑order transitions.
- Polaron energy minima anticipate the ordering wave vectors of the emergent charge‑ordered phases.
- In FCIs, electron‑phonon coupling boosts opposite‑chirality graviton weight, producing a chirality deficit.

2609.36036.title: Magnetoplasmon molecule
2609.36036.summary:
- Identified a four‑particle excitation (magnetoplasmon molecule) in a 2D electron gas under magnetic field.
- Molecule consists of two electrons and two Fermi holes of opposite spin; one hole participates in plasma oscillations while the other neutralizes charge.
- Studied coupling between the magnetoplasmon molecule and a magnetoexciton condensate.

2609.36041.title: Linking Topological Medium Range Order and Density-Wave Coherence to Metallic Glass Ductility
2609.36041.summary:
- Combined synchrotron G(r) and 4D‑STEM to quantify geometric and topological medium‑range order in Zr‑based metallic glasses.
- G(r) coherence length predicts baseline ductility, while topological motifs (Cu‑rich FCC vs Zr‑rich HCP) modulate mechanical response.
- Increasing Zr suppresses FCC‑like MRO, enlarges coherence volume, and promotes HCP‑like order, enhancing ductility.

2609.36051.title: Excitonic Stripe Order in the Two-Orbital Hubbard-Kanamori Model
2609.36051.summary:
- Excitonic stripe order emerges as a spatially modulated inter‑orbital particle‑hole coherence in the two‑orbital Hubbard‑Kanamori model.
- The sign of Hund’s exchange selects the condensate: ferromagnetic Hund favors triplet excitons, antiferromagnetic Hund stabilizes singlet excitons.
- Doping produces incommensurate excitonic density waves (stripes and spiral triplet textures), while crystal‑field splitting reshapes nesting and can stabilize triplet order even without pair hopping.

2609.36084.title: Measuring trainable degrees of freedom in materials graph neural networks: a random-subspace intrinsic dimension analysis
2609.36084.summary:
- Uses random‑subspace intrinsic‑dimension analysis to measure how many trainable directions GNNs need to reach near‑final accuracy.
- Reveals task‑specific dimensional demands: metallic classification and bulk‑modulus need few subspace dimensions, while band‑gap, formation‑energy, and phonon predictions require more.
- Shows that larger model widths raise absolute dimensional thresholds but keep fractional thresholds stable, and that dataset size mainly impacts band‑gap models.

2609.36258.title: Magnetic properties and Fermi-surface topology of kagome magnet HoV$_6$Sn$_6$
2609.36258.summary:
- HoV₆Sn₆ orders ferromagnetically below ~4 K with strong anisotropy (≈5 μB /Ho along c, ≈7 μB /Ho in‑plane).
- Tunnel‑diode‑oscillator measurements reveal quantum oscillations up to ~9 kT, mapping a multi‑sheet Fermi surface and cyclotron masses.
- Density‑functional calculations show V‑kagome‑derived flat bands, van Hove singularities, Dirac crossings, and a V‑dominated DOS supporting a ferromagnetic ground state.

2609.36353.title: Quantum metric induced nonlinear transport in the hidden loop-current phase of kagome metal RbV$_3$Sb$_5$
2609.36353.summary:
- Third‑order nonlinear transport shows a sharp kink and strong anisotropy in the longitudinal cubic response at ~35 K, with a magnetic‑field‑odd transverse component, signaling a hidden low‑T phase with loop‑current order.
- The quantum‑metric quadrupole directly contributes to the longitudinal third‑order response, revealing time‑reversal symmetry breaking and electronic reconstruction.
- A loop‑current CDW model reproduces the observed angular dependence, demonstrating that higher‑order nonlinear transport can probe subtle symmetry changes via quantum‑metric effects.

2609.36356.title: Artificial versus Natural Atoms: The uncanny capability of the many-body Schr\"odinger equation to produce emergent behavior
2609.36356.summary:
- Review of 25 years of theory and experiments on artificial atoms/molecules forming Wigner molecules.
- Wigner molecules show quenching of energy gaps, rovibational spectra, entanglement, pinning, and provide an alternative to the fractional quantum Hall effect.
- Finite quantum systems promise advances in quantum information, quantum computing, and fundamental many‑body physics.

2609.36706.title: Probing the electronic structure of $\mathrm{UTe}_2$ with ARPES and high-energy spectroscopy
2609.36706.summary:
- ARPES and X‑ray probes show strongly technique‑dependent electronic structure in UTe₂.
- Spectroscopy and DFT+DMFT reveal an intermediate‑valence U 5f ground state with mixed 5f²/5f³ character.
- The combined data provide key benchmarks for connecting the normal‑state electronic structure to its unconventional superconductivity.

2609.36868.title: Quantized Hyperfine Field at an Implanted $\mu^+$ Site in PrPb$_3$: Interplay between Localized $f$ Electrons and an Interstitial Charged Particle
2609.36868.summary:
- μ⁺ spin rotation shows spontaneous precession with harmonic frequencies in PrPb₃, first in f‑electron systems.
- Precession arises from coupling between μ⁺ spin and hyperfine‑enhanced, Ising‑anisotropic ¹⁴¹Pr nuclear spins.
- The μ⁺ suppresses nearest‑neighbor ¹⁴¹Pr spin dynamics, indicating a local alteration of the f‑electron state.

2609.36936.title: Ergodicity in a hole-dopped Anderson spin insulator
2609.36936.summary:
- A single hole in a 1D t‑JXX chain with random magnetic field can thermalize the spin sector at weak disorder, yielding ergodicity and hole delocalization.
- At stronger disorder the hole localizes with a finite length, restoring the Anderson spin insulator.
- Numerical results show a disorder‑controlled transition between these regimes.

2609.38247.title: Accidental accuracy and formal consistency in $GW$+BSE: Exact benchmarks and regime-dependent error cancellation
2609.38247.summary:
- GW+BSE optical gaps appear accurate because an underestimated GW gap cancels an oversized bare‑exchange kernel, despite formal inconsistency.
- Benchmarking the extended Hubbard dimer shows this cancellation is optimal only in the weak‑binding regime; the frozen‑W construction fails at all binding strengths.
- For strongly bound excitons, static kernels break down, indicating the need for beyond‑static‑kernel physics.

2609.38317.title: Hidden Angular Momentum Loop Currents in Symmetric Crystals
2609.38317.summary:
- Loop currents emerge from lattice dynamics, sustained by quantum and thermal fluctuations.
- In a symmetric 2‑D elastic lattice, neighboring plaquettes carry opposite currents while site angular momentum averages to zero.
- Directional elastic interactions in locally symmetry‑lowered environments organize these currents into a compensated, temperature‑persistent pattern.

2609.38365.title: Geometry and Mechanics of Ribbon Gridshells
2609.38365.summary:
- Ribbon gridshells: thin-sheet metamaterial formed by long, narrow ribbons intersecting at prescribed angles.
- Coarse-grained equations derived; solutions classified by ribbon intersection patterns, enabling arbitrary Gaussian curvature design.
- Soft modes exhibit both rigid and anomalously soft behavior, confirmed by experiment and numerics.

2609.38404.title: Energy-Efficient Non-Volatile Photonic Switching via Composition-Engineered Sn-Doped GST
2609.38404.summary:
- Sn alloying (5–10 at.%) cuts amorphization and crystallization energies, lowering programming energy.
- 10 at.% Sn devices endure >1000 cycles with modest extinction‑ratio loss; >10 at.% Sn raises energy due to phase segregation.
- Switching speed unchanged; encapsulation could mitigate PCM migration and void formation.

2609.38451.title: Ab initio calculated diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility of carbonate minerals
2609.38451.summary:
- DFT‑based calculations reproduce calcite’s diamagnetic susceptibility and AMS, validating the method for diamagnetic phases.
- New intrinsic diamagnetic reference values are given for magnesite and dolomite, correcting for magnetic‑impurity contamination.
- Fe²⁺/Mn²⁺ substitution models show paramagnetic anisotropy dominated by orbital magnetisation along the c‑axis, matching experimental trends.

2609.38464.title: Morphodynamics of lipid vesicles under osmotic forcing
2609.38464.summary:
- Osmotic shock induces rapid buckling, wrinkle smoothing, then slow invagination of lipid vesicles, controlled by a single dimensionless parameter Γ.
- Linear stability predicts buckling wavelength and growth rate; buckling time scales as Γ⁻², matching simulations.
- Folding dynamics reverse elastic energy flow, with bending energy released and dissipated by membrane viscosity; folding time scales as Γ⁻²⁄³, confirming the continuum model.

2609.38478.title: Stress-based structure optimization for a range-separated hybrid van der Waals density functional
2609.38478.summary:
- Ported AHBR RSH vdW‑DF to VASP, enabling robust stress‑based unit‑cell optimization for complex matter.
- Validated AHBR‑VASP against AHBR‑QE on non‑covalent interactions, bulk cohesion, and distorted‑rocksalt metal monoxides.
- Applied AHBR‑VASP to predict layer‑stacking motifs in the C₂N covalent‑organic framework, illustrating soft‑matter discovery.

2609.38481.title: Results of Classical and Nonclassical theories of nucleation for ordering transition in barium titanate
2609.38481.summary:
- Compares classical and nonclassical nucleation theories for the ordering transition in BaTiO₃.
- Applies a nonclassical model to the first‑order paraelectric cubic → ferroelectric tetragonal transition.
- Shows that the nonclassical approach captures nucleation behavior in this phase change.

2609.38509.title: Measures of Chaotic Advection in Simulations of Active Nematics
2609.38509.summary:
- Active MT bundles driven by ATP produce +½ defects that braid, generating chaotic advection quantified by topological entropy and Lyapunov exponent.
- Continuum models compared: standard Beris‑Edwards (BE) versus Beris‑Edwards with nematic locking (BENL), which enforces collective rotation constraints.
- BENL reproduces experimental defect dynamics and mixing metrics more accurately, supporting the nematic locking principle.

2609.38520.title: Modeling density variations in two-dimensional microtubule-based active nematics
2609.38520.summary:
- Introduces a density‑explicit model for 2‑D microtubule active nematics, moving beyond constant‑density assumptions.
- Generates simulations that reproduce experimental striation patterns and defect creation/annihilation dynamics.
- Accurately captures behavior in confined geometries, such as circular wells.

2609.38581.title: Theory of criticality-enabled $U(1)$ symmetry breaking in a class of 1+1D systems
2609.38581.summary:
- Shows spontaneous U(symmetry breaking at 1+1D Lifshitz critical points via two periodic scalars with Berry‑phase coupling.
- Finds U(‑charged vertex \(e^{i\beta\theta}\) orders long‑range while conjugate \(e^{i\beta\phi}\) decays stretched‑exponentially (\(\propto|x|^{2/3}\)).
- Confirms predictions with large‑N theory, analytic \(z\neq1\) criterion, and DMRG on an itinerant‑fermion chain, revealing long‑range U(

2609.38740.title: Sign problem and criticality in world-line quantum Monte Carlo methods
2609.38740.summary:
- World‑line QMC exhibits a sign problem for free fermions, tied to non‑analytic behavior of a hard‑core boson reference model.
- The sign’s temperature/size dependence reflects the 2D Kosterlitz–Thouless transition of the boson system.
- Phase‑transition information remains encoded in the sign statistics even when direct sign sampling becomes impractical.

2609.38848.title: Quantum quenches of scar states in the Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki model via Clifford augmented tensor network simulation
2609.38848.summary:
- Clifford‑augmented MPS efficiently captures highly magical AKLT ground and scar states (high stabiliser Rényi entropy, low entanglement).
- TDVP evolution shows string order in scar states decays after a quench to the Heisenberg Hamiltonian, with faster decay for larger bimagnon number.
- The decay illustrates that symmetry‑preserving quenches can strongly affect topological string order even within the same Haldane phase.

2609.38973.title: Eigenstate thermalization at the edge of the many-body spectrum
2609.38973.summary:
- Incompatible local \(\mathbb{Z}_2\) symmetries create exponentially large degeneracies yet preserve non‑integrability.
- Extensive conserved quantities that are mutually incompatible do not destroy ETH.
- ETH survives deep into the many‑body spectrum, enabling thermalization even near the ground state.

2609.39175.title: Tunability of the structural and magnetic transition in kagome material: PrIr$_3$B$_2$
2609.39175.summary:
- Temperature and pressure drive a monoclinic ↔ hexagonal structural transition, fully monoclinic at 280 K or 2 GPa.
- Monoclinic lattice anomalies at ~250 K and ~110 K correlate with a second MIM transition and resistivity crossover, hinting at charge‑ordered partial Fermi‑surface gapping.
- Antiferromagnetic ordering at 10 K opens a persistent superzone gap, underscoring robust magnetic and electronic order in the kagome lattice.

2609.39258.title: Multipartite entanglement hidden in vector-chiral correlations of spin-1/2 chains
2609.39258.summary:
- Established a bound on nearest‑neighbour vector chirality: QFI per spin ≤ k + 1 for k‑producible states, certifying entanglement depth.
- Showed multipartite entanglement in J₁–J₂ XXZ spin‑½ chains using iDMRG and thermal pure quantum methods at zero and finite temperatures.
- Suggested detection via spin‑current coupling to electric polarization, enabling dielectric loss spectroscopy to probe vector‑chiral entanglement.

2609.39303.title: Varying A-site radius and size disorder to tune magnetic ordering in compositionally complex perovskite oxides
2609.39303.summary:
- Synthesized single‑phase AM₇O₃ (12 cations) that ferrimagnetically orders 89–115 K.
- Transition temperature varies with A‑site radius, size disorder, and valence electrons.
- Demonstrates compositional tuning of magnetic ordering in complex perovskite oxides.

2609.39404.title: Chiral quantum chaos around exponentially many zero modes in the quantum breakdown model
2609.39404.summary:
- Zero‑dimensional, all‑to‑all quantum breakdown model shows Z₄ periodicity in fermion number, mirroring SYK symmetry classes.
- Hosts exponentially many many‑body zero modes protected by a chiral index across all five chiral symmetry classes.
- Spectral gap scaling and hard‑edge statistics reveal symmetry‑enriched quantum chaos.

2609.39417.title: Qantum Well Resonant Tunneling Diode Probe of Correlated States in Twisted Bilayer MoS$_2$
2609.39417.summary:
- Developed a quantum‑well resonant tunneling diode (QWRTD) to probe electronic states in ≈57° twisted bilayer MoS₂.
- Detected a robust integer insulating state at ν = 1 across all displacement fields, and a displacement‑field‑induced fractional insulating state at ν = 3/4 for D < –75 mV/nm.
- Temperature and magnetic‑field studies indicate the ν = 3/4 state is a generalized Wigner crystal, with similar correlated states observed in a device at ≈5°.

2609.39418.title: Weyl superconductivity from Feshbach resonance in the three-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model
2609.39418.summary:
- 3D Fermi‑Hubbard model superconductivity driven by near‑resonant dopant bound states via a Feshbach‑type mechanism.
- Strong‑coupling pairing yields a time‑reversal symmetry‑breaking \(d_{x^2-y^2}+i d_{z^2}\) order parameter.
- The superconducting phase hosts gapless Weyl points and a calculable critical temperature.

2610.00100.title: Transferable Graph Neural Network Surrogates for Molecular Dynamics Across Crystal Symmetries
2610.00100.summary:
- Single GNN surrogate predicts atomic displacements for MD across FCC Al, BCC Fe, HCP Mg without forces or integration.
- Achieves sub‑Ångström accuracy (~10⁻⁴ Å²) and stable nanosecond‑scale autoregressive propagation.
- Reproduces thermodynamic and structural features (RDF, MSD, coordination shells) without symmetry‑specific tuning.

2610.00110.title: Emergence of electronic modes and triplet pairing from spin-1 antiferromagnetic insulators in the Kanamori-Hubbard model
2610.00110.summary:
- Doping and temperature generate new electronic modes inside the gap of spin‑1 antiferromagnetic insulators in the two‑orbital Kanamori‑Hubbard model.
- These modes exhibit momentum‑shifted spin‑mode dispersions; doping‑induced modes differ between orbitals, whereas temperature‑induced modes follow the low‑energy spin mode.
- With weak inter‑orbital repulsion, doping induces onsite spin‑triplet pairing that opens a pair‑breaking gap, while temperature‑induced modes persist.

2610.00124.title: Loading history and window geometry bound compact-state slip ranking during granular shear startup
2610.00124.summary:
- Compact neural score of stress, pressure, coordination, non‑affine motion, and force‑network metrics ranks near‑slip windows better than prevalence but weaker than loading‑history (elapsed strain) alone.
- Recovery‑aware analysis keeps 4 % of activity‑gated events, favoring longer preceding intervals, yet remains compatible with a geometry‑null model.
- No distinct short‑horizon precursor emerges beyond loading history; compact observables provide temporally aligned slip information but are bounded by loading‑history and window‑geometry effects.

2610.00152.title: Quasi-static loading of granular media as a linear complementarity problem
2610.00152.summary:
- Casts quasi‑static granular response as a linear complementarity problem to handle friction‑induced incremental nonlinearity.
- Derives the LCP including particle curvature, frictional contact stiffness, and displacement constraints.
- Identifies eight pathologies (bifurcations and instabilities), including a newly reported continuous‑bounded bifurcation.

2610.00192.title: Migration Flows: Population Scaling and Heavy Tails
2610.00192.summary:
- Migration between counties explains population scaling of mean intercity flows and heavy‑tailed net‑flow distributions.
- Density‑dependent departure/arrival activities make mean flows scale with origin/destination populations; county‑pair net flows are Gaussian with SD ∝ mean.
- Averaging over a correlation distribution yields an intermediate power law with a Gaussian cutoff, and a stochastic model generates the required variance distribution.

2610.00273.title: Tunable flat bands and their signatures in electronic specific heat of an Aharonov-Bohm triangular quantum network
2610.00273.summary:
- Analytical condition for a momentum‑independent flat band in a triangular AB‑flux quantum network.
- AB flux tunes the flat‑band energy position via interference and hopping asymmetry.
- Flat‑band signature appears as a distinct feature in electronic specific heat, linking thermal response to band flatness.

2610.00324.title: Causality violations in cluster GW+DMFT: Exact Lehmann moments and the necessity of non-local vertex corrections
2610.00324.summary:
- GW self‑energies exhibit causality violations; GW+DMFT, though incorporating exact local self‑energies, still fails to enforce causality.
- The two‑site dimer hides the violation due to symmetry, while a frustrated three‑site ring exposes explicit Matsubara‑causality violations in both GW and GW+DMFT.
- Exact Lehmann moments show that the high‑frequency tail requires non‑local irreducible vertex corrections; the local‑only truncation in GW+DMFT leaves non‑local RPA resonances uncorrected.

2610.00326.title: Interior contacts in a narrow quantum Hall bar: a two-dimensional self-consistent screening calculation of the current distribution
2610.00326.summary:
- 2D self‑consistent Thomas‑Fermi‑Poisson calculation of density, filling factor, and current in a 3 µm GaAs/AlGaAs Hall bar with interior contacts.
- Three regimes for interior contacts across the ν = 2 plateau: galvanically connected (compressible bulk), floating (Hall potential of incompressible bulk), isolated (closed incompressible rings).
- Two‑terminal resistance between interior contacts rises sharply in floating/isolated regimes; isolation interval ends before the low‑field edge of the plateau and is set by the disappearance of the incompressible bulk.

2610.00336.title: From Quantized Hall Plateaus to Topological Surfaces: Quantum Capacitance as a Unifying Probe
2610.00336.summary:
- Quantum capacitance directly probes the density of states of topological boundary modes, linking quantum Hall plateaus and Dirac surface states.
- Self‑consistent screening splits the bulk into compressible/incompressible regions, yet plateaus stay quantised.
- Local capacitance shows the bulk is field‑dependent and non‑uniform, challenging the assumption of a uniformly gapped bulk.

2610.00351.title: Thermodynamic origins of multimode spinodal decomposition in multicomponent alloys
2610.00351.summary:
- Multicomponent alloys typically decompose in one pseudobinary mode because unlike elements mix, limiting unstable composition directions.
- Balanced repulsive triangles and attractive–repulsive pairs can produce two comparable downhill directions, yielding locally varied solid solutions instead of distinct blocks.
- A phase‑specific screen found Cu‑In‑Ir‑Ti as a candidate with nearly balanced modes, illustrating a design route for microstructures via spinodal decomposition.

2610.00452.title: Anyon Proliferation and Anyon Superconductivity in Higgsing Transitions via Conformal Embeddings
2610.00452.summary:
- Higgsing via conformal embeddings reduces the gauge group yet preserves or enlarges topological order, enabling anyon proliferation.
- In the \(SO(N)_2 \hookrightarrow SU(N)_1\) family (\(N\ge3\)), phases share the same intrinsic order but differ in global \(U(\) realization; odd \(N\) yields a non‑Abelian transition from a fermionic \(1/N\) Laughlin state to a charge‑\(2e\) anyon superconductor with the same \(\mathbb{Z}_N\) topological order.

2610.00534.title: Near-infrared magnetic linear and non-reciprocal directional dichroism in the chiral antiferromagnet SmFe3(BO3)4
2610.00534.summary:
- Near‑infrared magnetic linear dichroism appears below T_N and is tunable by rotating the AFM easy‑plane order with a magnetic field.
- Non‑reciprocal directional dichroism is observed for 4f–4f transitions in a toroidal geometry, revealing strong electric‑magnetic dipole interference.
- These optical anisotropies provide a route to image and time‑resolve the in‑plane AFM orientation in rare‑earth ferroborates.

2610.00626.title: Mechanism of Incommensurate Magnetic Order in $\mathrm{BaCo_2(AsO_4)_2}$: Interplay of Frustrated Further-Neighbor Exchanges and Bond-Directional Anisotropy
2610.00626.summary:
- Incommensurate spiral stabilized by J₂, J₃ frustration plus Γ, Γ′ anisotropies, without a dominant Kitaev term.
- Extended J₁–K–Γ–Γ′–J₂–J₃ XXZ model, parameters from ab initio, phase diagram mapped with Luttinger‑Tisza and exact diagonalization.
- Quantum order‑by‑disorder favors an out‑of‑plane FMₓ phase competing with the spiral, underscoring quantum fluctuation effects.

2610.00681.title: The half-filled optical Su-Schrieffer-Heeger-Hubbard model with uniaxial strain
2610.00681.summary:
- Strain‐induced anisotropic hopping reduces BOW degeneracy from four to two patterns.
- Phase diagram mapped in e‑ph vs Hubbard U space; critical temperature for BOW order identified.
- Directional gap opening in BOW phase revealed via analytic continuation of the spectral function.

2610.00810.title: Local geometry of the Fermi surface and its effect on the electronic characteristics of normal metals
2610.00810.summary:
- Fine Fermi‑surface features (nearly cylindrical/paraboloidal strips, local flattenings) can strongly modify galvanomagnetic responses.
- The resulting effects are highly sensitive to the propagation direction of high‑frequency disturbances and to the orientation of an external magnetic field.
- Experimental observation of these direction‑dependent phenomena is feasible in both conventional and layered metallic systems.

2610.01337.title: Robustness of the Verwey transition against remanent strain-induced defects in magnetite
2610.01337.summary:
- Uniaxial compression of stoichiometric magnetite generates line‑like defects and remanent strain fields.
- Despite this structural disorder, the Verwey transition temperature and its sharpness are unchanged.
- Dark‑field X‑ray microscopy and AC magnetic susceptibility confirm the transition’s robustness to strain‑induced defects.

2610.01371.title: Na$_2$Ir$^\text{IV}$Cl$_6$: The Missing Member of the Perfectly Cubic Vacancy Ordered $A_2$IrCl$_6$ Family, Another Potential $J_{eff}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ Ground State Candidate
2610.01371.summary:
- First synthesis of anhydrous Na₂IrCl₆ single crystals with a perfectly cubic fcc structure.
- Shows antiferromagnetic ordering at 91 K and remains water‑free and thermally stable up to 453 K.
- Offers a new platform to explore a potential J_eff = ½ ground state, contrasting with earlier monoclinic Na₂IrCl₆.

2610.01551.title: Room-temperature Magnetoelastic Coupling in UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$
2610.01551.summary:
- Giant magnetoelastic coupling near room temperature in UIr₄Al₁₅, seen as lattice‑parameter and bond‑distance anomalies at the magnetic transition.
- Structural distortions occur without symmetry breaking, directly linking magnetic alignment to subtle changes in atomic spacing and local bonding.
- Provides a rare bulk intermetallic platform where magnetism and lattice are strongly intertwined, enabling magnetically responsive quantum materials and sensing applications.

2610.02167.title: Polynomial-time classical and quantum simulation of quantum impurity models
2610.02167.summary:
- Classical algorithms run in polynomial time to estimate ground‑state energy and partition function of quantum impurity models.
- Complexity improved from quasipolynomial to polynomial for static properties.
- Dynamical properties (nonequilibrium Green’s functions) are classically hard but efficiently computable on a quantum computer, capturing full quantum computational power.

2610.02097.title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
2610.02097.summary:
- Z₂ toric code: any locality‑preserving Clifford realizing EM duality cannot be order‑two.
- Z_N toric code: order‑two Clifford exists only for odd N; impossible for even N.
- Shows emergent duality group law need not lift to a microscopic Clifford, via unavoidable string crossings.

2610.02075.title: Universal Bound and Phase Transition in Many-Body Fermionic Non-Gaussianity
2610.02075.summary:
- Derived universal upper bound and Haar mean of magic Rényi entropy, showing typical Haar‑random states reach maximal density \(\ln(4/\) per Majorana in the large‑system limit.
