- Showed that MRE can differ extensively between states with identical covariance matrices, revealing non‑Gaussianity beyond covariance.
- Identified a first‑order transition in MRE density during imaginary/real‑time evolution under the SYK Hamiltonian, marked by a kink and permutation‑symmetry breaking, absent in the thermal free energy.

2610.02006.title: Magnetic Phase Diagrams and Spin Hamiltonian of Monoclinic $α$-RuCl$_3$ from Angle-Dependent Torque Studies
2610.02006.summary:
- Monoclinic α‑RuCl₃ (≤100 µm) shows a 14 K magnetic transition, higher than the 7 K zigzag order in rhombohedral samples.
- Torque magnetometry up to 16 T uncovers anisotropic phase diagrams with reduced symmetry and larger critical fields.
- Field‑induced phases differ from rhombohedral counterparts, implying distinct spin‑Hamiltonian parameters.

2610.01990.title: Frustration-induced multiferroicity in hauerite MnS2
2610.01990.summary: - Below 48 K MnS₂ develops collinear AFM order, doubles the unit cell, breaks inversion symmetry, and shows up to 360 µC/m² ferroelectric polarization (type

2610.01860.title: Approximation theorems for fermionic Gaussian states
2610.01860.summary:
- Quantitative monogamy of two‑point correlations in fermionic Gaussian states via Majorana covariance matrices.
- Product‑state approximations for ground‑state and finite‑temperature energies on high‑degree graphs with error \(O(D^{-1/2})\).
- Finite Gaussian de Finetti theorem (\(O(k/n)\) trace‑norm closeness) and \(O(r^{-1})\) decay of conditional mutual information, yielding \(O(r^{-1/2})\) trace‑norm recoverability.

2610.01714.title: Complex magnetic phase diagrams in Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$
2610.01714.summary:
- Tb₂IrAl₄Ge₂ orders antiferromagnetically at 25 K, showing field‑induced metamagnetic transitions and nonlinear Hall effect.
- Er₂IrAl₄Ge₂ undergoes three zero‑field transitions and hosts multiple low‑field, competing magnetic phases.
- Both Ir‑based compounds expand the Ln₂MAl₄Ge₂ family, revealing diverse magnetic behavior in the Tb₂NiAl₄Ge₂‑type structure.

2610.01600.title: Why polar excitons stay sharp: parity protection of the center-of-mass recoil channel in exciton-phonon scattering
2610.01600.summary:
- Fröhlich coupling generates a universal COM‑recoil channel at \(q_*=\sqrt{2M_{\rm ex}\hbar\omega_{\rm LO}}/\hbar\) that yields a \(1s\to1s\) absorption rate ∝ \(N_{\rm LO}(T)\).
- The recoil linewidth scales as \(\gamma_{\rm LO}^{\rm recoil}\propto\mathcal{F}_{1s,1s}(q_*)^2\) and vanishes for mass‑symmetric excitons (η≈due to destructive electron–hole interference, explaining the sharp perovskite exciton lines.
- The observed 27

2610.01594.title: Mass-asymmetry-controlled exciton dressing and dissociation in a quantum lattice model
2610.01594.summary:
- Equal‑mass excitons are protected from phonon dressing by an exchange selection rule, preventing polaronic cloud formation.
- Increasing mass asymmetry breaks this rule, inducing a strong local polaronic dressing and an internal dressing crossover.
- The dissociation boundary is set by the global balance of Coulomb binding and polaronic stabilization, largely independent of dressing, and the symmetry that blocks dressing also drives dissociation at strong coupling.

2610.02234.title: Spectral Crossings Diagnose Multiply Quantized Vortex Splitting
2610.02234.summary:
- Spectral zero‑energy crossings in a two‑component Haldane sphere reveal whether a charge‑\(r\) vortex is fused or split into \(r\) unit zeros.
- The critical detuning scales as \(|\tau_c|\sim N^{-(r+}\) for a fused vortex and \(\sim N^{-2}\) for resolved unit zeros, confirmed by Feshbach reduction and numerics for \(r=1,2,3\).
- When a partially split cluster’s diameter \(d\) reaches the magnetic length \(\ell_B\), the scaling crosses over, enabling spectroscopic inference of \(d\) below imaging resolution.

2610.02239.title: Reply to "Comment on 'Topography of Fermi arcs in t-PtBi2 using high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy'"
2610.02239.summary:
- Confirmed Fermi arcs in t‑PtBi₂ are disconnected segments crossing EF only between Weyl points, with a finite band gap elsewhere.
- Found no superconducting gap down to 3 K; the Comment’s claim stems from misidentifying arc locations and using unsuitable interpolated data.
- Results agree with STM showing surface superconductivity only below 3 K, the temperature at which ARPES data were taken.

2610.02326.title: Fluctuation-induced magnetoresistance in graphene Hall bars at charge neutrality
2610.02326.summary:
- Quantitative theory of fluctuation‑induced positive magnetoresistance in graphene Hall bars at charge neutrality.
- Analytic MR expressions depend on Hall‑bar geometry, orientation, and momentum‑relaxation effects.
- Thermal‑fluctuation coupling of charge transport and hydrodynamic flow boosts conductivity, producing strong MR at weak fields.

2610.02346.title: Traveling waves, phase separation and pattern formation in the active stepping stone model
2610.02346.summary:
- Minimal run‑and‑tumble active stepping stone model couples migration with birth–death dynamics.
- Hydrodynamic equations show activity increases invasion wave speed, yet excessive activity breaks wave coherence.
- In two dimensions, activity triggers dynamic clustering and pattern formation governed by migration rules.

2610.02380.title: Thickness-Controlled Ferroelectric-to-Ionic Transport in CuCrP2S6 at Room Temperature
2610.02380.summary:
- <40 nm CCPS flakes retain reversible ferroelectric switching; >40 nm flakes lose FE and show Cu⁺‑driven ionic conduction and memristive switching.
- Thickness dictates the competition between ferroelectricity and ionic transport, while light boosts ionic mobility and couples photo‑ and ferroelectric responses.
- The work maps distinct thickness regimes, revealing tunable multifunctional electronic, photonic, and neuromorphic behavior in a single vdW material.

2610.02400.title: Chiral Vacuum Engineering of Quantum Hall Matter
2610.02400.summary:
- Chiral cavity splits co‑rotating modes (vacuum Rabi splitting, bare ground state) from counter‑rotating modes (crossing, energy shifts, two‑mode squeezed ground state) via SU(/SU(1,symmetry.
- Predicts chirality‑dependent Hall resistivity corrections and asymmetric Shubnikov–de Haas oscillations, absent in achiral cavities.
- Proposes detecting the squeezed ground state through current‑fluctuation measurements, feasible with recent terahertz chiral cavity parameters.

2610.02409.title: Projective symmetry group classification of fermionic $Z_2$ spin liquids on the dipolar-octupolar pyrochlore magnets
2610.02409.summary:
- Constructed and classified 48 fermionic Z₂ spin‑liquid PSGs on the dipolar‑octupolar pyrochlore lattice.
- Identified symmetry‑allowed mean‑field ansätze yielding gapless or flat‑band spinon spectra distinct from spin‑½ and bosonic cases.
- Computed spinon bands, specific heat, and dynamical structure factor; near‑linear Cₚ(T) and broad continua match experimental gapless fractionalized thermodynamics.

2610.02411.title: Distinguishing sodium-ion penetration and sustained transport in realistic hard carbon nanostructures
2610.02411.summary:
- Higher carbon density reduces pore accessibility, lowering Na⁺ uptake while charging persists.
- Na⁺ remains partially solvated and increasingly coordinated to the carbon framework under applied potential.
- Open HC‑C1 structures enable deeper, sustained Na⁺ displacement; denser carbons show only transient deep penetration before returning to the interface.

2610.02422.title: Highly Tunable Photon-Magnon Coupling Governed by Collective-Mode Profiles in Reconfigurable Dielectric-Resonator Arrays
2610.02422.summary:
- Site‑selective magnon–photon coupling achieved with reconfigurable dielectric resonator arrays on a microstrip line.
- Coupling strength governed by the local photon field amplitude; modes with a field node at the YIG sphere show no splitting.
- Coupled‑mode model and full‑wave simulations predict position‑dependent coupling, enabling post‑fabrication control for hybrid quantum architectures.

2610.02426.title: Breakdown of material-time scaling in the microscopic dynamics of metallic glasses
2610.02426.summary:
- Diffraction peak shifts follow material‑time scaling via the Tool‑Narayanaswamy‑Moynihan model.
- Microscopic autocorrelations violate material‑time scaling, exhibiting compressed‑exponential decay even for ±4 K jumps.
- Transient stress‑mediated volumetric frustration drives the compressed dynamics, disappearing upon equilibration.

2610.02635.title: Fractionalization-Induced Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking at Continuous Superconducting Transitions in Low-Symmetry Kondo Lattices
2610.02635.summary:
- Projective time‑reversal on Kondo fields (squared to –forbids a TR‑invariant condensate, enforcing twofold degeneracy of critical modes.
- The resulting continuous transition simultaneously breaks U((superconductivity) and time‑reversal symmetry, even with only one‑dimensional crystal irreps.
- An anisotropic Kondo‑Kitaev model illustrates the mechanism, yielding co‑existing superconductivity, TR breaking, and mirror‑symmetry breaking.

2610.03145.title: Correlated Metals, Metamagnetism, and Orbital Nematic Order in moir\'e Materials with Neural Quantum States
2610.03145.summary:
- Neural‑quantum‑state VMC maps the ν = 2 continuum model on a triangular lattice, revealing a phase diagram versus potential strength and Zeeman field.
- Strong correlations eliminate the expected band insulator, producing a first‑order metal–insulator transition whose critical potential depends on spin polarization.
- Unpolarized electrons form an s‑wave molecular insulator, while fully polarized electrons form an orbital‑nematic molecular crystal, generating metamagnetic jumps and multicritical points.

2610.03513.title: Melting phase diagram of the two-dimensional electron solid in a perpendicular magnetic field
2610.03513.summary:
- Measured thermal melting phase diagram of a 2D electron solid in SiGe/Si/SiGe quantum wells via double‑threshold V‑I onset density.
- Found that a perpendicular magnetic field raises the onset density (maximal at low T) and increases the melting temperature, in line with theory.
- Detected a plateau in melting temperature versus electron density at fixed field, hinting at resonance modes in crystallites.

2610.03569.title: Consistent perturbation expansions in screened interactions
2610.03569.summary:
- Introduces exact perturbation expansions in screened Coulomb interactions up to second order.
- Emphasizes a consistent expansion around the Kohn‑Sham system for improved accuracy.
- Demonstrates superior energy and spectral results on the symmetric Hubbard dimer across correlation regimes.

2610.03610.title: Decohering Kitaev's Sixteenfold Way: A Holographic Approach
2610.03610.summary:
- Uses a 3D Walker‑Wang holographic construction to analyze anyon decoherence in 2D topological orders.
- Conjectures a three‑step mapping (lift → transition → trace out bulk) that yields the mixed‑state density matrix after decoherence.
- Finds that decohering the fermion in all 16 Kitaev phases produces a mixed topological order, with the 3D bulk becoming the fermionic toric code.

2610.03678.title: Finite-momentum pairing and magnetic halos in a spin-imbalanced Holstein model
2610.03678.summary:
- Holstein model’s retarded attraction suppresses the sign problem, allowing unbiased QMC of spin‑imbalanced systems at low temperatures.
- Magnetization drives a crossover from zero‑momentum to finite‑momentum (FFLO) pairing, evidenced by oscillating pair correlations and a susceptibility peak at non‑zero Q.
- At high density (n≈FFLO coexists with short‑range checkerboard CDW and long‑range staggered spin “magnetic halos,” providing clear experimental signatures.

2610.02312.title: Counterdiabatic Quantum Circuits
2610.02312.summary:
- Presents a Hamiltonian‑free theory for adiabatic gauge potentials (AGP) of parameter‑dependent unitary operators.
- Computes exact/regularized AGP via a Hermitian banded linear system, avoiding diagonalization or matrix logarithms, with rapid Krylov convergence.
- Extends counterdiabatic shortcuts and AGP diagnostics to Floquet systems and quantum circuits, demonstrated on the kicked top and integrable brickwork circuits.

2610.03186.title: Topological phase transition in a symmetric blockade structure
2610.03186.summary:
- iDMRG on a cylinder maps the full phase diagram of a blockade Hamiltonian with local ℤ₂ symmetry.
- A single continuous transition separates a topologically ordered phase from a trivial paramagnet, stable up to Rabi drives ≈ the system’s energy scale.
- The charge gap remains open across the transition, while the symmetric sector gap closes, signaling flux condensation and charge confinement in the trivial phase.

2610.03730.title: Uniform meandric systems as percolation on planar maps: conjectures and a numerical study
2610.03730.summary:
- Numerical analysis of uniform meandric systems via random walk encoding, viewed as critical percolation on random planar maps.
- Strong negative association found between opposite open crossings; conjectures on asymptotic box‑crossing behavior.
- Introduces a law‑preserving peak/valley flip dynamics, showing percolation decorrelates faster than the underlying map.

2610.03766.title: Magnon chiral damping beyond the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction
2610.03766.summary:
- Antisymmetric Gilbert damping alone generates magnon chiral damping, independent of Dzyaloshinskii‑Moriya interactions.
- Effective damping becomes wave‑vector dependent: scalar part ∝ k², antisymmetric part ∝ k, reproducing experimental nonreciprocity.
- In two‑sublattice magnets, cross‑sublattice antisymmetric damping yields nonreciprocal magnon relaxation without DM.

2610.03767.title: Efficient, Geometry-only Prediction of Advection-dominated Particle Transport through Saturated Soils
2610.03767.summary:
- Introduced minD‑PNM, a pore‑network model that predicts microplastic breakthrough curves using only μCT pore geometry.
- Uses a \(t^{-3}\) transit‑time distribution and minimum‑dissipation partitioning to propagate transport through the network.
- Benchmarked against lattice‑Boltzmann/immersed‑boundary simulations and quartz‑sediment column experiments, achieving good agreement.

2610.03768.title: From Dirac surface response to Casimir forces in Bumblebee-CFJ electrodynamics
2610.03768.summary:
- Casimir force between planar massive Dirac sheets and a Lorentz‑violating Bumblebee–CFJ vector sector is computed with Lifshitz scattering using the one‑loop polarization tensor.
- Repulsion originates from CFJ‑induced TE/TM mode mixing and spatial dispersion, not from Hall conductivity; the surface response stays parity‑even.
- Increasing Dirac mass weakens the force and changes its long‑range scaling, while the CFJ parameter tunes attractive–repulsive transitions.

2610.03773.title: Tactile Perception through Fluid-Solid Interaction
2610.03773.summary:
- Fluid‑filled elastomeric channel transduces touch via pressure changes at two external sensors, enabling electronics‑free tactile sensing.
- Machine‑learning pipeline (feature extraction, soft clustering, neuro‑fuzzy inference) decodes position and force from pressure patterns.
- Demonstrated 1‑D and 2‑D touch localization, robust to underwater or magnetic‑interference environments.

2610.03774.title: Soap Films Amplify the Air-Water Interface but Neither Produce Detectable H2O2 Nor Enhance Reduction of Gold Ions
2610.03774.summary:
- Soap films fail to produce detectable H₂O₂ even after 300 cycles.
- Soap films do not enhance Au³⁺ reduction; gold nanoparticles form spontaneously in bulk.
- H₂O₂ generation and Au nanoparticle formation are linked to bulk HAuCl₄ chemistry, not to the air‑water interface.

2610.03778.title: Harnessing Measurement Error as a Thermodynamic Resource in Two-Reservoir Information Engines
2610.03778.summary:
- TRIEs with a two‑level system show monotonic work, efficiency, and fluctuation dependence on measurement error governed by demon control parameters.
- Conditions identified that allow useful work at any error level and simultaneous optimization of performance metrics.
- When the demon’s energy cost comes solely from the cold reservoir, the efficiency can exceed the Carnot bound, and a dual‑Otto cycle TRIE with a trapped \(^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^+\) ion is proposed.

2610.03782.title: Predicting and extending the bubble-free operating limit of capillary-fed water electrolysis
2610.03782.summary:
- Bubble-free limit in capillary-fed electrolyzers is set by separator pore size, balancing nucleation supersaturation and electrolyte permeability.
- Reducing pore size from 8 µm to 2 µm raises bubble onset from 18 to 73 A cm⁻² and cuts cell voltage by 11 V at 1 A cm⁻².
- Below ~45 µm pores, electrolyte replenishment limits performance, causing drying before bubble formation.

2610.03790.title: Information Entropy and Dissipation Potential in Stochastic Nambu Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
2610.03790.summary:
- Links the Nambu dissipation potential \(S_{\mathrm{NB}}\) to information entropy in stochastic Nambu nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
- Shows that, with an Einstein‑type relation, the stationary Fokker–Planck distribution is exponential in \(S_{\mathrm{NB}}\), making it the quasipotential of the steady state.
- Distinguishes \(S_{\mathrm{NB}}\) from Shannon entropy, introduces a Massieu‑type interpretation, a Nambu canonical distribution, and derives fluctuation covariances via a saddle‑point approximation.

2610.03813.title: Surface scalar plasmons on curved interfaces: a venue for analogue gravity
2610.03813.summary:
- Derived a massive Klein–Gordon equation for scalar surface plasmons on curved interfaces, revealing a geometric potential.
- Showed that specific curvature can cancel the effective mass, allowing massless SSP propagation.
- Applied the formalism to an analogue black hole, computing quasinormal mode frequencies and highlighting curvature‑controlled plasmon transport.

2610.03884.title: The ALPS project release 3.0: open source software for strongly correlated systems
2610.03884.summary:
- Release 0 of ALPS: open‑source libraries and applications for simulating strongly correlated quantum lattice models.
- New distribution channels (pip, Spack), GitHub CI, MIT license, revamped docs and Jupyter‑notebook tutorials.
- Modernized C++17 codebase with Boost/NumPy 0 compatibility and major updates to DMFT/DMRG solvers.

2610.03993.title: ToF-PAX-RIXS: A Time-of-Flight Spectrometer for combined ARPES and RIXS
2610.03993.summary:
- Combines time‑of‑flight ARPES and PAX‑RIXS in a single multimode electron‑optical column for sequential, identical‑condition measurements.
- Uses a thin metallic converter to transform scattered soft X‑rays into photoelectrons, preserving energy and momentum transfer information.
- Benchmarked at the Cu L₃ edge on CaCuO₂, reproducing conventional RIXS spectra with effective energy resolution after deconvolution.

2610.04290.title: Magneto-transport and electronic structure studies of ternary antimonides, La$T$Sb$_2$ ($T$ = Cu, Ag)
2610.04290.summary:
- Both LaCuSb₂ and LaAgSb₂ display positive dρ/dT, linear MR, and non‑Fermi‑liquid behavior (2–30 K).
- LaAgSb₂ exhibits a CDW, causing low‑T core‑level broadening and necessitating multi‑band transport.
- DFT+U+SOC reproduces valence bands, shows inequivalent Sb sites, and links Sb square nets to the CDW.

2610.04331.title: State-selective entanglement and point-gap topology in the unidirectional Bose-Hubbard chain
2610.04331.summary:
- Repulsive interactions suppress skin accumulation in the unidirectional Bose–Hubbard chain, driving a superfluid–Mott transition in the ground state.
- The ground state becomes uniformly filled with decreasing entanglement, whereas the steady state (largest‑imaginary‑energy eigenstate) shows a nonmonotonic entanglement crossover with four spatial maxima tied to competing doublon–holon sectors.
- Even at strong interaction the many‑body winding about the origin stays nonzero; projected doublon–holon manifolds reproduce the entropy profile, but the winding becomes ill‑defined as \(U/t\to\infty\).

2610.04654.title: Determining the j-Specific Unoccupied 5f Electronic Structure in Actinides
2610.04654.summary:
- HERFD XAS at M4,5 edges gives j‑specific unoccupied 5f DOS in actinides.
- Empirical comparison shows HERFD XAS ≈ j‑resolved BIS (IPES).
- Directly measures separate 5f5/2 and 5f7/2 unoccupied states.

2610.04663.title: Does a pole in the self-energy imply a violation of the Luttinger theorem?
2610.04663.summary:
- Luttinger theorem can remain valid even when the self‑energy has a pole.
- A model with two gapped bands plus a narrow residual Fermi‑liquid band (small residue Z) yields a Green’s function with two zeros and three poles.
- In Model I (bandwidth renormalized by Z) the Luttinger–Ward analysis holds for any Z > 0; in Model II it requires Z to exceed a density‑dependent critical value.

2610.04704.title: Peeling off Abelian Anyons and Proliferation Transitions
2610.04704.summary:
- An invertible one‑form global symmetry in (2+d TQFT “peels off” all Abelian anyons.
- The peeled anyons are described by U(Chern‑Simons gauge fields coupled to a scalar, forming a transition field theory.
- This theory exhibits a phase transition from the original TQFT to either a gapless phase or another TQFT, with detailed symmetry fate.

2610.04958.title: Floquet dressing of bulk metallic bands in 2H-NbSe2
2610.04958.summary:
- Floquet‑dressed replicas of bulk metallic bands in 2H‑NbSe₂ observed with time‑resolved ARPES, preserving parent‑band dispersion.
- Polarization‑dependent redistribution of replica weight explained by coherent Floquet–Volkov interference, not simple hybridization.
- Demonstrates control of itinerant bulk states in a multiband metal without relying on hybridization gaps, enabling manipulation of metallic transport and collective order.

2610.05175.title: Unveiling High-Energy Ultrafast Responses Driven by Fermi-Level Gap Opening in Charge-Density Waves
2610.05175.summary:
- Ultrafast pump–probe shows CDW gap in EuAl4 collapses under optical excitation.
- Gap shrinkage renormalizes interband transitions at the gap edge, yielding large transient reflectivity at high probe energies.
- Links low‑energy order‑parameter dynamics to high‑energy spectral responses in gapped quantum materials.

2610.05395.title: Complete Entanglement Structure of the Kitaev Honeycomb Spin Liquid from Exact Tensor Networks
2610.05395.summary:
- Exact 2‑D tensor‑network construction of all Kitaev honeycomb eigenstates via sequential quantum‑number and Gutzwiller projections (local MPS, \(D=2\)).
- Ground and excited states share bond dimension but differ in Schmidt spectra: area‑law vs volume‑law entanglement, with topological entropy appearing only after Gutzwiller projection.
- Projection collapses wavefunctions into a single gauge sector, demonstrating that excited states are also topologically ordered and extending the approach to other \(\mathbb{Z}_2\) spin liquids.

2610.06912.title: Correlated Low-Energy Model of Monolayer 1H-NbS$_2$: A cRPA+DMFT Study
2610.06912.summary:
- Single‑band Nb‑\(d_{z^2}\) model reproduces ARPES/STS features, including the Van Hove singularity.
- cRPA gives \(U_{\text{cRPA}}=138\) eV; DFT+DMFT captures strong correlations and spectral weight redistribution, outperforming static DFT+U.
- The minimal model reproduces spectral broadening seen in more elaborate multi‑orbital and electron‑phonon treatments, validating the downfolded approach.

2610.06915.title: Disorder into Correlation: A Microscopic Mechanism for Sub-McIntyre Avalanche Noise
2610.06915.summary:
- Polar‑optical‑phonon emission confined to a forward cone competes with alloy scattering, limiting carrier cooling.
- Reduced phonon cooling narrows the ionization path beyond dead space, synchronizing ionizations into a dynamic staircase.
- Explains sub‑McIntyre avalanche noise in Sb alloys and HgCdTe, making alloy disorder a tunable design parameter.

2610.06943.title: Time-Reversal Selection Rule for Twist Disorder
2610.06943.summary:
- Time‑reversal selection rule: twist harmonics that are frame rotations cancel backscattering; those that change coupling scatter.
- Zero‑set theorem gives universal thickness laws for electrons/phonons, set by band‑edge symmetry; random twist rescale but keep the same scaling order.
- Unprotected axes yield a transparent energy with heavy‑tailed disorder and an \(N^{-3}\) conductance decay; black‑phosphorus films demonstrate symmetry filtering, keeping ~100× more electron than hole conductance at 64 layers.

2610.06946.title: Interplay between spinodal decomposition and wetting in ternary to quinary mixtures
2610.06946.summary:
- 2D Cahn–Hilliard simulations of N = 3–5 component mixtures show surface‑directed spinodal decomposition around a filler particle.
- Wetting versus non‑wetting interfacial tensions generate lattice, droplet, and target (core‑shell) morphologies that later coarsen via curvature‑driven depletion.
- Coarsening slows with more components, but wetting accelerates it, illustrating how particle–component interactions control microstructural evolution.

2610.06951.title: $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry as Effective Time Reversal Symmetry for Anderson Localization in a Collinear Antiferromagnet
2610.06951.summary:
- PT symmetry acts as the effective time‑reversal symmetry for Anderson localization in BaMn₂Bi₂, even though ordinary TR symmetry is broken by antiferromagnetic order.
- Magnetoconductance follows standard TR‑breaking laws, but the degree of symmetry breaking is modulated by magnetocrystalline anisotropy that stabilizes PT‑related sublattices.
- Transverse magnetic fields strongly suppress localization by canting PT sublattices, whereas longitudinal fields have only a minor effect, highlighting the robustness governed by exchange and magnetocrystalline interactions.

2610.06985.title: CrystalJev: thinking fast and slow with atomistic foundation models for materials discovery
2610.06985.summary:
- CrystalJev performs a single frozen‑potential query per unrelaxed structure, outputting calibrated probabilities and finite‑sample guarantees instead of full relaxations.
- Across 65 Matbench Discovery models, a “stable” call is a probability derived from model errors and candidate population, matching relaxation accuracy at ~1/30th the cost.
- A value‑of‑information rule sends expensive relaxations only when predictions can change, and prospective tests show single‑pass forecasts overestimate stability by ≤1 % on unseen candidates.

2610.07007.title: Identifying Plastic Inorganic Semiconductors Requires More Rigorous Criteria
2610.07007.summary:
- GeSe tolerates ~23 % strain under macroscopic compression perpendicular to layers, yet fractures brittlely when bent along the c‑axis armchair direction.
- Conventional micropillar compression causes brittle fragmentation, whereas eccentric loading introduces shear that activates interlayer sliding and accommodates deformation.
- The study demonstrates that single‑direction or single‑scale tests are insufficient; a systematic, multi‑direction, multi‑scale evaluation framework is required to reliably identify plastic inorganic semiconductors.

2610.07013.title: A numerical and efficient model for thermo-field electron emission calculations
2610.07013.summary:
- Introduces GETELEC‑3, a fast open‑source solver for the 1D time‑independent Schrödinger equation that replaces Fowler‑Nordheim/Murphy‑Good approximations.
- Employs the Numerov algorithm (≤1 % uncertainty) and a parallel kernel to compute current density in milliseconds; a neural‑network residual model achieves <4 % error at even lower cost.
- Supports arbitrary potentials and density of states for metals and semiconductors, with a user‑friendly interface and compiled executable.

2610.07050.title: Spontaneous Motion Generates Reversible Nonreciprocity in an Achiral Active Elastic Ring
2610.07050.summary:
- Spontaneous rotation of an achiral active elastic ring creates mechanical nonreciprocity through off‑center elastic forces that couple deformation to propulsion.
- Reversing the rotation flips the antisymmetric response; a control scheme can preserve directionality while suppressing the near‑Hopf resonance.
- Near the Hopf threshold, the nonreciprocal response diverges inversely with distance to onset, giving rise to a self‑sustained traveling deformation above threshold.

2610.07113.title: Direct-Write Chemical Vapor Deposition
2610.07113.summary:
- 10 µm glass micro‑nozzle enables direct‑write CVD, producing 500 nm Al lines with 30 µm linewidth on TiN/Si in UHV.
- Continuous single‑pass, maskless growth allows systematic variation of deposition conditions on a single substrate.
- Transport model couples Knudsen emission and surface diffusion to quantify precursor diffusion length (L_d), which shrinks from 4 µm to 2 µm as temperature increases.

2610.07146.title: Heavy-fermion hybridization waves from Dirac spinons near a Kondo-breakdown quantum phase transition
2610.07146.summary:
- Hybridization waves emerge in frustrated Kondo lattices near a Kondo‑breakdown quantum phase transition, where local moments form a Dirac spin liquid.
- The wave vector \(\vec{Q}\) connects Dirac spinon nodes to low‑energy electronic states, setting the spatial periodicity.
- The wave amplitude is governed by a kinematic condition between electronic and spinon band structures, explaining observed spatially modulated screening.

2610.07156.title: Chiral Parafermions in Floquet $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Topological Order
2610.07156.summary:
- Realizes $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Floquet topological order in a driven Kitaev honeycomb model, yielding emergent constrained parafermions coupled to conserved $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields.
- Generates chiral parafermionic Floquet edge modes, whose propagation, fractional quantum‑information transport, and exchange statistics are quantified via correlation functions and the chiral unitary index.
- Shows dynamical anyon transmutation in the bulk with a non‑equilibrium loop order

2610.07158.title: Local-moment magnets on all close-packed lattices are equivalent
2610.07158.summary:
- Hidden symmetry links classical Heisenberg, XY, and Ising magnets on all close‑packed lattices when only nearest‑ and next‑nearest‑neighbour couplings (J₁, J₂) are present.
- The symmetry guarantees identical ground‑state energies and projected momenta for every close‑packed lattice, yielding a unified phase diagram.
- Fluctuations break this symmetry, so order‑by‑disorder effects can differ among close‑packed structures.

2610.07291.title: Odd-parity magnon spin polarization from chiral four-spin exchange in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
2610.07291.summary:
- Chiral four‑spin exchange creates a momentum‑dependent magnon spin in a honeycomb antiferromagnet at zero field.
- For a Néel vector tilted by θ₀, the exchange yields intersublattice magnon pairing (∝ cos θ₀ sin² θ₀); biaxial anisotropy mixes longitudinal sectors, producing odd‑in‑momentum, nonquantized mode spins while keeping magnon energies reciprocal.
- A temperature gradient induces spin density along the Néel axis; reversing the four‑spin coupling flips the spin

2610.07915.title: Two-exciton bound states in the Merrifield exciton model
2610.07915.summary:
- Exact solution of two‑exciton states in a finite Merrifield chain via Bloch states and plane‑wave ansatz, giving closed‑form energies and wavefunctions.
- Demonstrated that at most two bound‑state types exist (above or below the scattering continuum) and mapped their parameter regimes across the Brillouin zone.
- Offers quantitative benchmarks for exciton dynamics and optical responses in molecular aggregates.

2610.08266.title: Gradual Localization of Itinerant Cobalt 3d Electrons in the Pyrochlore Ferromagnetic Metal LuInCo4
2610.08266.summary:
- Powder neutron diffraction reveals a q = 0 collinear ferromagnetic structure with a 9 µB Co moment.
- Single‑crystal data exclude antiferromagnetic or helical order; diffuse q = 0 scattering broadens as temperature decreases.
- Low‑temperature metamagnetism is attributed to a ferromagnetic instability enhanced by gradual localization of itinerant Co‑3d electrons.

2610.08304.title: Symmetry protected quantum many body scars through half-gauging
2610.08304.summary:
- Studies quantum many‑body scars in stochastic‑matrix‑form Hamiltonians with symmetry defect insertion.
- Determines when scars survive defect insertion and shows half‑gauging creates symmetry‑protected scarred interfaces.
- Concludes that half‑gauged scarred systems are robust and generalizable to higher dimensions.

2610.08309.title: Exchange self-energy and vertex corrections to static screening in the two-dimensional electron gas
2610.08309.summary:
- Analytically derived leading beyond‑ring corrections (exchange self‑energy and vertex) to the static polarizability of a 2D electron gas.
- Individual divergent terms cancel, yielding a finite result that reproduces the Hartree‑Fock compressibility and renormalizes the Thomas‑Fermi wave vector.
- Exchange converts the one‑sided 2D Kohn kink into a sharp two‑sided peak, boosting Friedel oscillations 2–3× over RPA and affecting Kohn‑Luttinger pairing.

2610.08874.title: Thermal Diffusivity in Metallic Nanowire Aerogels
2610.08874.summary:
- Ag/Cu nanowire aerogels (20–500 mg cm⁻³) exhibit lower thermal diffusivity for 30 nm wires than 60 nm, due to surface scattering.
- Compaction densifies the aerogel yet reduces diffusivity ~300×, driven mainly by the thickness term rather than transport coefficient changes.
- Densification preserves the percolative network, showing aerogels cannot be treated as homogeneous bulk materials.

2610.08907.title: Zero Mode Operators and Charge-Conjugation Defects in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall-Superconductor Heterostructures
2610.08907.summary:
- Developed a bulk‑to‑boundary mapping that turns bulk Wilson operators into localized zero‑mode operators for non‑Abelian FQH‑SC heterostructures.
- Revealed a generalized zero‑mode algebra that separates zero‑mode anyons from local operators, showing tunneling probes bulk monodromy while direct anyon transfer probes \(G\)-crossed associativity.
- Applied the framework to recover \(\mathbb{Z}_{2m}\) parafermions in Laughlin states, \(\mathbb{Z}_2^{(n

2610.08921.title: Exact solutions for kinematics across interaction-deformed Fermi surfaces
2610.08921.summary:
- Exact rates of change for occupation deficit inside and surplus outside the interacting Fermi surface are derived when interactions are tuned at fixed density.
- These rates equal the weight swept by the deforming surface plus the change of Luttinger’s integrand at fixed momentum; the surface term difference equals the flux of incoherent weight \(1-Z_{\vec k}\).
- The resulting identities hold with or without Luttinger’s theorem, offering precise kinematic relations for interaction‑deformed Fermi surfaces.

2610.08924.title: Superconducting edge contact to a buried Ge quantum well
2610.08924.summary:
- Edge‑contact method combining anisotropic dry etch and wet etch accesses buried Ge quantum wells.
- Josephson junctions show near‑unity transparency; QPCs exhibit Andreev plateau ≈ 4e²/h.
- Quantized supercurrent in superconducting QPCs confirms high‑quality hybrid integration.

2610.08934.title: Remote magnon sensing detects the universal phase stiffness jump in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$
2610.08934.summary:
- Contactless, all‑optical detection of superconducting phase stiffness using propagating antiferromagnetic magnons in CrSBr.
- Magnon group velocity rises below Tc, quantitatively encoding Meissner‑screened phase stiffness and revealing the universal BKT phase‑stiffness jump in underdoped Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊δ under parallel field.
- Establishes magnons as local probes of superconducting electrodynamics and 2D phase‑ordering physics in bulk cuprates.

2610.08942.title: Matter wave bistability with a momentum chirped Bose-Einstein condensate
2610.08942.summary:
- Momentum‑chirped BECs cancel interaction‑induced resonance shifts, yielding sharp, multi‑valued Fabry‑Perot transmission spectra.
- Interaction‑assisted tunneling and bistability arise in a quasi‑1D BEC cavity of two Gaussian barriers, with an analytically optimized chirp.
- The effect enables matter‑wave switching and high‑precision velocity sensing, with sensitivity estimates provided.

2610.08955.title: From continuum neural quantum states to effective lattice models: Fluctuating Wigner molecules in moir\'e superlattices
2610.08955.summary:
- Maps continuum neural quantum states to site‑resolved charge and spin statistics, revealing emergent effective degrees of freedom.
- Discovers a low‑spin ground state at ν = 3 in moiré TMDs, with triangular Wigner molecules, strong doublon–hole charge fluctuations, and spin‑singlet cores.
- Motivates a spinful two‑orbital Hubbard model to capture intertwined charge and antiferromagnetic spin correlations.

2610.08957.title: Probing magnetic interactions in real space via magnetic pair distribution function analysis
2610.08957.summary:
- mPDF probes short‑range magnetic correlations, enabling extraction of exchange interactions in paramagnets.
- A mean‑field model with Onsager reaction field is used to fit mPDF data and determine exchange parameters.
- The method reproduces literature exchange values for several tested materials.

2610.08958.title: Phase diagram of a semiflexible magnetic polymer in three dimensions
2610.08958.summary:
- Coupled conformational, stiffness, and two‑state spin degrees of freedom in a semiflexible magnetic polymer on an FCC lattice.
- Zero‑field phase diagram: first‑order coil‑to‑globule/ferromagnetic collapse at low stiffness, globule‑to‑crystal transition at lower T, and direct coil‑to‑crystal transition at high stiffness.
- Monte Carlo and variational free‑energy analysis shows how bending rigidity and magnetic interactions reorganize polymer phases, linking flexible magnetic polymers to semiflexible homopolymers.

2610.08984.title: Valley transitions during spin shuttling in Si/SiGe heterostructures
2610.08984.summary:
- Valley excitations threaten coherent spin shuttling; modeled as a two‑level valley system in a mobile quantum dot.
- Three regimes found; at ~tens of m/s the ground‑state valley is preserved, enabling distance‑independent coherent shuttling.
- Partial Landau‑Zener strategy proposed, yielding higher valley‑shuttling fidelity than the standard Landau‑Zener approach.

2610.09036.title: Ambipolar metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe2
2610.09036.summary:
- Contact‑free RF reflectometry measures sheet resistance in bilayer MoSe₂, revealing both electron and hole metal‑insulator transitions.
- Critical densities differ fourfold yet share similar Coulomb‑to‑kinetic energy ratios, matching solid‑liquid coexistence seen by STM.
- Magnetoresistance peaks at each transition, indicating a field‑driven Pomeranchuk‑like expansion of the Wigner solid against the correlated liquid.

2610.09210.title: Multiorbital Anisotropy and Magnetic Excitations in Trilayer Nickelate Pr$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$
2610.09210.summary:
- XAS/RIXS resolve planar vs out‑of‑plane Ni–O hybridization in Pr₄Ni₃O₁₀.
- Dispersive magnetic excitations soften at the incommensurate SDW wave vector.
- Spin‑wave analysis shows strong intra‑trilayer exchange comparable to in‑plane couplings, largely independent of rare‑earth substitution.

2610.09345.title: Polarized neutron diffraction with ex-situ $^3$He neutron spin filter and two-dimensional detector for noncollinear incommensurate magnetic order
2610.09345.summary:
- Developed a ³He neutron spin filter combined with a 2‑D detector to capture polarized scattering outside the horizontal plane.
- Created a data‑reduction scheme that maps 2‑D intensity maps to 3‑D reciprocal‑space distributions while correcting for imperfect ³He polarization.
- Applied the method to Mn₃WO₆, successfully observing polarization‑dependent intensities of its out‑of‑plane incommensurate magnetic order.

2610.09453.title: Inhomogeneous cluster DMFT study on p-n junction Mott gap closing in Hubbard lattice
2610.09453.summary:
- Mott gap closes when the potential drop ≈ 35 t (U = 8 t), matching the 2×2 plaquette excitation energy.
- Drop direction barely changes the threshold; diagonal orientation yields a stronger zero‑energy coherent peak because of preserved orbital degeneracy.
- Inhomogeneous 2×2 plaquette DMFT shows the metallic phase dominates over the Mott insulator under comparable electric‑field strengths, aligning with experimental gap‑closing data.

2610.09656.title: Unified treatment of local dynamical interactions in correlated metals using Eliashberg theory
2610.09656.summary:
- Unified GW and Fan‑Migdal self‑energies into a single effective interaction, producing Eliashberg equations from the Hedin‑Baym framework.
- Solved local dynamical equations to obtain temperature‑dependent quasiparticle spectra, emphasizing the low‑energy transport window.
- Applied to Sr₂RuO₄: band renormalization agrees with experiment and DMFT, but low‑energy linewidth and resistivity are underestimated in the bubble approximation.

2610.10027.title: Efficient Optimization of Tensor Rings with Low-Rank Environments
2610.10027.summary:
- Two‑site Ring‑DMRG reduces local operations to \(O(p\chi^\) by compressing long environments to low‑rank form.
- Robustness achieved via gauge transformations, a generalized Davidson solver, and SVD‑based truncation when the environment is separable (alternating optimization otherwise).
- For critical systems, the needed environment rank \(p\) stays bounded with system size, giving tensor rings an advantage over tensor trains in the thermodynamic limit.

2610.10030.title: Fourth-order perturbation theory for the Frohlich polaron: Analytic structure of the weak-coupling series and the crossover to strong coupling
2610.10030.summary:
- Fourth‑order Rayleigh–Schrödinger series for 3D Frohlich polaron ground‑state energy and effective mass computed; third‑ and fourth‑order mass coefficients are new.
- Series converges with radius ≈ 5; ratio/Pade analysis reveals a power‑law singularity (exponent ≈ marking the weak‑to‑strong coupling crossover.

2610.10555.title: Magnetic localization and spectral asymmetry of a charged particle at a screw dislocation
2610.10555.summary:
- Radial dynamics combine an inverse‑square term from the screw‑modified conserved quantity \(\mathcal{J}=\ell-\beta k\) with a magnetic harmonic confinement.
- For \(q\mathcal{B}_0\neq0\) the spectrum is exactly solvable: equally spaced levels with an orientation‑dependent shift; opposite \(\mathcal{J}\) values share spatial profiles but different energies.

2610.10645.title: Axiomatic Incompatibility Between Thermal Equilibrium and Volume-Dependent Entropy in Ideal Gas Theory
2610.10645.summary:
- Volume‑dependent entropy for an ideal gas contradicts the thermal equilibrium axiom in reversible isothermal processes.
- The paper shows entropy must depend only on temperature, introducing a “pseudo‑isothermal” process (small adiabatic + isochoric steps) to recover classical work and heat relations.
- The corrected entropy matches Maxwell’s kinetic theory but differs from the Planck–Boltzmann microstate count, indicating a fundamental split between thermodynamic and statistical entropies.

2610.10647.title: Efficiency fluctuations in quantum heat engines with non-quasi-static adiabatic strokes
2610.10647.summary:
- Analyzed efficiency fluctuations in quantum Carnot and Otto engines with pistons executing non‑quasi‑static adiabatic strokes at constant speed, alongside quasi‑static isothermal/isochoric steps.
- Modeled pistons as single quantum particles in a 1‑D box; two‑point measurements capture stochastic work from unitary evolution during non‑equilibrium strokes.
- Demonstrated that piston speed introduces additional quantum fluctuations, modifying the average efficiency of both engine types.

2610.10668.title: Theory of Topologically Ordered Superfluids in 2+1 Dimensions
2610.10668.summary:
- Introduces topologically ordered superfluids (TOSFs) that support gapped anyons while remaining gapless via Goldstone modes.
- Shows a duality: gauging U(_c maps a TOSF to a gapped topological order with U(_dual symmetry and zero Hall conductance; gauging U(_dual recovers the TOSF.
- Provides algebraic and field‑theoretic tools, including parton constructions, to classify TOSFs and realize non‑Abelian vortex excitations.

2610.10679.title: SC$^\sharp$: superconductivity intertwined with topological order
2610.10679.summary:
- Introduces SC$^\sharp$ as a class of (2+D gapped superconductors whose elementary vortices are intrinsically non‑Abelian and cannot be factorized into invertible superconductor vortices plus bulk anyons.
- Proves no‑go results: elementary vortex quantum dimension ≥ √6, ruling out Fibonacci fusion, and constructs infinite families via systematic anyon condensation.
- Defines primitive SC$^\sharp$ phases that cannot arise by disordering lower‑charge condensates, revealing new intertwined topological order.

2610.10682.title: Spin Chain with Continuous Exponential Symmetry: Topological Phase and Beyond
2610.10682.summary:
- 1D spin‑S chains with a continuous exponential symmetry \(U(\rtimes\mathbb Z_2\) where the U(charge unit decays as \(q^{L-j}\).
- Integer \(S\): odd \(q\) supports a nontrivial \(\mathbb Z_2\) Haldane‑type SPT with protected edge modes; even \(q\) yields only trivial phases.
- Half‑odd‑integer \(S\): odd \(q\) forbids a unique symmetric gapped ground state (Lieb–Schultz–Mattis), while even \(q\) produces a novel “half‑SPT” phase with a single‑edge

2610.10706.title: Symmetric Mode Ansatz: Theory of Magnon Collective Modes in Chern Insulators
2610.10706.summary:
- Introduces the symmetric mode ansatz (SyMA) to analytically describe magnon spectra in Chern insulators, matching numerical results at integer and fractional fillings.
- Proves SyMA exactness in specific Hubbard models (Haldane, ideal continuum) and derives magnon‑gap bounds from Chern number, Berry curvature, and quantum metric.
- Shows uniform quantum geometry stabilizes Ising ferromagnetism and gapped magnons in moiré Chern insulators such as twisted MoTe₂.

2610.10709.title: Beyond Dry Flocking: Shape-Dependent Hydrodynamic Alignment
2610.10709.summary:
- Shape‑dependent hydrodynamic coupling of Marangoni swimmers drives flocking beyond dry‑matter assumptions.
- Triangular paper boats exhibit disorder‑to‑order and re‑entrant order‑to‑disorder transitions with camphor concentration and density.
- A reaction‑diffusion model of camphor fields reproduces the transitions, highlighting surface‑tension‑gradient propulsion.

2610.10710.title: Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal
2610.10710.summary:
- Explored Cooper pairing driven by collective modes in a magnetic Wigner crystal of rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.
- Showed that broken time‑reversal symmetry removes the Cooper logarithm, so a finite attraction threshold is needed for pairing.
- Hartree–Fock/TDHF calculations reveal that phonon‑mediated attraction can exceed this threshold, yielding bound electron pairs.

2610.10764.title: Gauging Modulated Symmetries: Bond Algebras, Higher-Form Symmetries, and Symmetry-Enriched Topological Order
2610.10764.summary:
- Constructive framework for modulated symmetries in lattice systems, using finite-dimensional representations of space group acting on finite Abelian internal symmetry.
- Kernel construction yields symmetry-allowed local interactions and an algebra of open operators; gauging maps these to extended Wilson/boundary operators preserving algebraic relations.
- In deconfined phase, the algebra realizes a mixed ’t Hooft anomaly, enabling microscopic realization of Abelian crystalline symmetry‑enriched topological phases with preserved electric‑magnetic braiding.

2610.11126.title: Probing and Manipulating Quantum Materials with Strong-field Terahertz and Mid-infrared Radiation
2610.11126.summary:
- Strong-field THz/MIR pulses probe and drive nonlinear electronic dynamics in quantum materials.
- Enables selective coupling of collective modes and symmetry‑sensitive responses.
- Facilitates field‑induced modifications of electronic structure and ordered states, as demonstrated at SECUF.

2610.11562.title: Multipolar fluctuations in localized $4f^2$-electron systems from dynamical mean-field theory: application to $\mathrm{PrCdNi}_4$
2610.11562.summary:
- Extended DFT+DMFT multipolar analysis to 4f² systems using j‑j coupling in the j=5/2 subspace to reproduce CEF splittings.
- Derived multipolar susceptibilities and inter‑multiplet interactions by mapping single‑particle to many‑particle bases.
- Applied to PrCdNi₄, predicting a (3z²–r²) antiferroquadrupolar order at q = (2π, π, driven by competing nearest‑ and fourth‑nearest‑neighbor interactions.

2610.11838.title: Magnon band splitting without altermagnetism in CuF2
2610.11838.summary:
- CuF₂’s monoclinic structure hosts weakly coupled square‑lattice layers (J₁≈115 K) with 4 % and 8 % interplane couplings that double the magnetic unit cell, eliminating altermagnetic band splitting.
- Strong Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interactions (|D|/J₁≈cant spins, pin the Néel vector to the b‑axis, and produce non‑chiral magnon band splitting.
- Combined ab initio, linear spin‑wave, and magnetization studies confirm the spin‑½ model and highlight relativistic effects in a 3d al

2610.12348.title: Constructing Large and Structured Decoherence-Free Subspaces in Hybrid Quantum Systems
2610.12348.summary:
- Build large decoherence‑free subspaces by coupling matter to a dissipative bosonic mode, selecting matter null states through global dissipation constraints.
- Employ Lie‑algebra representation theory (e.g., \(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})\)) to design many‑body operators whose null states form exponentially large DFS with volume‑law entanglement and long‑range kinetic correlations.
- Illustrate with a lossy cavity coupled to directed tunneling in 1D, revealing symmetry‑constrained Liouvillian skin

2610.12339.title: True vs false Fermi surfaces in the Pseudogap regime and their transformation with doping and temperature in the Hubbard Model
2610.12339.summary: - DiagMC and TPSC+ reveal that the pseudogap breaks Fermi‑li

2610.12294.title: Transducing quantum-spin-ice correlations into Weyl Fermi-arc transport at a synthetic Kondo lattice interface
2610.12294.summary:
- Coupled Eu₂Ir₂O₇/Tb₂Ti₂O₇ interface transduces quantum‑spin‑ice correlations into Weyl Fermi‑arc transport.
- Low‑T transport evolves from sixfold → twelvefold → re‑entrant sixfold anisotropy, a feature absent in classical‑spin‑ice interfaces.
- Interfacial coupling involves both dipolar and transverse multipolar Tb moments, enabling frustrated quantum magnetism to imprint distinct Weyl signatures.

2610.12257.title: Pressure-induced double-dome superconductivity in doped kagome metal Cs(V0.86Ta0.14)3Sb5 without charge density wave
2610.12257.summary:
- Ta‑doping suppresses CDW and boosts Tc to 29 K in Cs(V₀.₈₆Ta₀.₁₄)₃Sb₅.
- Pressure induces a non‑monotonic Tc: slight drop → peak at 61 GPa → decline to 3 GPa → rise to 46 K at 7 GPa, forming two superconducting domes.
- The double‑dome behavior occurs without CDW, showing it is intrinsic to V‑based kagome superconductors.

2610.12193.title: Orbital magnetic susceptibility and de Haas-van Alphen effect of a flat band from quantum geometry
2610.12193.summary:
- Flat band acquires field‑induced dispersion via first‑order orbital moment and second‑order quantum‑geometry term, giving a purely geometric orbital susceptibility.
- At the flat‑band chemical potential the $\mathcal{M}=0

2610.12136.title: Dynamical many-body control of high harmonic generation in a Mott insulator
2610.12136.summary:
- HHG up to 23rd order in La₂CuO₄ shows a 4 eV cutoff set by Hubbard bands, independent of field strength.
- Time‑resolved spectra separate carrier creation, intraband acceleration, and interband recombination, revealing photo‑doping‑induced many‑body band reconstruction.
- Above a critical excitation density, many‑body interactions suppress nonlinear intraband currents, making HHG a sensitive probe of correlation‑driven electronic changes.

2610.12075.title: Field-resolved hierarchy of superconducting energy gaps in PdTe
2610.12075.summary:
- PdTe exhibits two distinct superconducting gaps (~5 meV and ~1 meV) revealed by point‑contact Andreev spectra.
- Both gaps close at the same Tc, yet they collapse at different magnetic fields (~5 kG for the lower gap, ~5 kG for the higher).
- The higher‑energy gap persists to fields where zero resistance is lost, indicating a hierarchy of field‑robust superconducting responses.

2610.12044.title: Strange-metal behavior in correlated molecular conductors
2610.12044.summary:
- κ-(BEDT‑TTF)₄Hg₃₋δX₈ (X = Br, Cl) exhibits ρ(T) ∝ T and σ(ω) ∝ ω⁻⁰·⁷, classic strange‑metal signatures.
- The linear‑in‑frequency scattering rate reaches the Planckian dissipation limit, tied to incommensurate anion layers.
- Large‑scale spatial modulation of the anion layers is essential for the strange‑metal state, implying a general route for correlated strange metals.

2610.11982.title: Magnon dynamics driven by the symplectic quantum metric in a chiral soliton lattice
2610.11982.summary:
- Symplectic quantum metric dominates magnon dynamics in a 1D chiral soliton lattice.
- Wave‑packet velocity acquires a geometric term ∝ ∂k (quantum metric), overtaking group velocity for flat bands.
- Motion is a bounded trajectory whose phase‑space area is fixed by the symplectic metric.
